CafeReady Frozen Pastry Dough: Quick-Start Guide
for Café Partners
Ovenrise Industrial Bakery Co., Ltd., Lamphun · Ref. QS-CR-2026-03 · Version 3 · Issued 4 August 2026
1. About this guide
CafeReady is the frozen, unproofed pastry dough range made at the Ovenrise production plant in the
Northern Region Industrial Estate, Lamphun. Pieces are shaped, laminated with butter and blast-frozen.
Your café proofs and bakes them on site. This guide replaces Version 2 (March 2026); the main changes
are the new minimum order and a longer proofing time for the Danish swirl.
2. The CafeReady range
Butter croissant (code CR-70): 70 g raw weight, 60 pieces per case, 1,380 baht per case.
Pain au chocolat (code PC-80): 80 g raw weight with two dark chocolate batons, 48 pieces per
case, 1,296 baht per case.
Pandan custard Danish swirl (code DS-90): 90 g raw weight, 40 pieces per case, 1,240 baht per
case.
Prices exclude VAT and apply to orders delivered from 1 August 2026. Each case label shows the batch
code (for example CR-70-B2614).
3. When the delivery arrives
CafeReady leaves the plant at −22 °C in a refrigerated van. The driver will wait while you check the
delivery, so please follow these steps before you sign:
1. Open one case from the top of the stack and one from the bottom.
2. Insert a clean probe thermometer between two pieces of dough and read the temperature.
3. Accept the delivery if both readings are −15 °C or colder. If either reading is warmer than −15 °C,
refuse the affected product and write the reading on the driver's delivery note.
4. Sign the delivery note and move the cases into your freezer within 15 minutes.
Note. Refused product is replaced free of charge on the next scheduled delivery.
4. Storage
Store CafeReady in a freezer at −18 °C or colder. Unopened, the dough keeps for 120 days from the
production date. Once a case is opened, close the inner bag tightly and use the remaining pieces within
30 days. Use the oldest batch first. Thawed dough must never be refrozen: if pieces have been thawed
and not baked within 24 hours, throw them away.
5. Thawing and proofing
Most complaints about flat or greasy croissants come from proofing that was too warm.

1. The evening before, place the frozen pieces on a lined tray, leaving 5 cm between pieces.
2. Cover the tray loosely and thaw overnight in a chiller at 2–5 °C for 8 to 10 hours.
3. Move the tray to a proofer set at 26–28 °C and 75 % humidity.
4. Proof the croissant and pain au chocolat for 90 to 120 minutes. Proof the Danish swirl for 120 to 150
minutes (in Version 2 this was 100 to 130 minutes).
5. The dough is ready when the pieces have roughly doubled in size and wobble slightly when the tray
is moved.
6. Brush gently with egg wash just before baking.
Note. Never proof above 30 °C. At that temperature the butter layers melt into the dough, and the
pastry bakes flat and greasy.
6. Baking
Preheat the oven fully. Times are for a full tray. Bake until the pastry is deep golden brown on top and
underneath.
Convection oven: croissant and pain au chocolat at 165 °C for 16 to 18 minutes; Danish swirl at 160
°C for 20 minutes.
Deck oven: croissant and pain au chocolat at 180 °C for 18 to 20 minutes; Danish swirl at 175 °C for
22 minutes.
Let the pastries cool on the tray for at least 10 minutes before display.
7. Ordering and delivery
Place orders on the OvenLink partner portal or through your account manager. The order cut-off is 14:00,
two working days before your delivery day. Later orders move to the next delivery day on your route.
Minimum order: 6 cases per delivery, which may be mixed across products. Until 31 July 2026 the
minimum was 4 cases.
Delivery days: Chiang Mai city routes on Tuesday and Friday; Lampang and Lamphun on
Wednesday; Chiang Rai on Thursday.
Delivery fee: 350 baht for orders of 6 to 9 cases. Delivery is free for orders of 10 cases or more.
8. Quality claims
Report quality problems such as misshapen pieces or missing chocolate batons within 48 hours of
delivery. Submit the claim in OvenLink under "Quality claim" with the batch code, the number of affected
pieces and at least two photos. Keep the affected pieces in the freezer until we tell you they can be
thrown away, because we may collect them for testing. Approved claims are credited on your next
invoice. For any question, contact Pimchanok Lertsiri, Partner Support Manager, at
partners@ovenrise.example or 053 552 418 (Monday to Saturday, 07:00–16:00).

Public Access, Fishing and Boating Rules for the
Huai Sop Khong Small Hydropower Dam
Sop Khong Hydro Co., Ltd., Mae Chaem, Chiang Mai · Policy SKH-POL-07, version 3 · Effective 1 July 2026
1. Purpose and scope
The Huai Sop Khong Small Hydropower Dam sits on the Huai Sop Khong stream about 9 km north-west
of Mae Chaem town. Water levels near the dam can change quickly and without visible warning. These
rules apply to every visitor, permit holder and member of the public who enters land or water managed
by Sop Khong Hydro Co., Ltd. (the "Company"). They replace version 2 of this policy dated 1 March
2024.
2. Access zones
The site is divided into four zones, marked with coloured signs.
Zone A, Restricted (red signs): the dam crest, intake, spillway gates, powerhouse yard and the
stream bed down to 150 m below the powerhouse outlet. No public access except on a guided tour
(section 7).
Zone B, Headpond Recreation Zone (green signs): the reservoir upstream of the yellow buoy line,
200 m from the dam crest.
Zone C, Downstream Reach (blue signs): the stream from 150 m below the powerhouse outlet to
the Ban Sop Khong suspension bridge, a distance of about 2.4 km.
Visitor Area (white signs): the car park, the Visitor Centre and the public viewing platform.
3. Opening hours
The Visitor Area is open daily from 07:00 to 18:00, including public holidays. Until 30 June 2026 it opened
from 08:00 to 17:00; the longer hours apply from 1 July 2026. The viewing platform is closed while any
spillway gate is moving.
Boating in Zone B is allowed from 08:00 to 17:00 during the dry season, 1 November to 31 May. Boating
is not allowed at all from 1 June to 31 October. Fishing from the bank in Zones B and C is allowed from
sunrise to sunset all year, subject to the closed season in section 5.
4. Warning signals and water releases
Turbine start-ups, spillway gate openings and sediment flushing can raise the water level in Zone C from
about 0.6 m to 1.8 m within 20 minutes. Everyone in Zones B and C must obey the following siren
signals.
Two long blasts: a turbine will start in 15 minutes. Move out of the stream bed in Zone C and stay on
the bank.
Three long blasts of 10 seconds each, repeated after 5 minutes: a spillway gate opening or
sediment flushing will begin in 30 minutes. Leave the water and the stream banks in Zone C and

move at least 5 m above the water line.
One continuous tone lasting one minute: emergency. Leave Zones B and C immediately and go to
higher ground.
Amber lights flash at the four warning stations for as long as a release is in progress. While an amber
light is flashing, nobody may enter the water in Zone C for any reason.
Scheduled sediment flushing takes place on the first Wednesday of each month from November to May,
between 09:00 and 13:00. Anyone may receive free text alerts before every planned release by
registering at the Visitor Centre or by sending the word JOIN to 08 1745 2290.
Note. Unplanned releases can happen at any time during heavy rain. The sirens and amber lights,
not text alerts, are the official warning.
5. Fishing
5.1 Permits
Every angler aged 12 or over needs a valid Company fishing permit, which covers both Zone B and Zone
C. An annual permit costs 300 baht per calendar year for residents of Mae Chaem district and 900 baht
for all other anglers. A day permit costs 80 baht and is valid until sunset on the day of issue. Children
under 12 may fish without a permit next to an adult permit holder.
5.2 How to obtain an annual permit
1. Come in person to the Permit Desk in Room 2 of the Visitor Centre, open Monday to Saturday from
08:30 to 16:00. Online applications are not accepted.
2. Bring your Thai national ID card or passport. Residents claiming the resident rate must also bring
their house registration document.
3. Complete application form SK-F1, attach one passport-size photograph and sign the safety
declaration on its back.
4. Pay the fee in cash or by QR payment. The permit card is issued on the same day and must be
carried whenever you fish.
Day permits are also sold at the car park kiosk on Sundays from 07:00 to 12:00.
5.3 Fishing rules
Rod and line only, with a maximum of two rods per angler. Nets, traps, spears, explosives and
electric fishing are forbidden in all zones.
Daily catch limit: five fish per permit holder. Fish shorter than 25 cm must be returned to the water
alive.
Closed season in Zone C: from 16 May to 15 August no fishing of any kind is allowed in Zone C, to
protect spawning fish. Fishing in Zone B continues during this period.

6. Boating and swimming
Only non-motorised craft, such as kayaks, canoes and stand-up paddle boards, may be used in Zone B.
Every person on the water must wear a buoyant life jacket, and every craft must be signed in and out in
the boat log at the launching ramp. No more than 10 craft may be on the water at the same time.
Swimming is not allowed in Zones A and B. In Zone C, swimming is allowed only at Kaeng Hin Lai beach,
between 10:00 and 16:00, and only when the amber light at the beach is not flashing. Children under 14
must be accompanied in the water by an adult.
7. Group visits and powerhouse tours
Guided tours of the powerhouse and dam crest run from Tuesday to Saturday at 10:00 and 14:00. No
tours are held on public holidays. A tour group may have up to 20 people. Groups must book at least 7
working days in advance through the Community Relations Office (telephone 053 828 410).
Visitors must be at least 10 years old to enter the turbine hall and must wear closed-toe shoes.
Groups with visitors under 15 need one adult supervisor for every 10 young visitors.
Tours are free for schools located in Chiang Mai province. All other visitors pay 50 baht per person.
Tours are cancelled without charge when the reservoir level is above 412.5 m above mean sea level
(flood watch).
8. Drones and camping
Drones may not be flown within 500 m of the dam crest unless the Plant Manager has given written
permission at least 5 working days before the flight. Camping and open fires are not allowed on
Company land.
9. Breaches and penalties
First breach: a written warning and removal from the site for the day.
Second breach within 12 months: the fishing permit is suspended for 6 months without refund.
Serious breach (entering Zone A without a guide, crossing the yellow buoy line, or ignoring the
emergency tone): the permit is cancelled, the person is banned from all Company land and water for
2 years, and the case is reported to Mae Chaem police station.
Appeals may be made in writing to the Plant Manager within 30 days of the decision.
10. Responsibilities and contacts
Ms. Pornthip Wongkhamsing, Community Safety Officer, handles fishing permits, the text alert service,
the boat log and complaints from the public. Mr. Wichai Lertpanya, Plant Manager, decides on drone
permissions, appeals and any exception to these rules. For emergencies and people in the water, call the
Control Room, staffed 24 hours, on 053 828 499. This policy will be reviewed by 30 June 2027.

Incident Report: Storm Power Failure in the Nursery
and Reptile Incubation Wing
Huai Mae Kham Wildlife Rescue Centre, Chiang Rai · Ref. IR-2026-07 · Version 1.1 · Issued 2 September 2026
1. Summary
On the night of 14–15 August 2026 a thunderstorm cut mains power to the whole Huai Mae Kham
Wildlife Rescue Centre for 5 hours and 40 minutes, from 23:10 on 14 August to 04:50 on 15 August. The
standby diesel generator (asset GEN-02, 60 kVA) started correctly, but the automatic transfer switch did
not connect it to the East Wing, which houses the Mammal Nursery (Rooms E1 and E2) and the Reptile
Incubation Room (Room E4). The East Wing therefore stayed without power for 2 hours and 25 minutes,
until staff switched it over by hand at 01:35.
During that time the temperature in the Reptile Incubation Room fell from 29.5 °C to 24.1 °C, and the
Mammal Nursery fell from 30 °C to 25.8 °C. No animal died during the outage. Of the 41 forest tortoise
eggs in incubation, 6 later failed to hatch; the reptile team believes the cold period contributed to at least
4 of these losses. Two infant slow lorises and one infant binturong were moved to a heated transport
cabinet and recovered fully.
This report was prepared by the Incident Review Group, which met on 21 and 28 August 2026. Version
1.0 was circulated internally on 29 August; version 1.1 corrects the duration of the East Wing outage,
which was first reported as 2 hours and 10 minutes.
2. Timeline of the night
22:40 – The regional weather service issues a severe thunderstorm warning for Mueang Chiang Rai
and Mae Lao districts.
23:10 – Mains power fails across the site. GEN-02 starts within 12 seconds and powers the West
Wing, the clinic and the kitchen.
23:25 – Night keeper Thanakrit Moonsri notices that the East Wing corridor lights are still off and that
the incubator alarm panel in Room E4 is running on its internal battery.
23:40 – The night keeper phones the on-call facilities technician, who does not answer. The on-call
list on the notice board still showed the June rota.
00:05 – The night keeper reaches the duty veterinarian, Dr. Orawan Boonyasit, who arrives on site at
00:30.
00:45 – On Dr. Orawan's instruction, the two slow loris infants and the binturong infant are moved
from Room E1 into the heated transport cabinet in the clinic.
01:20 – Facilities Supervisor Chaiyaporn Phanphet arrives after being called by Dr. Orawan.
01:35 – Mr. Chaiyaporn switches the East Wing to generator power using the manual bypass handle
on the transfer switch. Heating returns in Rooms E1, E2 and E4.
03:00 – Room E4 is back to 29.0 °C. The incubators are checked one by one.
04:50 – Mains power returns. The transfer switch is left in manual mode until inspection.

3. Effect on animals
At the time of the outage the East Wing held 9 animals in the Mammal Nursery and 41 forest tortoise
eggs in three incubators in Room E4. The eggs came from two confiscated clutches received on 22 July
2026 and were due to hatch between 2 and 20 September.
Mammal Nursery: all 9 animals survived. The two slow lorises and the binturong, which are under 6
weeks old and cannot regulate their body temperature, were moved first. The six older animals
stayed in their rooms with extra bedding.
Reptile Incubation Room: by 14 September, 35 eggs had hatched and 6 had failed. Hatchlings are
being monitored for shell deformities until 30 November 2026.
West Wing and outdoor enclosures: not affected. One fallen branch damaged the fence of the
macaque pre-release enclosure, which was repaired on 16 August.
Note. The incubators in Room E4 have their own alarm batteries but no heating backup. The alarm
panel showed a low-temperature warning from 23:58, but the alarm only sounds locally in Room E4
and is not linked to the night keeper's radio.
4. Cause of the failure
An inspection by the generator service contractor on 18 August found that the control relay in the East
Wing section of the automatic transfer switch was corroded and had stuck in the open position. The relay
was last checked during the annual service on 9 November 2025. Under the centre's maintenance plan,
the transfer switch should also have been load-tested every three months; the last recorded load test
was on 3 February 2026, so the May 2026 test was missed.
The review also found three contributing factors:
The on-call facilities rota on the notice board had not been updated since June, so the night keeper
called a technician who had left the centre on 31 July.
Night keepers had not been trained to use the manual bypass handle. The handle is behind a locked
panel in the plant room and only facilities staff hold the key.
The written power-failure procedure, dated 2023, did not mention the East Wing as a separate circuit.
5. Revised power-failure procedure
The procedure below replaces the 2023 version with immediate effect. A laminated copy is posted in the
night keeper's office and in Rooms E1, E2 and E4. All night keepers and duty veterinarians must confirm
in writing that they have read it.
1. Within 10 minutes of any power cut, the night keeper checks the indicator lamps on the transfer
switch display in the plant room and walks to the East Wing to confirm that lights and heaters are on.
2. If the East Wing has no power, the night keeper calls the on-call facilities technician from the current
rota in the shared roster app, not from the notice board.
3. If the technician does not answer within 15 minutes, the night keeper calls the Facilities Supervisor
directly and then the duty veterinarian.

4. If the temperature in Room E4 or the Mammal Nursery falls below 27 °C, the night keeper moves
infants under 6 weeks old to the heated transport cabinet in the clinic, without waiting for the duty
veterinarian.
5. Only facilities staff, or a night keeper who has passed the bypass training, may operate the manual
bypass handle. The key is now kept in the sealed key box in the night keeper's office.
6. The night keeper records each step and its time in the incident log and informs the Centre Director by
message before 07:00.
Note. Incubators must not be opened during a power cut, even to check eggs, unless the duty
veterinarian or the Reptile Unit Lead gives permission. Opening a cold incubator lowers the
temperature further.
6. Responsibilities
The review group confirmed who is responsible for each part of power resilience at the centre:
Facilities Supervisor (Chaiyaporn Phanphet): quarterly load tests of GEN-02 and the transfer
switch, the annual generator service contract, the on-call facilities rota in the roster app, and bypass
training for night keepers.
Senior Veterinarian (Dr. Orawan Boonyasit): decisions on moving or treating animals during an
emergency, and the animal welfare section of every incident report.
Reptile Unit Lead (Sirilak Pansuwan): incubator settings, egg checks and hatchling monitoring.
Centre Director (Jiraporn Kaewlamai): approval of this report, notification of the foundation board
within 72 hours of any incident that affects animal welfare, and the budget for corrective actions.
7. Corrective actions
Replace the corroded relay and fit a new relay rated for humid conditions. Owner: Facilities
Supervisor. Completed on 19 August 2026 at a cost of 8,400 baht.
Install a battery-backed heater (minimum 4 hours) in each incubator in Room E4. Owner: Reptile Unit
Lead. Due 15 October 2026; budget approved at 36,000 baht for three units.
Link the Room E4 and Mammal Nursery temperature alarms to the night keeper's radio. Owner:
Facilities Supervisor. Due 30 September 2026.
Train all five night keepers on the manual bypass handle, with a practical test. Owner: Facilities
Supervisor. Two sessions are scheduled for 10 and 17 September 2026.
Run an unannounced power-failure drill on a night shift. Owner: Centre Director. To be held before 31
December 2026.
The Centre Director informed the foundation board of the incident on 16 August 2026. Progress on the
actions above will be reviewed at the monthly safety meeting on 7 October 2026, and this report will then
be closed or updated as version 1.2.
Prepared by the Incident Review Group: Dr. Orawan Boonyasit, Chaiyaporn Phanphet, Sirilak Pansuwan and Thanakrit
Moonsri. Approved by Jiraporn Kaewlamai, Centre Director, on 2 September 2026.

Deferring Your Offer: Frequently Asked Questions
Huai Sai Thong University (HSTU), Roi Et · Office of Undergraduate Admissions · Ref. ADM-FAQ-2026-07 ·
Version 2.1 · Updated 14 September 2026
This FAQ is for applicants who hold a confirmed undergraduate offer for the 2027 intake at Huai Sai
Thong University and wish to postpone their start by one academic year. It replaces Version 1.4 of March
2025. If an answer here differs from an email you received before 14 September 2026, this FAQ applies.
1. Eligibility
Who can ask to defer an offer?
Any applicant who has accepted an unconditional offer, or a conditional offer whose conditions have
already been met, may apply. You must also have paid the 3,000-baht seat confirmation fee. Applicants
admitted through the Portfolio Round and the Direct Admission Round are eligible. Applicants admitted
through the Faculty Scholarship Quota are not eligible, because quota places are tied to a specific intake
year.
Can every programme be deferred?
Most programmes allow deferral. The exceptions are the Bachelor of Nursing Science and the Doctor of
Veterinary Medicine, where clinical placement places are planned for each cohort. Applicants to these
two programmes who need to postpone must withdraw and apply again in the following admission cycle.
How long can I defer?
One academic year only. A 2027 offer can be moved to the intake starting in August 2028, never later.
Until the 2025 intake, two-year deferrals were allowed for national service; this exception has been
removed for all offers issued from 1 October 2025.
2. Applying for deferral
When is the deadline?
Deferral requests for the 2027 intake must be submitted by 16:00 on Friday 30 April 2027. Requests
received after this time are only considered for documented medical or family emergencies, and no later
than 31 May 2027.
How do I submit a request?
1. Log in to the HSTU Applicant Portal with the applicant number shown on your offer letter.
2. Open the "My Offer" tab and choose "Request deferral".
3. Write a personal statement of no more than 500 words describing what you plan to do during the
deferral year.
4. Upload supporting documents as PDF files of at most 5 MB each, for example a job offer, a volunteer
placement letter or a medical certificate.
5. Pay the non-refundable deferral processing fee of 1,500 baht by QR payment within 3 working days.
The request is not reviewed until the fee is received.

You will receive an automatic acknowledgement email with a request number beginning with "DEF-".
Keep it for all later contact.
3. Review and decision
Who decides on my request?
Requests are first checked for completeness by the Deferral and Re-entry Officer, Ms Pimchanok
Lertwattana, who may ask you for missing documents. The decision itself is made by the Assistant Dean
for Admissions, Asst. Prof. Dr. Somkiat Inthaphan, after consulting the programme chair. The programme
chair gives advice but does not approve or reject requests.
How long does the review take?
A decision is normally sent within 15 working days of the date your fee is received.
What happens to my seat confirmation fee?
If the deferral is approved, your 3,000-baht seat confirmation fee is carried forward to the 2028 intake
and you do not pay it again. If the request is refused, your original 2027 offer remains valid and you may
still start in August 2027.
4. During the deferral year
Do I need to confirm that I am still coming?
Yes. Every deferred student must reconfirm their place in the Applicant Portal between 1 and 31 March
2028. Students who do not reconfirm in this window lose the deferred place and the carried-forward fee.
A reminder is sent by email and SMS on 1 March and on 20 March 2028.
May I study at another university while my place is deferred?
You may take short courses, language classes or online modules of up to 12 credits in total. If you enrol
in a full degree programme at another institution, the deferred HSTU place is cancelled.
Note on scholarships. Merit scholarships awarded with a 2027 offer are held for deferred students
only if the scholarship letter says "deferrable". All other scholarships are cancelled on deferral.
5. Fees and contact
Will my tuition fee change?
Deferred students pay the tuition rate published for the 2028 intake, not the 2027 rate. For most
programmes the 2027 rate is 21,500 baht per semester.
How can I contact the Admissions Office?
Email deferral@admissions.hstu.example, call 043 518 220 (Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 16:30), or visit
Room 112, Ground Floor, Rattana Building, main campus, Roi Et.

Minutes of Joint Handover Committee Meeting No.
3/2026
Banyan Ridge Village Phase 2, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai · Thanachot Land Co., Ltd. · Ref. JHC-BR2-03/2026 ·
18 September 2026
Venue: Clubhouse Meeting Room B, 19:00–20:45. Developer: Sirinthip Prasertkul (Handover Manager,
chair), Anan Kaewmala (Site Engineer), Wanida Rungsri (Customer Care, minutes). Residents: Montree
Pimsri (Chair, Interim Residents Committee), Jiraporn Thepsuwan (Treasurer).
1. Common-area defect survey
Phase 2 has 146 houses, 131 transferred to buyers. Anan Kaewmala reported that 22 of the 37 items
from the 9 September walk-through are fixed. Open: the north retention pond pump trips during heavy
rain, 6 street lights on Soi 3 do not work, and pool tiles are loose at the shallow end. The pool stays
closed until about 10 October 2026. The pond pump will be replaced, not repaired.
2. Handover date of the common areas
The handover to the village juristic person was planned for 1 November 2026. Because the open defects
must be closed first, the committee agreed to move the handover to 1 December 2026. The owners’
meeting to register the juristic person stays on Sunday 22 November 2026, 10:00, clubhouse hall.
3. Common maintenance fee
Until 30 September 2026 the developer charges 25 baht per square wah per month. From the handover
date the fee set by the owners’ meeting applies; the proposal to be voted on is 32 baht per square wah
per month. Jiraporn Thepsuwan will send the draft 2027 budget to owners by 6 November 2026.
4. Private house defects and warranty
Agreed procedure for reporting defects inside a house:
1. Fill in the defect form in the Banyan Ridge resident app, or on paper at the sales office, with the
house number and photos.
2. Customer Care sends a reference number within 2 working days.
3. The site engineer inspects within 7 working days and books the repair with the owner.
4. The owner signs the completion sheet.
Warranty from the transfer date: 5 years for structure, 1 year for fittings (doors, taps, wiring).
5. Action points
Replace the north pond pump by 15 October 2026: Anan Kaewmala. Repair the Soi 3 street lights and
send a photo report: Sirinthip Prasertkul. Send the owners’ meeting invitation by 6 November 2026:
Montree Pimsri. Next meeting: 16 October 2026, 19:00.

Fire Safety Rules for Charging and Storing E-Bike
and E-Scooter Batteries
Lamyai Court Condominium Juristic Person, Hat Yai, Songkhla · Policy LC-FS-04, version 2 · Effective 1
November 2026
1. Purpose and scope
These rules apply to all owners, tenants and staff at Lamyai Court (Towers A and B). They replace version
1 of 15 January 2025, which allowed charging on balconies.
2. Shared Charging Room
Except as allowed in section 4, e-bike and e-scooter charging must take place in the Shared Charging
Room, Room B1-07 on basement level 1 next to the Tower B lift lobby. It is open from 06:00 to 23:00
daily and has 16 bays, a heat detector linked to the fire alarm panel and a sprinkler. Security staff unplug
any charger still connected after 23:00.
3. How to register a vehicle
1. Fill in form LC-FS-04A at the Juristic Office (Tower A, ground floor).
2. Bring the vehicle and original charger for a battery inspection by the duty technician.
3. Pay the fee of 300 baht per vehicle and receive a bay sticker and access card, valid 12 months.
4. Rules inside units and common areas
No parking or charging in corridors, stairwells, lift lobbies or on balconies.
A removable battery of 500 Wh or less may be charged inside a unit between 07:00 and 22:00, only
while an adult is present. Batteries above 500 Wh may only be charged in Room B1-07.
Modified or repaired batteries are not allowed. Vehicles use the service lift only.
Note. Mobility scooters used by residents with a disability are exempt from the in-unit limits, but
must still be registered under section 3.
5. Emergencies and breaches
If a battery smokes or swells, leave, close the door, press a fire alarm call point and call security on
extension 199. A second breach within 12 months brings a 2,000 baht fine. Contact: Kittiya Somboon,
Fire Safety Officer. Approved by Thanya Prasert, Building Manager.

Memo: Temporary Relocation of Station SK-05 (Ban
Phru)
Songkhla Lake Basin Air Monitoring Network (SLBAMN) · Ref. SLB-MEMO-2026-19 · 14 September 2026
To: Field technicians, data desk staff and site hosts, Hat Yai cluster · From: Dr. Chanida Yodsaeng,
Network Manager
Subject: Move of Station SK-05 to a temporary site and handling of its data
1. Decision
Ban Phru Municipal School will re-roof Building 2 from 5 October to about 20 December 2026. Station
SK-05 (on that roof since 2021, inlet at 11 m) will move to the car park of Ban Phru Sub-district Health
Promoting Hospital, 1.2 km south-east, with the inlet on a 4.5 m mast. The last valid hour at the school is
2 October 2026, 23:00; removal is on 3 October and installation on 4 October. After a 48-hour check,
data from the temporary site, code SK-05T, are published from 7 October 2026, 00:00. Return to the roof
is planned for early January 2027, subject to the school’s written confirmation.
2. How SK-05T data are handled
From 3 to 6 October the public map shows SK-05 as “Station offline”. SK-05T data are not merged
into the long-term SK-05 series.
While SK-05 is away, the Hat Yai district haze alert uses SK-02 (Kho Hong), trigger 50 μg/m3 PM2.5
(24-hour mean). The old 37.5 μg/m3 trigger was retired on 1 June 2026.
An annual mean needs 75 % data completeness; SK-05 will reach about 68 % in 2026, so its 2026
mean is reported as “indicative”.
3. Procedure for the move crew
1. Before power-off, download the logger memory and upload it to the SK-05 folder on the data desk
drive.
2. Run a leak check and a flow check and write both results in the station log book.
3. At the new site, place the mast at least 20 m from the hospital’s standby generator exhaust.
4. Check the flow is within ±4 % of 16.7 L/min. If not, do not start sampling and call the Field
Operations Lead.
5. Send photos of the set-up from four sides to the data desk the same day.
4. Responsibilities

September 2026

For the 2026 season the fee was 450 baht per hive for the whole flowering period. After discussion with
Prasit Rungruangchai, the committee agreed the following fees for the 2027 season:
Standard colony (at least 8 full frames of bees, laying queen): 520 baht per hive per season.

TapCast Dawn Alert: Frequently Asked Questions
Khlong Mek Weather Services Co., Ltd., Surat Thani · Subscriber Care · Ref. KMW-FAQ-TC-2026-03 · Version
3.0 · Updated 18 September 2026
This FAQ is for rubber smallholders, tapping teams and cooperatives using TapCast Dawn Alert. It
replaces Version 2.2 of February 2026.
1. About the service
What is TapCast Dawn Alert?
TapCast Dawn Alert is a pre-dawn weather message that tells you whether it is worth tapping your rubber
plot that morning. Rain on freshly cut panels washes latex out of the cup and can spread panel disease,
so our forecasters look at the five hours that matter most to tappers, from 03:00 to 08:00, for the 5 km
grid cell that contains your plot. The service covers plots in Surat Thani, Nakhon Si Thammarat,
Chumphon and Phang Nga.
When will I receive the message?
The main alert is sent at 02:30 every morning, all year round, including public holidays. Until 30 June
2026 the main alert was sent at 03:15; it was moved earlier because many teams start cutting before
03:00. Plots that receive an AMBER code also get a second message, the 04:30 update, which confirms
or changes the code.
What do the colour codes mean?
GREEN – TAP: the chance of 2 mm or more of rain on your grid cell between 03:00 and 08:00 is
below 30 %.
AMBER – WAIT: the chance is between 30 % and 60 %. Prepare as usual but wait for the 04:30
update before cutting.
RED – DO NOT TAP: the chance is above 60 %, or lightning is expected within 10 km of your plot
during the window.
STORM MODE: sent instead of a colour code on days when a tropical storm or heavy-rain warning
covers your province. No tapping advice is given on these days.
2. Plans and prices
Which plans are available?
Basic: 59 baht per month. SMS alert for one plot, main alert and 04:30 update.
Plus: 99 baht per month. Up to three plots, alerts by SMS and LINE, and a three-day tapping outlook
every Sunday evening.
Cooperative: 35 baht per member per month, with a minimum of 20 members. Each member gets
the Plus features for one plot, and the cooperative receives a single monthly invoice.
Paying for a full year in advance gives you twelve months for the price of ten on the Basic and Plus
plans. The annual discount does not apply to the Cooperative plan, which is billed monthly only.

Is there a free trial?
Yes. New subscribers on the Basic or Plus plan get 14 days free. The trial was 30 days for anyone who
joined before 31 May 2026. Only one free trial is given per mobile number.
3. Registering and changing a plot
How do I register my plot?
1. Add the LINE official account @tapcastkm, or call the Subscriber Care line on 077 410 286.
2. Send the location pin of your plot, taken while standing inside the plot, not at your house.
3. Tell us the time your team usually starts cutting, between 01:00 and 04:00. This lets us warn you if
rain is expected before 03:00.
4. Choose your plan and pay, or start your free trial.
5. Reply "OK" to the confirmation SMS. Alerts begin from the next morning if your reply is received
before 20:00.
Can I move my plot to a different location?
Yes. Send the new location pin through LINE or the Subscriber Care line. Changes received before 20:00
take effect the next morning. Basic subscribers may change the plot location twice per calendar month
at no charge; each further change costs 20 baht. Plus and Cooperative subscribers can change locations
without a fee.
4. Forecast quality and responsibility
Who prepares the forecasts?
Forecasts are produced at our forecast centre on Talat Mai Road, Surat Thani, by a duty team of two
forecasters on every night shift. The duty team combines regional model output with radar data and
readings from 146 partner rain gauges, most of them installed at cooperative collection points. The Chief
Duty Forecaster, Ms Supattra Nimmanee, reviews and signs off every 04:30 update before it is sent.
Changes to the colour-code thresholds or to the forecast models can only be approved by the Head of
Forecast Operations, Mr Kittisak Sornprasit.
How accurate is TapCast?
During the 2025–2026 tapping season, 88 % of GREEN days stayed dry enough to tap, measured as less
than 2 mm of rain at the nearest partner gauge between 03:00 and 08:00. For RED days, rain of 2 mm or
more actually fell on 81 % of occasions. Accuracy is usually lower in November and December, during
the northeast monsoon.
5. The Rain Guarantee
What happens if I get GREEN and it rains?
If your plot received a GREEN code and the nearest partner gauge recorded 5 mm or more of rain
between 03:00 and 08:00 that morning, you can claim a Rain Guarantee credit of 10 baht against your

next bill. You can receive at most 3 credits per calendar month. Credits are not paid in cash and expire if
you cancel the service.
Note. No Rain Guarantee credit is given on STORM MODE days, for plots registered with a location
pin taken outside the plot, or for the first 3 days after a plot location change.
How do I claim a credit?
1. Within 7 days of the morning concerned, open the LINE official account and type "RAIN".
2. Select the date and the plot from the menu.
3. Wait for the result, which is sent within 5 working days after the gauge record has been checked.
Who decides on my claim, and can I appeal?
Claims are checked by the Subscriber Care team against the gauge records. If you disagree with the
result, reply "APPEAL" within 14 days of the decision. Appeals are decided by the Subscriber Care
Manager, Ms Ratchanee Phothisan, and her decision is final. The forecast team does not handle claims
or appeals.
6. Pausing and cancelling
Can I pause the service during the leaf-fall season?
Yes. Most plots stop tapping during wintering, when the trees shed their leaves, usually between
February and April. You can pause your subscription once per calendar year for up to 90 days without
charge. To pause, send "PAUSE" and your planned restart date through LINE or call Subscriber Care by
the 25th of the month before the pause starts. Alerts restart automatically on the date you gave.
Cooperative members must ask their cooperative office, which arranges pauses for the whole group.
How do I cancel?
Send "STOP" by SMS to 4 2 8 6 1 or through LINE. Monthly plans end at the end of the current billing
month. Annual payments are refunded for the full unused months, minus a 50 baht handling fee, if you
cancel within the first six months; after six months annual payments are not refunded.
7. Messages, outages and your data
What if the SMS does not arrive?
If the main alert has not arrived by 02:50, call the recorded TapCast line on 077 410 299, enter your
mobile number and you will hear the code for your plot.
Who can see my plot location?
Your location pin is used only to choose your grid cell and nearest gauge. On the Cooperative plan, the
cooperative manager can see the grid cell of each member, but not the exact pin.
For any other question, the Subscriber Care line, 077 410 286, is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to
Saturday.

Customer Guide: Releasing Empty Hopper Wagons
from Private Sidings
Thanarak Rail Logistics Co., Ltd. (TRL), Kaeng Khoi, Saraburi · Ref. TRL-OPS-G07, version 3.1 · Issued 15
September 2026 · Effective 1 October 2026
1. Purpose and scope
This guide explains, step by step, how customers with a private siding return empty TRL covered hopper
wagons after unloading. It applies to the four private-siding areas served by TRL's daily trip trains: Kaeng
Khoi (sidings K1 to K6), Ban Phachi (sidings P1 to P3), Tha Lan (siding T1) and Sikhio (sidings S1 and
S2). It covers two wagon classes:
THC-40: 40-tonne covered hopper used for bulk cement, grain and fertiliser.
THC-55: 55-tonne pressure-discharge hopper used for plastic pellets and fine powders.
Version 3.1 replaces version 3.0 of 2 February 2026. The main changes are a shorter free time for THC-55
wagons, a new 14:00 cut-off for release notices and the move of all release notices to the SidingLink
portal. Paper release forms (form TRL-F12) are no longer accepted from 1 October 2026, except during a
portal outage (see section 4.3).
2. Key terms
Placement time: the time TRL's shunting crew records a wagon as placed on your siding. It is
shown on the placement slip and in SidingLink.
Free time: the period after placement during which you may unload and release a wagon without
charge. For THC-40 wagons the free time is 48 hours. For THC-55 wagons it is 36 hours from 1
October 2026; until 30 September 2026 it was 72 hours.
Release time: the time a valid release notice is submitted in SidingLink. This stops the detention
clock, provided the wagon then passes inspection.
Detention charge: the charge for each started 24-hour period that a wagon stays on your siding
after its free time has ended. The rate is 1,200 baht per wagon per period for THC-40 and 1,500 baht
per wagon per period for THC-55, excluding VAT.
Release tag: the green numbered tag (TRL-T4) fixed to the discharge outlet lever of an empty wagon
to show that it is closed and ready to move. Red tags (TRL-T5) mark wagons that must not be
moved.
Note. Free time runs continuously, including weekends and public holidays. It is not paused while
your own unloading equipment is out of service.
3. Preparing the wagon for release
Your siding supervisor (the person named as "siding supervisor" in your siding agreement) must make
sure each wagon is prepared as follows before a release notice is sent.

1. Discharge the load completely. Tap the hopper sides with a rubber mallet to free material stuck to the
slopes. No more than 50 kg of residue may remain in a THC-40 wagon and no more than 20 kg in a
THC-55 wagon.
2. Close all bottom discharge gates and lock each gate lever with its pin. On THC-55 wagons, also
close the air inlet valve and vent the hopper until the pressure gauge reads zero.
3. Close and latch all top loading hatches, remove any customer covers, and clear tools and chocks
from the track.
4. Release the wagon's hand brake, unless your siding agreement requires it to stay applied on a
gradient.
5. Fix a green release tag to the outlet lever and write the wagon number and the time on it.
If a wagon cannot be prepared, for example because a gate is jammed or a hatch is bent, do not try to
force it. Fix a red tag and report it as described in section 6.
4. Submitting the release notice in SidingLink
4.1 Steps in the portal
1. Log in to SidingLink with your company account. Each customer has up to five user accounts.
2. Open "Wagons on siding", which shows each wagon's placement time and the end of its free time.
3. Select the wagons to release. You may release up to 12 wagons in one notice. For more wagons,
send a second notice.
4. For each wagon, enter the release tag number and confirm the three checks on screen (gates locked,
hatches closed, residue within the limit).
5. Submit. SidingLink issues a release number beginning with "RN-" and sends a confirmation e-mail to
the siding supervisor. Keep the release number for any later query.
4.2 Cut-off and collection
Release notices submitted by 14:00 are collected by the next morning's trip train, which normally
reaches the sidings between 06:00 and 10:00. Notices submitted after 14:00 are collected by the trip
train of the following day. Trip trains run every day at Kaeng Khoi, Ban Phachi and Tha Lan. At Sikhio
there is no trip train on Sundays and public holidays, so wagons released there after 14:00 on a Saturday
are collected on Monday (or on the next working day after a holiday).
The detention clock stops at the release time, not at the time of collection. A late collection by TRL
therefore does not increase your charges.
4.3 Portal outage
If SidingLink is unavailable for more than 30 minutes, telephone TRL Control and e-mail a paper form
TRL-F12 to control@thanarak-rail.co.th. The release time is the time the e-mail is received.
5. Inspection on collection
Before coupling, the TRL train crew inspects each released wagon. The inspection procedure and the
training of train crews are the responsibility of Ratchanee Boonmak, Wagon Inspection Supervisor. Each
wagon receives one of three results, which are entered in SidingLink within 4 hours of the inspection:

Accepted: the wagon is collected and the detention clock is closed at the release time.
Accepted with remark: the wagon is collected, but a minor fault (for example a missing gate pin or a
residue level close to the limit) is recorded. No charge is made for a first remark. A second remark on
the same siding within 30 days is charged as a rejection.
Rejected: the wagon is left on the siding and a red tag is fixed. The release notice is cancelled and
the detention clock keeps running as if no release had been made, until a new valid release. You
must correct the fault and submit a new release notice. A cleaning fee of 3,500 baht per wagon is
also charged if the wagon was rejected for excess residue and TRL's contractor cleans it at the
depot instead.
If you disagree with a rejection, you may lodge a dispute in SidingLink under "Inspection results" within 3
working days of the inspection. Attach photographs of the wagon taken before collection. Disputes are
decided by Kittipong Rakthai, Siding Operations Manager, who replies within 5 working days. If the
dispute is upheld, the rejection, any cleaning fee and any extra detention charges are cancelled.
6. Damaged wagons and incidents
If a wagon is damaged on your siding, or you find damage that was already present at placement, the
siding supervisor must report it to TRL Control at Kaeng Khoi (036 318 400, 24 hours) by telephone
within 2 hours of discovery, and record it in SidingLink under "Report a defect". Fix a red tag and do not
move the wagon with your own shunting equipment. TRL's wagon technician will assess the wagon,
normally within 24 hours.
The detention clock is suspended from the time of the report until the technician's assessment. If the
damage was caused by the customer, repair costs are charged at the rates in Annex B of your siding
agreement and the detention clock resumes from the assessment. If the damage was already present at
placement or was caused by TRL, no detention charge is made for the wagon.
7. Charges and billing
Detention charges are invoiced monthly by TRL Customer Billing, led by Wanchai Duangdee, with an
itemised list of wagons and periods. Invoices are issued on the fifth working day of the following month
and are payable within 30 days.
Detention charges are waived or reduced in the following cases:
TRL placed a wagon without the 12-hour advance placement notice required by your siding
agreement. Free time then starts at 06:00 on the day after placement.
Access to the siding was closed by flooding or by an order of a public authority. The clock is
suspended for the period of closure, which TRL Control records in SidingLink.
A shortage of trucks, staff or storage capacity at your own plant is not a reason to waive charges.
Questions about an invoice must be sent to billing@thanarak-rail.co.th within 15 days of the invoice date;
after that the invoice is treated as accepted.

ChillCrate Loan Service: Customer Fact Sheet
Mae Kuang Cold Store Co., Ltd., San Sai, Chiang Mai · Ref. MKC-CS-LF-07, version 3 · Issued 15 September
2026
1. What the service is
ChillCrate is Mae Kuang Cold Store's loan service for insulated, returnable crates with a built-in
temperature data logger. It is meant for small customers who collect chilled or frozen goods from our San
Sai warehouse in their own vehicles, such as cafés, bakeries, butchers, ice-cream makers and veterinary
clinics, and who do not own a refrigerated van. Each crate keeps its contents in range for a stated hold
time and records the temperature every 5 minutes.
The service is open to any business with a registered Mae Kuang customer account. Private individuals
cannot borrow crates. This version of the fact sheet replaces version 2 of 2 March 2026; the main
changes are the new deposit amount, the longer free loan period and the new Blue Line size.
2. Crate types
Green Line, 32 litres (chilled, +2 °C to +8 °C): uses two chilled gel packs; hold time 10 hours at an
outside temperature of up to 35 °C. Suitable for dairy, fresh meat and cakes.
Green Line, 60 litres (chilled, +2 °C to +8 °C): uses four chilled gel packs; hold time 8 hours.
Blue Line, 45 litres (frozen, −18 °C or colder): new from 1 October 2026; uses three phase-change
plates frozen at −25 °C; hold time 6 hours. Suitable for ice cream, frozen seafood and frozen dough.
Gel packs and plates are conditioned by our warehouse team and are inserted before the crate is handed
to you. Do not add your own ice, dry ice or gel packs: they change the hold time and can damage the
logger.
3. Prices and deposit
Loan fee: 90 baht per crate per loan for Green Line crates and 140 baht for the Blue Line crate.
Free loan period: 48 hours from collection, counted from the time printed on the hand-over slip. Until
30 September 2026 the free period was 24 hours.
Late return: 60 baht per crate for each started day after the free period.
Deposit: 1,500 baht per crate, paid by bank transfer or card at the Customer Desk. Until 30
September 2026 the deposit was 1,200 baht per crate; crates already on loan under the old deposit
keep it until they are returned.
Lost or unreturned crate: if a crate has not come back 14 days after collection, it is treated as lost
and the deposit is kept in full. A replacement logger alone is charged at 2,300 baht if only the logger
is missing or broken.
Note. Customers on a monthly storage contract of 20 pallet positions or more pay no loan fee for up
to 10 crates per month. Late-return charges and deposits still apply to them.

4. How to borrow a crate
1. Book on the Mae Kuang customer portal under Services > ChillCrate, or by phone at 053 104 772, at
least 24 hours before collection. Blue Line crates must be booked 48 hours ahead, because the
plates need a full freezing cycle.
2. Give the product type, the target temperature range and the expected travel time. Our team will
refuse a booking if the travel time is longer than the crate's hold time.
3. Come to Loading Bay 3 (chilled) or Loading Bay 5 (frozen) at the booked time, between 06:00 and
18:00, Monday to Saturday. Bring your customer account number and pay the deposit at the
Customer Desk first.
4. The bay checker loads your goods, closes the crate, starts the logger and gives you a hand-over slip
with the crate number, seal number and start time.
5. Keep the crate closed and out of direct sun. Do not break the seal until you reach your destination.
5. Returning a crate
Return crates empty, with all gel packs or plates inside, to the Returns Counter next to Loading Bay 1,
Monday to Saturday from 08:00 to 17:00. Crates cannot be returned on Sundays or public holidays; the
late-return charge is not added for those days. Remove all labels you added. A crate returned with food
residue is charged a cleaning fee of 150 baht.
At the counter, staff read the logger and give you a printed temperature summary. The full record (every
5-minute reading) is e-mailed to the account's registered address within one working day. Mae Kuang
keeps records for 12 months.
6. Deposit refunds
Deposit refunds are handled by the Customer Accounts team, led by Ms Kanyarat Inthawong, Customer
Service Lead. The deposit, less any late-return, cleaning or logger charges, is paid back to the original
card or bank account within 5 working days of the return. Questions about a refund go to
accounts@maekuangcold.example or extension 214.
7. If the temperature went out of range
If the printed summary shows an excursion (any reading outside the crate's range for more than 15
minutes in a row; a shorter rise while unloading is not counted), the counter staff mark the record and
send it to Mr Theerawat Moonkham, Quality and Temperature Assurance Officer. He decides whether the
cause was the crate or the way it was used, and replies within 2 working days (extension 238,
qa@maekuangcold.example). The decision whether the goods themselves can still be sold or used
remains the customer's own responsibility; Mae Kuang does not give advice on product safety.
If the cause was the crate (for example a faulty seal or a logger fault), the loan fee is refunded and the
crate is taken out of service for repair.
If the travel time exceeded the stated hold time, or the crate was left open or in the sun, no fee is
refunded.

Moving Home with Dwello: Handing Over, Resetting
or Taking Your Smart Home Devices
Thaweesuk Digital Home Co., Ltd., Bangkok · Dwello Help Centre · Ref. DW-HC-0412 · Version 2.1 · Updated
14 September 2026
This help-centre article is for Dwello customers who are selling a house or condominium, moving out of a
rental, or buying a home that already has a Dwello system installed. It replaces Version 1.4 of January
2026. Steps refer to the Dwello app version 5.8 or later on Android and iOS.
1. Before you start
Which devices does this article cover?
This article covers the Dwello Home Hub H3 and the older Home Hub H2, the Dwello Lock D7 door lock,
Dwello Sense door and window sensors, Dwello Aircare wall thermostats and the Dwello Leakstop water
shut-off valve. Dwello Eye indoor cameras are covered only where we say so; their recordings are
handled under the cloud video rules in section 6.
Which devices should stay in the home?
Devices that are fixed to the building are normally part of the sale or the rental contract and should stay:
the Lock D7, Aircare thermostats and the Leakstop valve. Plug-in devices such as the Home Hub, Sense
sensors and Eye cameras can be taken with you unless your sale agreement says otherwise. Removing a
Leakstop valve must be done by a licensed plumber, because the main water pipe has to be closed and
refitted.
What are my options?
Handover Pass: you pass the whole system, with its rooms, device names and automations, to the
next owner or resident. Your personal data is removed. This is the best choice when the devices stay
in the home.
Full reset: every device is returned to factory settings and removed from your account. The next
person sets everything up from the beginning.
Move Mode: you keep your setup and take the hub and plug-in devices to your new address.
2. Using the Dwello Handover Pass
How do I create a Handover Pass?
1. Make sure the Home Hub is online and every device shows a green status dot in the app.
2. Open the app and go to Home settings > Moving out > Create Handover Pass.
3. Confirm your account password and the one-time code sent to your registered mobile number.
4. Choose what to keep for the next person. Automations and room layout are kept by default; scenes
that use your personal phone location are always removed.
5. Give the 10-character Handover Pass code to the new owner, together with the hub's serial number
printed under the base.

The new owner enters the code under Add a home > I have a Handover Pass. The code is valid for 72
hours after it is created. Until 30 June 2026 the code was valid for 7 days, but we shortened it after
reports of codes being shared outside the sale. If the code expires, the original owner must create a new
one; an expired code cannot be extended.
What is removed when I hand over?
When the new owner accepts the code, the following are deleted from the home and cannot be
recovered: all Lock D7 PIN codes and fingerprints, the door entry history, family member accounts, guest
access links and your notification settings. Lock key cards are not deleted automatically. We recommend
you hand all key cards to the new owner, who should delete any missing cards under Lock > Key cards
on the first day.
3. Doing a full reset
How do I reset the Home Hub H3?
First remove the home from the app under Home settings > Remove this home. Then press and hold
the round button on the back of the H3 for 15 seconds, until the ring light flashes orange three times, and
release it. The hub restarts in about two minutes and the ring light turns slow blue, which means it is
ready for a new setup. Do not unplug the hub while the light is orange, as this can damage the firmware.
The older Home Hub H2 has no round button. Push a straightened paper clip into the pinhole marked
RESET next to the power socket and hold it for 30 seconds.
How do I reset the Lock D7?
The Lock D7 can only be reset with its master card, the black card supplied in the box. Open the battery
cover on the inside unit, hold the master card against the keypad and press the SET button for 5
seconds until you hear two beeps. The lock then deletes all users and returns to factory settings. If the
master card has been lost, the lock cannot be reset by the owner for security reasons and a Dwello
technician must visit with proof of ownership, such as a title deed copy, a sale contract or a tenancy
agreement in your name.
4. Taking your devices with you
How does Move Mode work?
Turn on Move Mode under Home settings > Moving out > Move Mode before you unplug the hub.
Move Mode saves your full setup in your account for 30 days. When you plug the hub in at the new
address and connect it to Wi-Fi, the app asks you to restore the saved setup. After 30 days the saved
setup is deleted and the hub must be set up as new.
5. Rentals and landlords
Can a landlord keep control of the devices?
Yes. Landlords should use a Dwello Landlord account, which is free. The landlord owns the home in the
app and gives each tenant the Resident role with an end date that matches the tenancy. Up to 6

residents can be added to one home. While a Resident role is active, the landlord cannot view Eye
camera feeds or the door entry history, but can still see device health and battery levels. On the end date
the Resident role is removed automatically and all PIN codes created by residents are deleted at 12:00
noon.
Tenants moving out of a home owned by a Landlord account do not need a Handover Pass or a full
reset. They only need to return the key cards and remove any of their own plug-in devices.
6. Subscriptions and cloud video
What happens to my Dwello Care subscription?
Dwello Care subscriptions belong to the person, not the home, and are not transferred with a Handover
Pass. Dwello Care Basic costs 79 baht per month and includes 7 days of camera history. Dwello Care
Plus costs 149 baht per month, or 1,440 baht if paid yearly, and includes 30 days of camera history,
priority phone support and one free technician visit per year.
You can cancel at any time under Account > Subscriptions. Monthly plans stop at the end of the current
month, with no refund for the remaining days. If you cancel a yearly Care Plus plan, we refund 120 baht
for each full month that has not yet started, minus an administration fee of 200 baht. No refund is made if
fewer than two full months remain.
A new owner who accepts a Handover Pass receives a 60-day free trial of Care Plus, once per home.
What happens to my camera recordings?
When you hand over or reset the home, your Eye camera recordings are not passed to the new owner.
They remain in your account for 14 days, so you can download any clips you want to keep, and are then
permanently deleted.
7. Getting help
How do I book a technician?
Book a visit in the app under Help > Book a technician or call the Dwello Help Centre on 02 118 4630,
from 08:00 to 20:00 every day. Visits are available from Monday to Saturday and must be booked at least
two working days ahead. A visit costs 450 baht in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani and Samut
Prakan, and 850 baht in all other provinces. The fee covers up to one hour of work; replacement parts
are charged separately. Care Plus subscribers get one visit per year at no charge, in any province.

Float First: Free Swimming and Water-Safety
Lessons for Grades 2 to 4 Begin in November
Saeng Arun Primary School, Phitsanulok · Parent Newsletter Issue 2026/07 · Published 1 October 2026
Phitsanulok, 1 October 2026 – Every pupil in Grades 2, 3 and 4 at Saeng Arun Primary School will take
part in Float First, a new ten-week swimming and water-safety programme, during the second semester.
Lessons take place at the Bueng Phra Aquatic Centre, about 6 kilometres from the school, and start on
Tuesday 10 November 2026.
1. Why the school is starting Float First
Many of our families live close to the Nan River and the irrigation canals east of Bueng Phra, and the
floods of September 2025 reached two of the village roads our pupils use every day. In June 2026 our
physical education team ran a simple water-confidence check with 238 pupils in Grades 2 to 4. Only 92
of them could float on their back for 30 seconds without help, and 54 had never been in water deeper
than their waist. The school board decided that learning to float and to call for help is as basic a skill as
reading and road safety.
"We do not expect every child to become a strong swimmer in ten weeks," said Director Nanthawan
Sirikhet. "We want every child to know how to stay on the surface, how to help a friend without jumping
in, and when to stay away from the water altogether."
2. Who takes part and what it costs
All pupils in Grades 2, 3 and 4 are included in Float First as part of the physical education timetable.
Grade 1 pupils are not included this year; a shorter pilot for Grade 1 is planned for the first semester of
2027. Grade 5 and 6 pupils are not part of the weekly lessons, but Grade 5 pupils who took part in the
2025 trial and did not pass its final swim check may join the Saturday catch-up group described in
section 7.
Lessons, instructors and the school bus are free for families. The programme is funded by a grant of
186,000 baht from the Nan Riverbank Community Fund and by the Saeng Arun Parents' Association.
Families only pay for the pupil kit:
Float First kit (swimming cap, mesh bag and name tag): 120 baht, paid to the class teacher together
with the consent form. Families who hold a school fee waiver receive the kit free of charge.
Swimwear: families provide their own. Plain, close-fitting swimwear is required; T-shirts, jeans and
football shorts are not allowed in the pool.
Replacement cap: 40 baht if a cap is lost or damaged.
Parents of last year's Grade 4 pupils may remember the trial lessons at a private pool in 2025, which cost
350 baht per child for six sessions. That fee no longer applies.
3. Timetable and transport
Each grade has one lesson per week on a fixed day, for ten sessions in total:

Grade 2: Tuesdays, from 10 November 2026.
Grade 3: Wednesdays, from 11 November 2026.
Grade 4: Thursdays, from 12 November 2026.
Sessions run weekly until the week of 22 December 2026, pause for the New Year break, and continue in
the weeks of 5, 12 and 19 January 2027. The final session in the week of 19 January is the assessment
session. Because Thursday 10 December 2026 is a public holiday, the Grade 4 session for that week
moves to Friday 11 December.
The school bus leaves from Gate 2 (the Rim Khlong Road gate) at 13:10 and returns to Gate 2 at 15:20.
Each session lasts 90 minutes at the centre, of which 45 minutes are spent in the water; the remaining
time is for changing, a short safety talk on the poolside and a head count. Two teachers travel on every
bus. Parents who collect their children at 15:20 should wait at Gate 2, not at the main gate, because the
main gate car park is closed to cars between 15:00 and 15:45.
4. Consent forms and health questions
Every pupil needs a signed Float First consent form (form F-07, sent home in the blue folder this week)
and the one-page health questionnaire. Both must reach the class teacher by Friday 23 October 2026.
Pupils whose forms have not arrived by that date cannot travel to the pool and will stay at school for a
supervised reading session in the library until their forms are received.
The school nurse, Ratchanee Inthapan, reviews every health questionnaire. A doctor's note confirming
that the child may swim is required before the first session for pupils with epilepsy, a heart condition, ear
grommets (ventilation tubes) or a perforated eardrum. Asthma does not require a doctor's note, but a
child with asthma must bring their reliever inhaler in the mesh bag every week; without it the child may
not enter the water that day.
Illness on the day
Parents should keep the child out of the water, and tell the class teacher in the morning, if the child has a
fever, vomiting or diarrhoea in the previous 48 hours, an open wound or a skin infection, or conjunctivitis
(red, sticky eyes). A child who has had an ear infection in the last 7 days also sits out, even if they feel
well. Children who sit out still travel with the class and take part in the poolside safety talk, unless they
have a fever, in which case they stay at school.
Note. A child who sits out for health reasons is not marked absent for the purpose of the certificate
(see section 7) if the parent informed the class teacher by 08:30 on the day.
5. Safety at the pool
All lessons are taught by instructors from the Bueng Phra Aquatic Centre who hold a current lifesaving
qualification, and one lifeguard watches the teaching area at all times. Pupils are grouped by ability using
cap colours, and the number of children per instructor depends on the group:
Red cap: cannot yet float without help. At most 6 pupils per instructor, in water no deeper than 0.9
metres.

Yellow cap: can float on the back for 30 seconds but cannot yet swim 15 metres. At most 8 pupils
per instructor, in the 1.1-metre section.
Green cap: can swim 15 metres without stopping. At most 10 pupils per instructor, and may use the
1.4-metre section with an instructor in the water.
Every child starts in a red cap in the first session and moves up after the instructor checks them. Pupils
may not move to a deeper section on their own, even if a friend is there. Teachers do a head count when
pupils enter the water, every 15 minutes during the lesson and again when they leave.
6. What pupils will learn
The programme follows the "Float, Shout, Reach" approach. Pupils learn to float on their back and their
front, to tread water, to turn towards the side and hold on, and to shout and wave for help. They also
practise helping a friend from the side by reaching with a pole or throwing a floating object, and they
learn the rule that children never jump in to rescue someone. Two short classroom lessons in December
cover flooded roads and canal edges.
At the assessment session in the week of 19 January 2027, pupils who can float for 2 minutes, tread
water for 30 seconds and swim 10 metres to the side receive the Float First Certificate. Pupils who also
swim 25 metres without stopping receive the Float First Gold badge in addition to the certificate. Results
are sent home with the semester report.
7. Missed sessions, rain and the Saturday catch-up group
To receive the certificate, a pupil must attend at least 8 of the 10 sessions as well as the assessment. A
pupil who misses 3 or more sessions is not assessed in January, but may finish the programme in the
Saturday catch-up group, which meets at the centre on 30 January and 6 February 2027 from 09:00 to
11:00. Parents bring their child to the centre for these Saturday sessions, as there is no school bus.
Catch-up pupils who pass the checks on 6 February receive the certificate in the same way.
If an official thunderstorm warning is issued for Mueang Phitsanulok, or lightning is seen near the centre,
the session is cancelled. The school will post a cancellation in the class LINE group by 11:30 on the day.
A cancelled session does not count as a missed session: it is replaced in the reserve week of 26 January
2027, on the same weekday as usual. If a pupil cannot attend the replacement session, it does count as
missed.
8. Contacts
Programme questions, timetable and catch-up places: Teerapong Khamwilai, PE Coordinator, Room
B-104, telephone 055 214 377 (school hours).
Health questionnaire and doctor's notes: Ratchanee Inthapan, School Nurse, Health Room next to
the canteen.
Kit payments and fee waivers: the school office, Building A, ground floor, Monday to Friday 08:00 to
16:00.
Parents may watch a lesson from the spectator seats after registering at the centre reception.

Rest, Rest-Period Advance and Tapping
Resumption

Tapping while the trees shed and regrow their leaves in the dry months weakens them and increases the
risk of tapping panel dryness, so the estate stops all tapping during wintering. This year the rest is longer

the tapping panels for dryness and bark disease, the condition of the cups, spouts and hangers, and the

Blocks A to C: inspection from 9 March to 13 March 2026.
Blocks D to F: inspection from 16 March to 20 March 2026.

inspects its rows. A household that misses its inspection date must phone the field office on 075 291 448
to book a new date, and cannot resume tapping until the inspection is completed. Trees marked with a
yellow ring of paint show signs of panel dryness. They must not be tapped until the field supervisor
removes the mark, which normally takes one to three months.
6. First weeks after resumption
For the first two weeks after resumption, tapping is every third day instead of every second day, so that
the new leaves can mature. Stimulant may not be applied to any panel until 20 April 2026.
Questions about this notice: Pornthip Chuaykliang, Estate Manager, 075 291 441.

Khlong Sakae Bridge Barge Strike Inspection
Pa Sak Structural Diagnostics Co., Ltd. for Krungkao Crossing Co., Ltd. · Ref. PSD-IR-2026-031 · Issued 18
September 2026
1. Incident and scope
At about 04:40 on 14 September 2026, a loaded sand barge drifting downstream on the Pa Sak River
struck the upstream nose of Pier P3 of the Khlong Sakae Bridge, the four-span toll bridge (KC-04) in
Ayutthaya owned by Krungkao Crossing. Pier P3, its bearings and spans 2 and 3 were inspected on 15
September, and the P3 pile cap was surveyed underwater on 16 September.
2. Findings
Pier P3 upstream nose: concrete spalled over an area of about 1.6 m by 0.9 m, with two main
reinforcing bars exposed but not bent. Two diagonal cracks of 0.4 mm and 0.25 mm run from the
spall.
Pile cap: the steel fender frame on the upstream side is torn over a length of 3.2 m and two of its five
timber rubbing strips are missing.
Bearings at P3: the elastomeric bearing under girder G2 of span 3 has shifted 12 mm laterally; the
other seven bearings at P3 are within the 5 mm tolerance.
The structure is rated Condition Class C (serious defect, safe under restriction). It was Class B at the
routine inspection of 22 February 2026.
3. Interim traffic restrictions
The bridge reopened at 16:00 on 17 September 2026 with the following restrictions:
Gross vehicle weight limit: 18 tonnes (the normal limit is 25 tonnes). Buses on the Route 9 shuttle
service are exempt up to 21 tonnes but must cross one at a time.
Speed limit: 30 km/h on spans 2 and 3; 50 km/h elsewhere on the bridge.

Nong Lom Chatbot: Rules of Use and Handover
Policy
Jomtien Crest Residences Management Co., Ltd. · Ref. JCR-POL-2026-07, version 2.0 · Approved by the
Management Committee on 18 August 2026 · Effective 1 September 2026
1. Purpose and scope
Jomtien Crest Residences Management Co., Ltd. ("the Management Office") manages the four
condominium buildings of Jomtien Crest Residences on Thappraya Road, Jomtien, Chon Buri: Buildings
A (Sea Wing), B (Garden Wing), C (Hill Wing) and D (Studio Wing), with 1,186 units in total. Since 3
February 2025 it has used an automated chatbot, Nong Lom, to answer routine questions and register
maintenance requests.
This policy sets out what Nong Lom may and may not do, when a conversation must be handed to staff,
and how records are kept. It applies to owners, registered tenants, and household members aged 15 or
over who are listed on the unit's resident card. It also applies to all Management Office staff who read or
act on chatbot records. Version 2.0 replaces version 1.3 of 10 January 2025.
2. Where Nong Lom is available
Nong Lom can be reached 24 hours a day through three channels:
the Jomtien Crest official LINE account;
the chat window in the Resident Portal;
the touch-screen kiosk in the lobby of Building B, next to the parcel room.
Nong Lom answers in Thai, English, Russian and Simplified Chinese. A resident may switch language at
any time by typing "language" followed by the language name. Voice messages are not processed.
To use any service that concerns a specific unit, the resident must first link their LINE or portal account to
their unit with the one-time code printed on the resident card. Without a linked account, Nong Lom gives
general information only.
3. Services Nong Lom may provide
Within its approved scope, Nong Lom may:
1. answer questions using only the approved knowledge base, which consists of the House Rules (2026
edition), the Common Facilities Guide, published notices, and the fee schedule approved by the
Annual General Meeting;
2. register maintenance requests for common areas and for unit faults covered by the Management
Office, and give the resident a request number in the format MR-2026-00000;
3. book the meeting room on the 2nd floor of Building A, the barbecue terrace and the guest parking
bays, subject to the booking rules in the Common Facilities Guide;
4. notify residents of parcels received;
5. issue a statement of the common fee balance and a QR code for payment to the juristic person's
bank account;

Every answer about rules or fees must show the source (for example "House Rules, rule 4.2") so that the
resident can check it. If the knowledge base has no answer, Nong Lom must say so and offer a handover
to staff. It must not guess.
4. Things Nong Lom must not do
The following actions are reserved to staff and are blocked in the chatbot:
waive, reduce or postpone the common fee, the sinking fund contribution or any late-payment
surcharge;
approve renovation works, the use of the service lift for moving furniture, or access for contractors
outside the permitted working hours of 08:30 to 17:00, Monday to Saturday;
release CCTV recordings, or confirm whether a particular person entered the building;
share another resident's name, phone number, unit number or vehicle registration.
For these requests Nong Lom opens a handover (section 5) or gives the correct form.
Note. Nong Lom can show a resident the late-payment surcharge that applies to their own account,
but only the Resident Services Manager, Ms Saowalak Rattanaporn, may approve a waiver, and only
in writing after a request on form JCR-F12.
5. Handover to staff
5.1 When a handover is mandatory
Nong Lom must stop answering and transfer the conversation to a person in any of the following cases:
the resident types "staff", "human" or " เจ้าหน้าที่ ", or asks for a person in any supported language;
the message describes an urgent safety situation: fire or smoke, a gas smell, water leaking into
another unit or into an electrical room, a person trapped in a lift, a medical emergency, or a threat of
violence;
the resident has asked the same question three times without a satisfactory answer;
the message is a formal complaint about a staff member, a contractor or the security team;
5.2 Urgent safety messages
For urgent safety messages Nong Lom immediately shows the 24-hour security control room number
(038 251 400, extension 1) and sends an alert to the control room screen and to the on-duty building
engineer. The control room must call the resident back within 5 minutes. Nong Lom always tells the
resident to call 191 or 1669 first if there is danger to life. Urgent messages are never placed in the normal
queue.
5.3 Normal handovers and response times
Non-urgent handovers go to the Resident Services team. During office hours (Monday to Saturday, 08:00
to 19:00) a staff member must reply within 30 minutes. Handovers received outside office hours, or on
Sundays and public holidays, must receive a reply by 10:00 on the next working day. Until 31 August

2026 the office-hours target was 60 minutes; it was shortened when the team was increased from three
to five officers.
6. Conversation records and personal data
Conversations are handled under the Privacy Notice (version 4, May 2026). The Data Protection Officer,
Mr Chaiwat Phongsri, is responsible for the retention rules in this section.
Text of conversations: kept for 180 days from the last message, then deleted automatically. Under
version 1.3 this period was 1 year.
Photos and videos sent with maintenance requests: kept for 90 days after the request is closed.
Records linked to a complaint, an insurance claim or an incident report: kept for 2 years after
the case is closed, and then deleted.
Residents must not send ID card images, passport pages or bank card details through Nong Lom. If
such an image is received, Nong Lom warns the resident and the image is deleted within 24 hours.
Documents that require ID must be submitted at the counter on the ground floor of Building B.
7. Quality checks
Every month, the Resident Services Manager reviews a random sample of 150 conversations, of which at
least 20 must be in English, Russian or Chinese. An answer counts as correct if it agrees with the
approved knowledge base and gives the right source. The target is at least 95 % correct answers. If the
result falls below 90 % in any month, the Management Office restricts Nong Lom to registering
maintenance requests and bookings, and stops free-text answers about rules and fees, until the
knowledge base has been corrected and a new sample of 50 conversations reaches 95 %.
8. Residents' rights and opting out
Using Nong Lom is optional: the same services are available by phone, by e-mail or at the counter. A
resident who does not want their conversations kept for quality checks may type "no review" at the start
of a conversation; that conversation is then excluded from the monthly sample, although it is still kept for
the normal retention period in section 6.
9. Complaints and review of this policy
Complaints about Nong Lom, including wrong answers that caused a missed booking, may be made on
form JCR-F14 at the counter or by e-mail. The Resident Services Manager replies within 7 working days.
If the complaint concerns personal data, it is passed to the Data Protection Officer, who replies within 15
days.
The Management Committee reviews this policy every year in August, or earlier if Nong Lom is given a
new service. Changes are announced on the LINE account at least 14 days before they take effect.
