Daenglift to Delete Precise Trip Routes after 30
Days
Press release · Lanna Lift Mobility Co., Ltd. · Ref. PR-2026-09 · For immediate release, 1 October 2026
CHIANG MAI, 1 October 2026 – Lanna Lift Mobility Co., Ltd., the operator of the Daenglift app for
booking shared red-truck rides in Chiang Mai and Lamphun, today announced shorter limits on how long
it keeps personal data. The changes follow a privacy review completed in August 2026 and cover all
riders and the 1,240 driver partners.
1. What changes on 1 November 2026
Precise GPS route of each trip: deleted 30 days after the trip. Until 31 October 2026 these routes
were kept for 18 months.
Pickup and drop-off areas: kept for 12 months, rounded to an area of about 500 metres, for fare
disputes.
Payment and receipt records: kept for 5 years (unchanged).
In-vehicle camera footage: kept on the driver’s camera for 14 days, then overwritten. If an incident
report is filed within those 14 days, the footage is copied to secure storage and kept for up to 180
days.
Closed accounts: erased within 30 days of the deletion request (previously 90 days), except
payment records.
Exception. If a rider or driver has an open complaint or safety report about a trip, the precise route of
that trip is kept until the case is closed, but never longer than 12 months after the trip. It is then
deleted.
2. Faster access to your own data
Riders can ask for a copy of the data Daenglift holds about them in the app under Settings › Privacy › My
Data. From 1 November 2026 the company will answer within 15 days instead of 30. The first copy in any
12 months is free; each further copy in the same 12 months costs 100 baht, charged to the Daenglift
wallet.
“After a month we do not need a rider’s exact route home, so we will not keep it,” said Kanyarat
Phetchompoo, Data Protection Officer. “Complaints about how we handle personal data should come to
my team; we reply within 7 working days.”
3. Contacts
Data protection questions and complaints: Kanyarat Phetchompoo, Data Protection Officer,
dpo@lannalift.example, or by post to 88/4 Chang Phueak Road, Chiang Mai 50300.
Media contact: Pakorn Siriwattana, Communications Manager, press@lannalift.example (media
enquiries only; data requests sent here are not processed).

Internal Memo: New Limits on Remote Fault Resets
and Return to Service
Rongnam Lift Engineering Co., Ltd., Hat Yai · Ref. RLE-OPS-MEMO-2026-11 · 21 September 2026
To: All dispatchers, field technicians, field supervisors and contract managers
From: Narumon Kaewprasert, Head of Service Operations (Room 2C, ext. 220)
Subject: Which faults may be reset through the UpSight portal, effective Monday 5 October 2026
1. Background
At 01:40 on 3 September 2026 a night dispatcher used the UpSight remote monitoring portal to reset a
door lock fault on passenger lift L3 at a multi-storey car park on Phetkasem Road. The lift returned to
service and ran for 26 minutes while the landing door at level 4 was not fully locked. Nobody was hurt.
UpSight logs show 214 remote resets from January to August 2026, 37 of them for door circuit faults.
2. Decision
From Monday 5 October 2026, every fault shown in UpSight is placed in one of three categories, and
what a dispatcher may do depends on the category. Until 4 October 2026 the old rule applies: a
dispatcher may make up to 2 remote resets per lift in any 24 hours, for any type of fault.
2.1 Category A – safety faults (never reset remotely)
Category A covers door lock and landing door contact faults, safety circuit open, overspeed governor
trip, brake monitoring faults, safety gear operation, pit stop switch, and any fault that occurs while the
car is more than 300 mm away from a floor level. A Category A fault may only be cleared by a technician
standing at the lift. The dispatcher sends the nearest available technician at once.
2.2 Category B – drive and control faults (supervisor approval)
Category B covers inverter overheating, drive communication loss, encoder faults, levelling errors of 15
mm or more, and repeated door reopening caused by the door motor. A dispatcher may make one
remote reset of a Category B fault per lift in any 24 hours, and only after the duty field supervisor has
approved it by phone. After any approved Category B reset, a technician must visit the lift within 48
hours to find the cause. If the same Category B fault returns within those 24 hours, it is treated as a
Category A fault.
2.3 Category C – comfort faults (dispatcher may reset)
Category C covers car lighting, the ventilation fan, the floor display and voice announcer, the car
intercom test warning, and levelling errors below 15 mm. A dispatcher may reset a Category C fault
remotely without approval, at most 3 times per lift in any 24 hours. A fourth one is left for the next routine
maintenance visit.
Note. UpSight version 4.2 will be installed on the night of Sunday 4 October 2026. From that version
the portal greys out the reset button for every Category A fault. Until the update, dispatchers must
apply these rules by hand from 5 October.

3. Trapped passengers
A remote reset must never be used to release trapped passengers, whatever the category of the fault.
When the intercom or the building reports an entrapment, the dispatcher keeps voice contact with the
passengers every 10 minutes and sends a technician under the rescue procedure RP-04. Our target
attendance times for entrapments are 30 minutes for hospital lifts, 45 minutes elsewhere in Hat Yai
municipality, and 90 minutes for sites outside the municipality, including Sadao and Songkhla city.
4. Returning a lift to service after a Category A fault
1. The technician corrects the cause and tests the door locks on every landing.
2. The technician runs the lift for at least 5 complete trips from the lowest to the highest floor with no
passengers.
3. The technician makes a video call to the duty field supervisor and shows the repaired part and the
final test run. The supervisor confirms the return to service on the call.
4. The technician completes return-to-service form RS-2 in UpSight, including the supervisor's
confirmation time, before switching the lift back to normal operation.
If the supervisor cannot be reached within 20 minutes, the lift stays out of service and the technician calls
the Head of Service Operations.
5. Responsibilities
Dispatch Lead (Somkiat Rattanaphol, Control Room 1B, ext. 110): makes sure every shift follows the
categories, checks the reset log each morning at 08:00 and reports any breach to the Head of
Service Operations the same day.
Duty field supervisor: approves or refuses Category B resets and confirms every Category A return
to service.
Field technicians: attend Category A faults, carry out the test runs and complete form RS-2.
Safety Officer: audits 10 randomly chosen RS-2 forms each month and reports the result to the
monthly safety meeting.
6. Charges to customers
Customers with a Comprehensive contract pay nothing extra for any callout. Customers with a Basic
contract pay a callout charge for every visit made outside contract hours (Monday to Friday, 08:00 to
17:00). From 1 July 2026 this out-of-hours callout charge is 1,800 baht per visit; until 30 June 2026 it was
1,500 baht. Basic contract customers will not be charged for the follow-up visit required after an
approved Category B reset. Callouts for Category A faults are charged as normal.
7. Briefings and transition
Dispatchers and field supervisors must attend one briefing in Training Room 3B on 29 or 30 September
2026, 13:30 to 15:30. Technicians are briefed at depot toolbox talks. Contract managers send customer
letter CL-09 to all building managers by Friday 2 October 2026.

Riding in the Rainy Season: Plaewlom Rain Pause
FAQ
Plaewlom Mobility Co., Ltd., Chiang Mai · Plaew Help Centre · Ref. PLM-HC-0218 · Version 3.0 · Updated 8
September 2026
This article explains what happens to your Plaew e-scooter ride when heavy rain, strong wind or flooding
makes riding unsafe in Chiang Mai. It applies to all Plaew S4 and older Plaew S3 scooters in our Chiang
Mai service area. It replaces Version 2.2 of June 2025.
1. What a Rain Pause is
What is a Rain Pause?
A Rain Pause is a temporary stop to new rides in all or part of the service area. The map turns grey in the
affected area, the Unlock button is disabled, and scooters already on the road show a warning on the
handlebar display.
When is a Rain Pause started?
We start a Rain Pause when any of our 14 roadside weather sensors records rainfall of 8 mm or more in
one hour, or wind gusts of 50 km/h or more. Until 31 May 2026 the rainfall trigger was 15 mm per hour;
we lowered it after a review of wet-weather falls during the 2025 season. A Rain Pause is also started for
a single district when water stands on a road in that district, even if the rain has stopped.
Who decides to start and end a Rain Pause?
The decision is made by the Duty Operations Controller in the Plaewlom Control Room on Huay Kaew
Road, which is staffed from 05:30 to 01:00 every day. A person always confirms the pause and decides
when it ends. Outside staffed hours the system starts a pause on its own when a trigger is reached, and
it stays on until the first controller of the morning shift lifts it. Ride credits are handled by the Rider Care
team (section 3).
How long does a Rain Pause last?
A pause lasts at least 30 minutes. It ends when the rainfall has stayed below 4 mm per hour for 20
minutes in a row and no road in the area is reported as flooded.
2. If you are already riding
Will my scooter stop suddenly?
No. Your scooter never switches off in motion. When a pause begins, the top speed of the scooter is
reduced from 20 km/h to 12 km/h and the display shows a blue rain symbol. Please end the ride as soon
as it is safe to do so.
Do I keep paying per minute?
The normal fare is 10 baht to unlock plus 3 baht per minute. During a Rain Pause the per-minute charge
stops automatically 15 minutes after the pause begins, so a ride that continues longer is not charged for

the extra time. The unlock fee is never refunded once the ride has started.
Note. Plaew Pass holders (399 baht per 30 days) already ride without a per-minute charge for the
first 45 minutes of each ride. If a single Rain Pause lasts more than 6 hours, your Pass is extended
by one day automatically.
Where can I end my ride during a pause?
During a Rain Pause the usual rule that rides must end inside a purple parking zone is relaxed. You may
end your ride on any pavement at least 1.5 metres wide, as long as the scooter does not block a
doorway, a bus stop or a ramp. The normal out-of-zone parking fee of 100 baht is waived for rides that
end within 60 minutes of the start of the pause.
This relaxation does not apply in Red Flood Zones. They include the riverside roads along the Ping River
between Nawarat Bridge and Iron Bridge, the underpass at Khuang Singh intersection and the low
section of Wua Lai Road. Ending a ride inside a Red Flood Zone costs 300 baht at any time, because our
team must recover the scooter before the water rises.
What if my battery runs out during a pause?
If the battery level falls below 5 % during a Rain Pause, you may end the ride wherever you are, including
inside a Red Flood Zone, and neither the 100-baht nor the 300-baht fee is charged. To qualify, report the
low battery through the app within 30 minutes of ending the ride and attach a photo of the parked
scooter. Without the report within 30 minutes, the normal fees apply.
3. Ride credits and refunds
Can I get credit for a ride cut short by a Rain Pause?
Yes. If you had to end a ride early because of a pause, you can receive a ride credit equal to the time
charges of that ride, up to 60 baht per ride. Credits are added to your Plaew wallet, cannot be paid out in
cash and expire 90 days after they are issued.
How do I claim the credit?
1. Open the Plaew app and go to Account > Ride history.
2. Choose the affected ride and tap Report a problem > Ride ended by Rain Pause.
3. Add a short description of where you stopped. A photo is optional unless you parked inside a Red
Flood Zone.
4. Send the claim no later than 7 days after the ride. Claims sent after 7 days are not accepted.
The Rider Care team reviews claims within 2 working days and sends the result to your registered email
address.
4. Safety and contact
Plaew scooters are rated IPX5 and can be ridden in light rain, but never through standing water deeper
than 5 cm. If you see a Plaew scooter lying in floodwater or blocking a road, report it in the app under
Report a scooter, or call Rider Care on 053 118 460 (06:00 to 24:00).

Minutes of the KongTrace Platform Team Decision
Meeting: Retirement of the v2 Public API
Pingthara Software Co., Ltd., Chiang Mai · Ref. PTS-KT-MIN-2026-19 · Meeting held 24 September 2026 ·
Minutes approved 30 September 2026
Venue: Meeting Room Doi Inthanon (4th floor), Pingthara office, Nimmanhaemin Road, Chiang Mai, with
remote attendance by video call, 10:00–12:10.
Present: Thitima Chaiwong (Engineering Manager, chair); Anucha Rattanakorn (Staff Engineer, API
Gateway); Natcha Boonmee (Partner Integrations Lead); Pakorn Siriwan (Site Reliability Engineer); Jirapat
Khamsaen (QA Lead, remote); Sasithorn Wongdee (Product Manager, KongTrace). Minutes: Ekkachai
Phumipat (Technical Writer). Apologies: Wanchai Inthong (Head of Customer Support).
1. Approval of the previous minutes
The minutes of meeting PTS-KT-MIN-2026-17 (27 August 2026) were approved with one correction: the
API gateway upgrade recorded under item 4 was to version 3.14.2, not 3.12.2.
2. Current use of the v2 Public API
Anucha Rattanakorn presented the traffic figures for the four weeks ending 20 September 2026. The
KongTrace v2 Public API still carries about 14 percent of all tracking requests, down from 31 percent in
June 2026. Of the 212 partner accounts that call the API, 37 still send at least some requests to v2. Nine
of these 37 send more than 50,000 v2 requests per day and are treated as "large v2 users". The largest
of these is a regional courier in Hat Yai that has not yet started its migration.
The meeting noted that v2 depends on the old tracking-event database cluster (kt-events-legacy), which
runs on hardware whose support contract ends on 31 March 2027. Keeping v2 alive after that date would
require a new hardware contract quoted at 1,240,000 baht per year. Sasithorn Wongdee confirmed that
no partner contract obliges Pingthara to keep v2 beyond the published sunset date, provided at least
120 days of written notice is given.
3. Decision 19-1: retirement timeline
The meeting agreed the following timeline for the retirement of v2. The originally announced sunset date
was 30 November 2026; it was moved because the notice letters to partners were sent late, on 14
August 2026, and the 120-day notice period must be respected.
Deprecation headers: from 1 October 2026 every v2 response carries a "Sunset" header with the final
date and a link to the migration guide.
First brownout: Tuesday 3 November 2026, 10:00–11:00. All v2 requests receive an error response
with code 410 during this hour.
Second brownout: Tuesday 8 December 2026, 10:00–14:00 (4 hours).
Third brownout: Tuesday 5 January 2027, 09:00–17:00 (8 hours).
Final sunset: Monday 18 January 2027 at 09:00 (Bangkok time). After this moment v2 returns code
410 permanently and the v2 endpoints are removed from the gateway configuration one week later.

Brownouts are never scheduled on the 1st or the last working day of a month, because many partners
run monthly billing jobs on those days. Pakorn Siriwan confirmed that none of the dates above clashes
with this rule. Thitima Chaiwong noted that no brownout may be cancelled without her written approval;
a cancelled brownout is not replaced by a later one.
Note. The v2 webhook service is not part of this decision. Webhooks registered through v2 keep
working until the webhook redesign is finished, and their retirement will be decided at a separate
meeting in the first quarter of 2027.
4. Decision 19-2: extension requests from partners
Natcha Boonmee proposed a controlled extension process for partners who cannot finish their migration
by the sunset date. The meeting agreed that an extension keeps a partner's v2 access open after the
final sunset through a separate allow-list on the gateway. Extensions are granted only to partners on the
Business or Enterprise plan; partners on the Starter plan are not eligible. The procedure is as follows:
1. The partner's account owner submits the "v2 Extension Request" form in the KongTrace partner
portal no later than 7 December 2026. Requests sent by e-mail or through the support chat are not
accepted.
2. The form must include a named technical contact, the current migration status, and a migration plan
with a target completion date.
3. The Partner Integrations team checks the request within 5 working days and arranges a 30-minute
review call with the partner's technical contact.
4. Natcha Boonmee recommends approval or refusal, and Thitima Chaiwong makes the final decision.
The partner receives the decision in writing through the portal.
5. If approved, Pakorn Siriwan adds the partner's API keys to the extension allow-list before the final
sunset.
An extension lasts for a maximum of 60 calendar days after the final sunset and cannot be renewed.
During an extension the partner's v2 traffic is limited to 20 requests per second, compared with the
normal v2 limit of 100 requests per second. Partners with an extension are still affected by the three
brownouts. A fee of 15,000 baht per month or part of a month applies to each extension, except for
partners whose contract started before 1 January 2024, who receive the extension free of charge.
5. Rate limits and support for migrating partners
Anucha Rattanakorn reported that the v3 batch tracking endpoint, which accepts up to 200 tracking
numbers in one call, is now generally available. Partners moving from v2 often make many single-number
calls, so the team agreed to raise the v3 limit for migrating partners from 50 to 150 requests per second
for 90 days after their first v3 call. The higher limit is applied automatically; partners do not need to
request it.
Natcha Boonmee will hold two online migration clinics for partners, on 15 October 2026 and 12
November 2026, both from 14:00 to 15:30. The nine large v2 users will each be offered a personal
migration session with an engineer from the API Gateway group. The Hat Yai courier has already booked
its session for 8 October 2026.

6. Testing and release of the v2 shutdown
Jirapat Khamsaen explained the test plan for the shutdown. All v2 shutdown changes will be tested first
on the staging environment, then on the partner sandbox, where v2 will be switched off on 19 October
2026, three months before the production sunset. Contract tests for the 14 most used v3 endpoints must
pass on every build before the sunset configuration is merged. The gateway configuration change for the
final sunset will be released by Pakorn Siriwan and reviewed by Anucha Rattanakorn; no other team
member may approve it.
The meeting confirmed that a rollback is allowed only during the first 2 hours after the final sunset and
only if more than 5 percent of all v3 requests fail in that time. A rollback for any other reason, including
requests from partners, requires a new decision by the chair.
7. On-call arrangements for the sunset week
For the week of 18 to 22 January 2027 the on-call rotation will be doubled: two engineers will be on call
at all times instead of one. Pakorn Siriwan will be primary on-call on 18 January. Engineers on the
doubled rotation receive the normal on-call allowance of 1,800 baht per day plus an extra 600 baht per
day for the sunset week. Customer Support will keep a dedicated chat channel open from 08:00 to 20:00

07 · Issued 1 October 2026
This notice is for every runner registered for the Lampang Wang Riverside City Marathon 2026, which

transfer, change or defer your entry. It replaces Notice WRCM-N-2026-04 of 2 July 2026.

Embankment repairs will close the riverside road between the old wooden bridge and Kad Kong Ta street
from 1 December 2026 to 31 January 2027, so our original start line cannot be used. All distances will
now start from the north car park of the Lampang Municipal Stadium on Phahonyothin Road. The finish

announced:

10 km run: 05:30, previously 06:00.
5 km Family Fun Run: 06:15, previously 06:30.

08:20. The half marathon has a time limit of 3 hours 30 minutes, which means its course closes at 08:15.

Seedling Survival Survey Summary – Enrichment
Planting 2025
Khok Pa Rang Community Forest Committee, Phanna Nikhom District, Sakon Nakhon · Ref. KPR-SV-2026-03
· Issued 18 September 2026
1. Purpose and survey details
This summary reports the first-year survival count for the Khok Pa Rang Enrichment Planting 2025, in
which 3,600 native seedlings were planted in three plots between 12 and 20 July 2025. The count was
carried out from 8 to 10 September 2026 by nine village volunteers and four Grade 11 students, led by
Survey Lead Anchalee Boonrueang.
2. Results by plot
Plot A – Upper Ridge: 1,400 planted, 1,078 surviving (77 %).
Plot B – Stream Bank: 1,200 planted, 588 surviving (49 %). Of the 612 dead seedlings, 430 were
recorded as killed by the stream overflow of 19–24 August 2026, when water stood on the plot for six
days.
Plot C – Old Cassava Field: 1,000 planted, 710 surviving (71 %). Around 150 seedlings were
browsed or trampled by cattle before the bamboo fence was finished on 2 October 2025.
By species, Makha Mong did best across all plots, followed by Yang Na. Pradu had the weakest survival
on dry ground.
3. Replanting rule applied
Under the resolution of the general meeting of 22 March 2026, any plot with first-year survival below 60
% is replanted in the next rainy season. Until that meeting the threshold was 50 %. Plots A and C are
above the threshold and will receive only gap filling by volunteers, limited to 100 seedlings per plot.
Exception. Where more than half of a plot's dead seedlings were killed by flooding, replanting is
postponed by one year so that the planting layout can be redesigned, and only flood-tolerant
species may be used. The redesign must be approved by the committee chair before any seedlings
are ordered.
4. Actions and next steps
Committee Chair Kittisak Phonsawan will review the Plot B redesign at the committee meeting on 12
December 2026.
Volunteers will repair the Plot C fence by 31 October 2026.
Gap filling in Plots A and C is scheduled for the first two weekends of June 2027.
The dry-season check, which records water stress and fire damage, will take place on 15 March
2027. The full second-year count is planned for September 2027.

Night Base-Load Walk-Down: Step-by-Step Guide
for Tenant Floor Wardens
Nightwatt Energy Survey Co., Ltd., for the Building Management Office of Phet Pailin Tower, Khon Kaen · Ref.
NES-KK-26-031, version 2 · Issued 19 October 2026
Phet Pailin Tower is an 18-storey office building on Mittraphap Road, Khon Kaen. As part of its 2026
energy audit, the Building Management Office has engaged Nightwatt Energy Survey Co., Ltd. to
measure the building's night-time base load: the electricity that the tower keeps using when almost
nobody is inside.
This guide is for the floor warden that each tenant has named for the audit. Version 2 replaces version 1
of 2 October 2026; the survey date has moved from Thursday 5 November to Thursday 12 November
2026 because of the Loy Krathong holiday arrangements.
1. Key facts about the survey night
Survey night: Thursday 12 November 2026, from 20:00 to 04:00 on Friday 13 November.
Base-load window: 23:00 to 03:00. During these four hours the main meter and every floor sub-meter
are logged at one-minute intervals.
Survey control desk: Meeting Room 3.07 on Level 3, staffed all night by Nightwatt and the building
engineering team. Internal telephone extension 3307.
Survey team: four Nightwatt auditors led by Chanakan Wongsuriya, Lead Auditor. The building's
Chief Building Engineer, Pakorn Saengdao, joins them on the plant floors.
2. Before the survey night
1. Confirm your floor warden. Each tenant sends the name and mobile number of one floor warden
and one deputy to the Building Management Office (bmo@phetpailin.example) by Friday 30 October
2026.
2. Walk your floor during a normal working day. Use the Nightwatt Floor Checklist (form NES-F4) to
list every item that normally stays on overnight, including anything on a timer.
3. Tag critical equipment. Fix a red "DO NOT SWITCH OFF" tag to any item that must keep running.
4. Return the checklist. Email the completed form NES-F4 to the Building Management Office by
Monday 9 November 2026 at 17:00. Floors whose checklist arrives late are still surveyed, but they do
not receive a tenant floor report (see Section 5).
5. Register any late workers. Staff who must stay on a floor after 21:00 on 12 November are
registered with the Building Management Office by Thursday 5 November 2026, giving names and
expected leaving time. Each tenant may register up to 4 people.
3. During the survey night
Your warden or deputy must be reachable by mobile telephone from 20:00 to 01:00, and one of you must
meet the Nightwatt auditors at your floor's lift lobby at the time given in the visit schedule. The schedule
is emailed to wardens on Tuesday 10 November.

3.1 What the auditors do on your floor
Walk the floor with the warden and compare what is running with the checklist.
Fit plug-in meters to selected equipment. Each tenant floor gets up to 6 plug-in meters free of
charge; they stay in place until 08:00 on Friday 13 November.
Measure untagged items and, where useful, run a short switch-off test of up to 15 minutes on lighting
circuits, water heaters or idle equipment to see how much the floor load falls.
3.2 Who decides what may be switched off
The floor warden points out equipment and answers questions, but does not operate building plant. Only
the Lead Auditor, Chanakan Wongsuriya, may approve a switch-off test on a tenant circuit, and she does
so only after the warden has agreed on behalf of the tenant. Base-building plant (air handling units,
chilled water pumps, ventilation fans and lifts) is switched only by Pakorn Saengdao or a building
engineer he names on the night. Tenants must never switch base-building plant themselves.
Equipment that is never switched off. Anything with a red tag, all server and network equipment,
refrigerators and freezers, fire and security systems and medical devices are measured with clamp
meters or plug-in meters only. They are not part of any switch-off test, even if the tenant offers to
allow it.
3.3 Staff working late
Registered late workers may stay on their floor until 23:00. From 23:00 to 03:00 floors must be empty so
that the base load is clean; the only exception is building security and the survey team. Anyone not
registered by 5 November is asked to leave the floor by 21:00.
4. After the survey night
1. Do not move or unplug the plug-in meters. A Nightwatt auditor collects them between 08:00 and
09:30 on Friday 13 November.
2. Report any equipment that failed to restart, or any item found switched off in the morning, to the
control desk before 10:00 on 13 November.
5. Tenant floor reports and extra meters
Each tenant whose checklist arrived on time receives a two-page floor report by Friday 11 December
2026. It shows the floor's night load and the top five overnight consumers.
Tenants who want more than the 6 free plug-in meters may request extra meters on form NES-F4, in the
"extra meters" box. Extra meters cost 350 baht each for the survey night and are invoiced to the tenant
by the Building Management Office in December. In the 2024 survey the fee was 250 baht per meter, and
only 4 meters per floor were free. Requests for extra meters after 9 November cannot be met.

Notice to All Airside Pass Holders: Replacement of
Laminated Passes with GateKey Smart Passes
Sirilom Airports Company Limited · Mukdahan Regional Airport · Circular AVSEC-CIR-2026-07 · Issued 1
October 2026
To: All holders of a Mukdahan Regional Airport identification pass, and the pass sponsors of every
employer operating at the airport.
From: Somkiat Laorattana, Head of Aviation Security, Sirilom Airports Company Limited
Subject: Mandatory re-issue of all identification passes between November 2026 and January 2027
1. Why passes are being replaced
Since the terminal opened in 2019, Mukdahan Regional Airport has used laminated photo passes in three
colours (green, blue and yellow). These passes cannot be cancelled remotely when lost. The airport is
therefore moving to the GateKey airside pass system, in which every pass carries a contactless chip
checked at each staff security door and vehicle gate.
About 1,340 people currently hold a laminated pass. Every one of them must attend a short re-issue
appointment in person; there is no automatic conversion and no postal option.
Laminated passes remain valid until 31 January 2027 at 23:59. From 1 February 2027 a laminated pass
will not be accepted at any staff checkpoint, and a holder without a GateKey pass will be refused entry
even if he or she is on duty.
2. Re-issue waves
To keep queues short, holders are called in three waves according to their employer.
Wave A – Sirilom Airports staff, including Aviation Security, Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting, and the
Maintenance Department: Monday 2 November to Friday 20 November 2026.
Wave B – airlines, ground handling companies and the airport's two cargo agents: Monday 23
November to Friday 18 December 2026.
Wave C – concessionaires (shops, cafés and the currency exchange counter), the fuel farm operator,
and cleaning, catering and building contractors: Monday 4 January to Friday 22 January 2027.
Appointments take place at the Pass Office, Room G-14 on the ground floor of the Administration
Building, next to the staff car park entrance. The Pass Office is open for re-issue appointments Monday
to Friday from 08:30 to 15:30, closed for lunch from 12:00 to 13:00. Two extra Saturday sessions, from
09:00 to 12:00, will be held on 5 December 2026 for Wave B and on 16 January 2027 for Wave C. Walk-
in visits are not served.
Note. The former Pass Office counter in the landside arrivals hall (Room T-03) closed permanently on
30 September 2026.

3. What the pass sponsor must do before the appointment
Before a holder can be booked, the employer's pass sponsor must complete the following steps in the
GateKey sponsor portal:
1. Submit a re-issue request for the holder at least 10 working days before the chosen appointment
date. Requests submitted later can only be booked in the last three days of the wave, if places
remain.
2. Upload a criminal background check certificate issued no more than 6 months before the
appointment date. Until this circular, certificates up to 12 months old were accepted; the 12-month
rule no longer applies to any request.
3. Confirm that the holder has completed the online module "AVSEC Basic 2026" within the last 90
days.
4. Select the zones the holder needs for his or her actual duties (see section 5).
The Pass Office checks each request within 3 working days and returns incomplete requests to the
sponsor with the reason shown.
4. At the appointment
The holder must bring his or her Thai national identity card or, for foreign staff, a passport with a valid
work permit, together with the old laminated pass, which is surrendered and cut at the desk. The
appointment takes about 20 minutes, and the pass is printed and activated while the holder waits.
A holder who cannot show the old pass is treated as having lost it (see section 8).
5. New zone system
GateKey passes do not use colours; the zone numbers a holder may enter are printed in large figures on
the front of the pass and stored on the chip:
Zone 1: apron, aircraft stands and airside roads.
Zone 2: baggage make-up hall and the hold-baggage screening room.
Zone 3: departure sterile area after passenger screening, including the gate lounges.
Zone 4: terminal back offices, plant rooms and the landside service corridor.
Zones are granted according to the duties stated by the sponsor, not according to the colour of the old
pass. Any zone that a holder has not used for 90 consecutive days is removed automatically from the
chip, and the sponsor must request it again if it is still needed.
A GateKey holder with Zone 1 access may escort visitors who hold a daily visitor pass, up to a maximum
of 2 visitors at the same time. Holders whose pass was issued less than 3 months earlier may not act as
escorts.
6. Missing your wave
A holder who is not re-issued during his or her own wave may still be booked later, but a late re-issue
surcharge applies (see section 7). The surcharge is waived in only two cases:

the holder joined the employer after the wave had closed, as shown by the employment start date in
the sponsor portal; or
the sponsor uploads a leave record showing that the holder was absent for at least 15 consecutive
calendar days falling within the dates of the wave, for example maternity leave, long sick leave or an
overseas training course.
Shorter absences, including ordinary annual leave, do not qualify for the waiver. Holders who return from
long leave after 31 January 2027 cannot use their laminated pass at all and must be booked as soon as
they return; until then they may only enter airside areas under escort with a visitor pass.
7. Fees
The following fees apply to all GateKey passes issued from 2 November 2026. They are billed to the
employer, not to the individual holder, on the monthly airport services invoice.
Standard GateKey pass for employees of airlines, ground handlers, cargo agents, concessionaires
and the fuel farm operator: 350 baht per pass, valid for 3 years.
Sirilom Airports staff: no charge.
Contractor pass, valid for the length of the contract up to a maximum of 6 months: 500 baht per
pass.
Late re-issue surcharge, for a holder re-issued after his or her own wave has closed without a waiver:
200 baht per pass, in addition to the pass fee.
Daily visitor pass: 50 baht per visitor per day, with a limit of 5 visitor days per person in any calendar
year.
8. Lost, stolen and damaged passes
A lost or stolen GateKey pass must be reported to the Aviation Security Control Room immediately, on
internal extension 2299. The sponsor must then file a written loss report in the portal within 24 hours.
Replacement after a first loss: 1,000 baht. Until 30 September 2026 the fee for a lost laminated pass
was 600 baht; the higher fee applies to every loss reported from 1 October 2026, including losses of
old laminated passes.
Replacement after a second loss by the same holder within 24 months: 2,500 baht, and the case is
referred to the Head of Aviation Security, who may suspend the holder's airside access for up to 30
days.
Damaged pass, where the damaged pass is handed back: 150 baht.
9. Scope and contacts
The GateKey pass does not replace the staff car park sticker, which remains under the Facilities
Department and will be dealt with in a separate notice. Questions about bookings, sponsor requests and
fees should be sent to the Pass Office Manager, Pornthip Khunthaisong, on internal extension 2214.
Questions about zone decisions, escort rules and suspensions should be addressed to the Head of
Aviation Security, Somkiat Laorattana, on extension 2201. Sponsors are asked to pass this notice on to
all their pass holders by 15 October 2026.

Inspection Summary – HiveRunner H3 Floor
Markers after Floor Recoating
Phrom Daen Fulfilment Co., Ltd., Distribution Centre DC-2, Bang Phli, Samut Prakan · Ref. PDF-RB-2026-11 ·
Issued 24 September 2026
1. Background
The 46 HiveRunner H3 robots in Zone B (aisles B01–B28) find their position by reading square code
markers glued to the floor every 1.2 metres. On the nights of 6 and 7 September 2026 the contractor
recoated the Zone B floor with a new epoxy sealer. In the following week the robots logged 312 "marker
not found" stops, compared with an average of 19 per week in August. This inspection, led by Robotics
Maintenance Lead Thipwan Kesorn, checked every marker in Zone B on 15 and 16 September 2026.
2. Findings
Markers checked: 4,860 in total.
Grade C (unreadable or lifting): 214 markers, of which 171 lie in the charging lanes in aisles B25–
B28, where the sealer was applied twice.
Grade B (readable but glossy): 602 markers. Robots read them at the normal speed of 1.5 m/s, but
not reliably at the old top speed of 2.0 m/s.
Grade A (as new): all remaining markers.
No collision or injury was linked to the stops, but each stop blocked an aisle for about 4 minutes until a
technician reset the robot.
3. Actions
All Grade C markers will be replaced by 3 October 2026, starting with the charging lanes. Grade B
markers stay in place and will be checked again at the monthly inspection. The Zone B speed limit,
temporarily lowered to 1.0 m/s on 9 September, returns to 1.5 m/s once the charging lanes are finished.
Any future floor treatment in a robot zone must be approved in writing by the Site Safety Officer, Kittikorn
Chaiyawong, at least 10 working days in advance.
4. Replacing a marker
1. Put the aisle in "maintenance" mode on the fleet console, so robots route around it.
2. Scrape off the old marker and clean the spot with the approved solvent; let it dry for 15 minutes.
3. Glue the new marker using the alignment template, with the arrow pointing to the aisle's even-
numbered end.
4. Scan the marker with the handheld reader and enter its code in the console before releasing the aisle.
Note. Zone A was not recoated and is not affected. Its recoating, planned for November 2026, is on
hold until a matte sealer is proposed.

1. SCOPE AND BUYERS
These terms cover ex-works sales from our Kaase plant of coarse cocoa bean shell (grade CS-1) and

Wet product is charged on a moisture-corrected weight:
Wc = Wn × 100 − M100 − Mref (1)
where Wc is the chargeable weight (t, to 0.001 t), Wn the net weighbridge weight (t), M the measured
moisture (% wet basis) and Mref = 8.0 %. If M is 8.0 % or lower, Wc = Wn (no premium for dry
product).
A = Wc × p × ( 1 − d ) + H (2)
where A is the invoice amount before VAT (GHS), p the base price per tonne, d the volume discount
(0 below 40 t, 0.05 from 40 t, 0.08 from 100 t collected in the calendar month, current load
included) and H = GHS 85.00 per vehicle loaded by our front loader (nil if the buyer hand-loads
bagged product).
Worked example. A mushroom grower collects 12.40 t net of CS-1 at 11.5 % moisture, its collections
that month reach 46 t, and we load the truck. Wc = 12.40 × 88.5 / 92.0 = 11.928 t, so A = 11.928 ×

Lumbre HB-320 Olive-Stone Boiler and Malaxer Hot-Water Loop:
Commissioning Report
Almazara Torrebermeja S.C.A., Jaén · Maintenance and Energy Office · CR-CAL-2026-03 rev. 1 · Issued 21 October 2026 ·
Supersedes the draft rev. 0 of 17 October 2026
1. SCOPE AND INSTALLATION
This report records the cold and hot commissioning of the new olive-stone biomass boiler at the Almazara
Torrebermeja S.C.A. mill, Carretera JA-3200 km 4, 23009 Jaén. The boiler is a Lumbre HB-320 (nominal output 320
kW, serial number HB320-26-0418 ) supplied and installed by Calderas Guadalbullón S.L. of Mengíbar under order
PED-2026-117 . It replaces the 250 kW diesel boiler used up to and including the 2025/26 campaign, which burned
on average 31,400 litres of heating oil per season.
The boiler heats a closed water loop that serves the six malaxers of Lines 1 and 2 (three per line, in the ground-floor
process hall), the washer make-up water heater and the decanter dilution water tank. It burns the cooperative's own
olive stone, separated from the pomace by the pitting unit in Building C and stored in the 18 t steel silo SIL-04
(usable capacity 16.5 t). The loop design temperatures are 80 °C flow and 60 °C return.
Cold commissioning (pressure test, interlocks, dry runs of the stone auger): 6 to 8 October 2026.
Hot commissioning (first firing, efficiency, emissions and malaxer tests): 13 to 16 October 2026.
Hydrostatic test: 6.0 bar for 2 h on 6 October, no drop; safety valve PSV-12  set at 4.0 bar.
Witnesses: Inmaculada Cobo Martos (commissioning engineer, Calderas Guadalbullón S.L.), Rafael Expósito
Liébana (technical manager, Almazara Torrebermeja) and Francisco Jesús Moral Higueras (head miller, maestro de
almazara).
2. MALAXER HEAT DEMAND

malaxation set point. The cooperative markets all Line 2 oil as cold extracted, so the paste must never exceed 27 °C;
the standing set point for both lines is 26 °C. The heat demand of one line is estimated with equation (1).

Hw = H0 · ( 1 − w ) − 0.678 · w (2)

Seasonal Weighing and Moisture Monitoring of the Heritage
Wooden Fleet: A Field Method
Harriet Ashdown-Vere and Owen Catchpole
Boat Care Committee, Aston Ferry Rowing Club, Aston Lane, Remenham, Henley-on-Thames RG9 3DH, United Kingdom
Method note AFRC-MN-07, version 2.1 · approved by the Club Committee on 14 September 2026 · replaces version 1.4
(March 2022)
ABSTRACT. Aston Ferry Rowing Club keeps nine wooden boats built between 1958 and 1994 for exhibition
races and heritage events. Water uptake in the hull timber is the earliest measurable sign of failing varnish and
of the soft rot that ended the life of the club's 1952 eight in 2019. This note sets out how the fleet is weighed
with two suspended load cells, how results are compared with each boat's reference dry mass, how pin
moisture readings are corrected for timber species, and who acts on the Amber and Red levels.
1. Purpose and scope
The method applies to the nine boats in Table 1, stored in Bay 3 of the boathouse on the Berkshire bank
opposite Temple Island. It does not apply to the club's 31 composite boats or to the launches, which have their
own survey (AFRC-MN-03).
Each boat is weighed four times a year: in the first fortnight of March, in the week after Henley Royal
Regatta, in mid-September and in the first week of December. A boat lent to an outside event (for example a
film shoot at Hambleden) is also weighed within 10 days of its return. A reading taken outside the conditions in
Section 3 is recorded as “non-standard” and never used for an Amber or Red decision.
2. Equipment and calibration
Version 1.4 of this note used two platform scales under the canvas, which gave a spread of up to 1.8 kg on
repeat weighings of the same eight. From the September 2026 weighing onward the boat is lifted clear of the
trestles in two 75 mm webbing slings, each hanging from a Kestrelscale KS-300 crane load cell (0–300 kg,
resolution 0.05 kg; club assets BC-114 bow and BC-115 stern) on the Bay 3 gantry. The total mass is the sum of
the two readings minus the tare of the slings and shackles, which was measured on 2 September 2026 as 1.35
kg for the pair and must be remeasured whenever a sling or shackle is replaced.
Before every session each cell is zeroed with its sling hanging and the 20 kg cast-iron check mass (BC-117)
is hung on it. If either cell reads outside 19.90–20.10 kg the session is postponed and the Boatman is told the
same day; members never adjust the cells.
3. Conditions for a standard weighing
A hull weighed straight after an outing reads heavy because of surface water, so a weighing counts as standard
only if all of the following apply:
the boat has not been on the water for at least 72 hours and has been stored upside down on its rack in Bay
3 for that whole period (version 1.4 required 48 hours);
the bilge has been sponged out and the boat has been tipped on its side for 5 minutes to drain the canvas
and buoyancy spaces;
relative humidity in Bay 3 is 75 % or less and air temperature is between 8 °C and 24 °C, read from the
Bay 3 thermo-hygrometer at the start;
seats, stretchers, riggers and the cox box are removed and the boat is weighed bare; fixed fittings such as
the rudder, fin and saxboard brass stay on.
If Bay 3 is too humid, single and double sculls only may be weighed in the gym loft, hanging from the loft
beam with the same cells.
PAGE 1 OF 3 ASTON FERRY ROWING CLUB · HERITAGE FLEET WEIGHING METHOD · AFRC-MN-07 V2.1

4. Reference dry mass and action levels
Each boat's reference dry mass is the mean of the standard weighings of March and September 2023, after the
fleet had been dried for six weeks by Rushbrook Wooden Boat Conservation at Wargrave. For carvel and
moulded hulls the Amber level is a gain of 2.5 % and the Red level a gain of 5.0 %; for the single sculls, whose
small mass makes the result more sensitive to fittings, the levels are 3.0 % and 6.0 %. Clinker hulls take up
water through their laps by design, so for the two tubs the levels are 4.0 % and 7.0 %. In version 1.4 every boat
used 3.0 % and 6.0 %. Table 1 gives the resulting masses in kilograms, rounded to 0.1 kg; the table values are
the ones to apply.

4.1 What happens at each level
A result below the Amber level needs no action beyond recording. At or above the Amber level the boat stays in
use, but the Boat Care Committee chair must be told within 7 days, the varnish is inspected for cracks, and the
boat is weighed again after a further 14 days dry in Bay 3. Two Amber results in a row are treated as Red.
At or above the Red level the boat is withdrawn from all rowing at once: the weighing member hangs a red
tag on the bow ball and locks the boat on its rack, and the Captain of Boats is informed the same day. Only the
Captain of Boats may release the boat again, and only after Rushbrook Wooden Boat Conservation has
surveyed the hull and a standard weighing below the Amber level has been recorded. A boat lent to an outside
event while carrying a Red tag is not covered by the club's insurance.
A result is never corrected for new fittings. If a fitting has been added or replaced, the Boat Care Committee asks the Club
Committee to revise the boat's reference in Table 1; until the revision is approved the old reference applies.
5. Procedure
Two members who have completed the half-day weighing course carry out each session; one must sit on the
Boat Care Committee.
1. Record the date, RH, temperature and hours since the last outing, and do the check-mass test (Section 2).
2. Set the slings at the positions in Table 2, measured from the bow ball along the gunwale, with the spreader
board inside the hull at each sling.
3. Lift the boat with the gantry chain hoists until it is 50 mm clear of the trestles, level it to within 20 mm end
to end, and wait 60 seconds for the readings to settle.
4. Note both readings, lower, and lift twice more. The result is the mean of the three totals; if they differ by
more than 0.30 kg, find the cause and repeat.
5. Take pin moisture readings at the six stations in Section 6.

Pin moisture readings are taken at six fixed stations: the keel at bow and stern canvas, and both garboards at the

7. Recording, review and responsibilities
The Boatman, currently Dennis Okafor-Hale, keeps the equipment, books Bay 3 and the gantry for each
session, and arranges external verification of the check mass. Owen Catchpole, as Boat Care Committee chair,
reviews every Amber result and signs off the quarterly summary for the Club Committee. Harriet Ashdown-

loan of a heritage boat for an outside event.

Thawing Frozen Sawlogs Before Debarking: An Energy and
Residence-Time Model for the Kuusikkoniemi Hot-Water Pond
Aino Rautiainen, Joonas Kylmälä and Henrik Lehtovaara
Napapiiri Institute of Wood Technology, Rovaniemi, Finland, and Kuusikkoniemi Saha Oy, Rovaniemi, Finland
Working paper NIWT-WP 2026/11 · LAUHA winter thaw pond project · 22 September 2026
ABSTRACT. Frozen bark adheres strongly to the stem, so ring debarkers leave bark residue on winter logs and
the chips sold to pulp mills fail their bark limit. In the LAUHA winter thaw pond project, Kuusikkoniemi Saha
Oy and the Napapiiri Institute of Wood Technology built and tested a two-basin hot-water pond in front of
debarking line DB-2 during the winter of 2025–26. This working paper presents four simple equations,
calibrated on the trial data, for the thawing energy per cubic metre of log, the residence time in the pond, the
daily pond capacity and the heat demand placed on the sawmill's bark-fired boiler. It closes with the operating
rules proposed for the winter of 2026–27. The figures are planning values for this site only.
1. Introduction
Kuusikkoniemi Saha Oy operates a sawmill on the west bank of the Kemijoki, 14 km south of Rovaniemi town
centre. The mill saws about 214,000 m3 (solid, under bark) of sawlogs per year, of which 68 % is Scots pine
and 32 % Norway spruce, bought mainly from private forests around Ranua, Kemijärvi and Sodankylä. Logs
arrive by truck and are stored in the open log yard for 2 to 20 days before sawing. Between November and
March their core temperature commonly falls below −20 °C, and in January 2026 the coldest batch logged by
the trial reached −34 °C.
The mill has two debarking lines. Line DB-1 handles small logs with a top diameter below 15 cm, which are
sold whole as pulpwood or chipped. Line DB-2, a single-rotor ring debarker with a normal feed speed of 70
m/min, prepares all sawlogs for the main saw line. In earlier winters the mill slowed DB-2 to between 35 and
40 m/min whenever the yard temperature was below −15 °C, and still measured an average bark residue of 4.6
% (by area) on debarked pine. The pulp mill that buys the sawmill chips accepts at most 1.0 % bark by dry
mass and deducts EUR 3.20 per tonne of chips for each 0.5 percentage point above the limit.
The LAUHA project (budget EUR 1.86 million, of which 40 % came from the Kemijoki Valley Industry
Fund and the rest from the company) built a hot-water pond with two parallel concrete basins, A and B,
between the log sorting deck and DB-2. The pond was commissioned on 14 October 2025 and the trial ran from
1 December 2025 to 15 March 2026. During that period 3,912 log batches were followed with core temperature
probes, and the bark residue after DB-2 was measured on a sample of 25 logs per shift.
2. Thawing energy per cubic metre of log
To debark cleanly, the cambium layer under the bark must be thawed; in practice the mill aims to bring the
outer 5 cm of the stem to about +5 °C. The model treats the log as a uniform body and adds three terms:
warming the frozen wood to 0 °C, melting the freezable water and warming the thawed wood to the target
temperature. Per cubic metre of solid log, the heat required is
E =
ρ × [cf × ( 0 − Tlog ) + ( u − ufs ) × L + cu × Tt ]
3600
(1)
where E is the thawing energy (kWh per m3 of solid log), ρ the basic density (kg of dry wood per m3 of green
log), cf and cu the specific heat of the frozen and unfrozen wet wood (kJ per kg of dry wood per K), Tlog the core
temperature of the log on arrival at the pond (°C), u the moisture content (kg of water per kg of dry wood), ufs
the fibre saturation point, taken as 0.30 (water below this level does not freeze), L the latent heat of fusion of ice,
334 kJ/kg, and Tt the target temperature, +5 °C. The divisor 3600 converts kJ to kWh.

The parameter values measured on Kuusikkoniemi logs in the trial are, for Scots pine: ρ = 410 kg/m3, u = 0.95,
cf = 3.2 and cu = 5.2; and for Norway spruce: ρ = 380 kg/m3, u = 0.85, cf = 3.0 and cu = 4.8. Pine has the higher
moisture content because of its wide, wet sapwood, so it needs more energy per cubic metre than spruce at the
same temperature.
Example 1 (pine at −25 °C). For a pine batch with Tlog = −25 °C, formula (1) gives E = 410 × [3.2 × 25 +
(0.95 − 0.30) × 334 + 5.2 × 5] / 3600 = 410 × (80 + 217.1 + 26) / 3600 = 36.8 kWh/m3. Spruce at the same
temperature needs 29.8 kWh/m3.
3. Residence time in the pond
The time a log must stay in the water depends mainly on its diameter and on the water temperature. The trial
data were fitted to the empirical form
t = κ × a × d2
Tw
(2)
where t is the minimum residence time (hours), κ a cold-log correction factor, equal to 1.00 when the log core
temperature is −20 °C or warmer and 1.25 when it is colder than −20 °C, a the species coefficient (h·°C/cm2), d
the mid diameter of the log over bark (cm) and Tw the pond water temperature (°C).
The fitted species coefficients are a = 0.95 for Scots pine and a = 0.80 for Norway spruce, with a residual
standard error of 1.1 hours over 3,912 batches. The first draft of this paper (NIWT-WP 2026/04, April 2026)
used a = 1.10 for pine, a value taken from laboratory tests on short billets; that value overstated the residence
time by about 15 % and is withdrawn. For mixed batches, the operators use the pine coefficient and the largest
mid diameter in the batch.
Example 2 (pine, coldest week). A pine batch with a largest mid diameter of 22 cm and a core temperature
of −25 °C enters basin A at Tw = 40 °C. Because the logs are colder than −20 °C, κ = 1.25, and t = 1.25 ×
0.95 × 222 / 40 = 14.4 hours. The same batch at −15 °C (κ = 1.00) would need 11.5 hours.
4. Daily pond capacity and heat demand
Each basin holds log baskets with a gross volume of 420 m3, so the pond has a total gross volume Vp = 840 m3.
Logs fill only part of a basket; the trial measured a solid-volume fraction of 0.55. The volume of logs that the
pond can thaw per day is
Vday =
φ × Vp × 24

(3)
where Vday is the daily pond capacity (m3 of solid log per day), φ the solid-volume fraction of a loaded basket
(0.55), Vp the gross basket volume of the basins in use (m3; 840 with both basins, 420 with one) and t the
residence time from formula (2) (hours).
The pond water is heated through a plate heat exchanger connected to the sawmill's 6.0 MW bark-fired boiler,
which also supplies the drying kilns. The average heating power drawn by the pond is

Example 3 (both basins, coldest week). With t = 14.4 hours from Example 2 (unrounded 14.37 h), formula
(3) gives Vday = 0.55 × 840 × 24 / 14.37 ≈ 772 m3 per day. With E = 36.8 kWh/m3 from Example 1, formula

is 39.3 MWh of heat; at the internal heat transfer price of EUR 24 per MWh used in the LAUHA budget, the
pond costs about EUR 943 per day in this week.
The DB-2 saw line consumes about 820 m3 of sawlogs per day on the two-shift winter schedule. In the
coldest weeks the pond is therefore slightly short of capacity when only pine is ponded, and the gap is covered
from the 1,500 m3 buffer of already debarked logs kept in the covered log hall.
5. Proposed operating rules for winter 2026–27
The following rules are proposed for the pond from 1 November 2026. They were agreed with Kuusikkoniemi
Saha Oy on 15 September 2026.
1. Which logs are ponded. Pine sawlogs with a core temperature below −4 °C and spruce sawlogs below −8
°C must pass through the pond before DB-2. Spruce sawlogs between −8 °C and −4 °C may go straight to
DB-2 if its feed speed is reduced to 45 m/min for the batch. Logs with a top diameter below 15 cm always
go to DB-1 and are never ponded, whatever their temperature.
2. Water temperature. Pine destined for the export joinery grades may be ponded at no more than 42 °C,
because warmer water caused a grey-brown discolouration of the sapwood in the trial; other pine may be
ponded at up to 45 °C and spruce at up to 48 °C. During the trial the basins were run at up to 50 °C for all
logs until 9 January 2026, when the discolouration was found. Mixed batches follow the lowest limit that
applies.
3. Temperature measurement. The core temperature of every incoming batch is measured with a probe at
10 cm depth on three logs, and the coldest reading counts. Batches stored for more than 24 hours in the
heated log hall are exempt from measurement and are treated as −4 °C.
4. Single-basin operation. When one basin is drained for cleaning (planned every 6 weeks, normally on a
Sunday), Vp = 420 m3 in formula (3), and the pond operator must inform the saw line foreman before the
start of the shift so that the debarked-log buffer can be used.
Responsibilities. The pond operator on each shift sets the residence time with formula (2) and records it in the pond log.
The water temperature limits in rule 2 are set and changed only by the production manager (Henrik Lehtovaara). Questions
on the model go to Dr Aino Rautiainen at the Napapiiri Institute of Wood Technology.
6. Results of the trial and limitations
With the pond in use, the average bark residue on debarked pine fell from 4.6 % to 0.8 % by area, and the bark
content of the chips sold to the pulp mill averaged 0.7 % by dry mass, so no price deductions were made after
20 December 2025. DB-2 ran at its normal 70 m/min for 91 % of the trial shifts.
The model has two main limitations. First, formula (1) ignores the heat taken up by snow and ice on the logs,
which added up to 2 kWh/m3 after heavy snowfall. Second, the coefficients in formula (2) were fitted to logs
with mid diameters of 14 to 38 cm and should not be used outside that range.

MEDIA RELEASE · REF. WSW-MR-2026/14 · ROCKINGHAM WA, 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 · FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Peron Point desalination plant to cut output for 23 days
while divers replace worn brine diffuser nozzles
Warnbro Sound Water Company Pty Ltd · Lot 12 Point Peron Road, Rockingham WA 6168 · Media and Community Relations
From 2 to 24 November 2026 the Peron Point Seawater Desalination Plant will produce 70 to 105
megalitres a day instead of its usual 140, so that 36 of the 48 nozzles on its offshore brine diffuser can
be replaced under the Peron Point Diffuser Renewal Project.
What is happening
Warnbro Sound Water Company Pty Ltd (WSWC),
owner and operator of the Peron Point plant, today
confirmed the dates and budget of the Peron Point
Diffuser Renewal Project. The works will cost AUD 11.8
million, up from the AUD 9.4 million estimate given to
the Rockingham community reference group in May
2026, mainly because a third diving vessel has been
added to shorten the period of low output. Garnet Bay
Diving Services of Mandurah will cut off each worn
duckbill nozzle and clamp a new one onto the existing
riser. The other 12 nozzles, replaced in 2022 after storm
damage, stay in place.
"Customers will not notice any change at the tap. We
have filled our storage ahead of the works," said
WSWC Managing Director Bronwyn Tregenza.
Why now: the 2026 seabed survey
The plant's Marine Environmental Management Plan
(MEMP) requires an independent survey of bottom
water and seagrass around the outfall every winter.
Shoalwater Benthic Consulting surveyed the outfall
between 11 and 22 August 2026. Two sites close to the
diffuser, PP-02 and PP-03, recorded dissolved oxygen
below the MEMP trigger. Divers found many nozzles
stiff and partly blocked by tubeworms, so the brine left
them as slow, heavy jets that mixed poorly with
seawater.

PRESS RELEASE · FOR IMMEDIATE USE · 22 SEPTEMBER 2026
Kasa 92.1 FM climbs McCarthy Hill: new mast, solar
backup and a signal that reaches Kasoa
Ablekuma Kasa Community Radio (AKCR) · Dansoman, Accra · Ref. AKCR/PR/2026-07 · Background facts and engineering
notes for editors attached
Ablekuma Kasa Community Radio will move its 92.1 MHz transmitter from the rooftop in Dansoman to a
45-metre mast on McCarthy Hill, Weija, on Monday 19 October 2026 at 06:00, and will keep
broadcasting through power cuts on a new solar-charged battery bank.
The announcement
For seventeen years Kasa 92.1 FM has broadcast from
a 30-metre steel mast bolted to the roof of the old
Dansoman community library. Beyond the Densu River
the signal fades, and every major power cut has taken
the station off air within minutes. "Our listeners in
Kasoa and Bortianor kept phoning to say they lost us
halfway through the morning market prices," said
station manager Naa Adjeley Quaye-Mensah. "From
19 October they should not have to."
The new site is a fenced plot leased from the McCarthy
Hill Residents' Welfare Committee for 15 years at GHS
9,600 a year. It holds a new 1,000-watt transmitter, a
four-bay dipole antenna, a 12 kWp solar array on the
equipment-shelter roof and a 48-volt lithium battery
bank. The equipment was supplied and installed by
Tetteh-Bruce Broadcast Services Ltd of Tema under
contract TBB/AK/0417.
Test nights before the switch
Engineers will run test transmissions from McCarthy Hill
on the nights of 5 to 15 October 2026, Monday to
Thursday only, between 00:30 and 04:30. During those
hours listeners may hear tone, a looped station
identification or short silences. Normal programmes
continue from Dansoman outside the test hours. The
Dansoman rooftop transmitter stays in place as a
standby until 30 November 2026 and will then be
dismantled.
What listeners need to do
Nothing, for most people: the frequency stays at 92.1
MHz and no retuning is needed. Car radios with a
stored preset and phones with an FM receiver will pick
up the new signal automatically. Listeners in tall
buildings in Dansoman may find a west-facing window
gives better indoor reception.
Engineering notes for editors
Chief engineer Kofi Ankrah-Lamptey has supplied the three planning formulas the station uses. The figures
quoted in this release were calculated with them.
PERP = 10 log10 PTX + Gant − Lf − Lc (1)
where PERP is the effective radiated power in dBW, PTX the transmitter output in watts, Gant the antenna gain in dBd, Lf
the feeder cable loss in dB and Lc the loss in connectors and the filter in dB. To convert back to watts, ERP = 10P/10.
At McCarthy Hill the transmitter delivers 1,000 W into a four-bay antenna with a gain of 6.2 dBd. The 65 m of 7/8-
inch feeder loses 2.1 dB per 100 m, which rounds to 1.4 dB, and the filter and connectors lose 0.3 dB. Equation (1)
gives 30.0 + 6.2 − 1.4 − 0.3 = 34.5 dBW, about 2,820 W ERP. The station's community broadcasting
authorisation caps ERP at 3.0 kW (34.8 dBW), so the new site works just inside the limit. The Dansoman rooftop
delivered 300 W into a 3.0 dBd antenna with 0.9 dB of losses, or 26.9 dBW (about 490 W ERP).

where d is the radio horizon in kilometres, ht the height of the antenna centre above average surrounding terrain in
metres, hr the receiving antenna height in metres (1.5 m for a hand-held or car radio, 10 m for a rooftop aerial), and 4.12 a
constant that allows for normal bending of VHF waves in the atmosphere.
How far the signal reaches
The antenna centre on McCarthy Hill stands 112 m
above average terrain, against 38 m at Dansoman. For
a car radio (hr = 1.5 m), equation (2) gives 4.12 ×
(10.58 + 1.22) = 48.6 km from the hill, compared with
30.4 km from the old rooftop. The horizon is an upper
limit: buildings and hills shorten it, so the station plans
its service on a smaller primary service area with a
radius of 35 km. It takes in Kasoa, Bortianor, Weija,
Amasaman and the Kaneshie market; beyond it, in
places such as Nsawam, reception is not guaranteed.
Staying on air when the power goes
Until now a diesel generator took up to four minutes to
start after a power cut. At McCarthy Hill the transmitter,
studio-to-transmitter link and exciter run from the
battery bank whenever grid power fails, and the solar
array recharges it during the day. The generator moves
to the hill as a last reserve and starts only when the
battery falls to 30 % of capacity.

power cut lasts longer than three hours, the duty
engineer switches the transmitter to reduced-power
mode (500 W output), in which the whole site draws
1,150 W.
Reporting reception after the move
The engineering team collects reception reports from
19 October to 30 November 2026. To send one:
1. Tune to 92.1 MHz and score what you hear from 1
(nothing) to 5 (as clear as the studio).
2. Note your GhanaPost GPS digital address or the
nearest landmark, and whether you were indoors,
outdoors or in a vehicle.
3. Send an SMS or WhatsApp message to 024 921
0921 in the form SIGNAL score address time, for
example SIGNAL 2 GA-544-1290 07:15.
4. If you score 1 or 2 inside the 35 km primary service
area, a volunteer signal walker will call you back
within three working days to arrange a visit.
Reports sent during the October test nights are logged
but answered only after 19 October.
Paying for the move
The project cost GHS 512,400 in total. The Adaklu
Civic Media Fund gave a grant of GHS 300,000, the
Ablekuma Traders' Association contributed GHS
40,000 and GHS 100,050 came from the station's own
reserves. The remainder was raised by the Hold the
Signal listener drive, which ran from 1 June to 31
August 2026 and collected GHS 72,350 from 3,118
donors.

hours a day (05:00 to 24:00) in Ga, Twi, Ewe and English, with a Hausa hour on Fridays at 20:00.

Caves d'Affinage d'Épagny SC is a cooperative that ripens hard mountain cheese for its member dairies

producers who make cheese in mountain huts on the pastures around Moléson, Charmey and the
Vallée du Motélon and who have no cellar of their own that stays cool and humid enough for long
ripening. The Alpage Shelf Permit gives the holder the right to store a fixed number of wheels in the
cooperative's cellars for one season, with turning and rind care done by cellar staff.
The permit is issued and signed by Séverine Pasquier, Managing Director. Shelf allocation,

Affineur (cellar master). Hygiene, sampling and pest control are handled by Nadine Murith, Hygiene

Applicants must run a summer alpage dairy in the Canton of Fribourg or the Pays-d'Enhaut (Vaud) and
hold a valid dairy hygiene registration for the 2027 summer. Each applicant may hold one permit, for
between 6 and 60 wheels.

refused and must be taken back the same day.
4. SHELF BOARDS AND PERMIT FEE
Each spruce board holds two wheels side by side, and boards are allocated whole, so an odd number of
wheels takes up one half-empty board. The permit holder chooses one of the two cellars on form ASP-
A:
Cave Basse (lower cellar, 13 °C, 94 to 96 % relative humidity): wheels are turned and brushed
twice a week. Care charge CHF 2.60 per wheel per month.
Cave Haute (upper cellar, 15 °C, 90 to 92 % relative humidity): wheels are turned and brushed
once a week. Care charge CHF 1.90 per wheel per month.
The permit fee covers board rent and care for the whole stay and is set by equation (2).
F = F0 + M × (p × ⌈ n2 ⌉ + c × n) (2)
where F is the permit fee (CHF), F0 the application fee of CHF 120 (CHF 95 for the 2026 season), M the
number of months the wheels are in the cellar (any started calendar month counts as a full month), p
the board rent of CHF 4.20 per board per month (CHF 3.80 until 31 December 2026), n the number of
wheels on the permit, ⌈ n/2 ⌉  the number of boards (n divided by 2, rounded up), and c the care charge
for the chosen cellar.
Worked example: 15 wheels in Cave Basse for 7 months use ⌈ 15/2 ⌉  = 8 boards. F = 120 + 7 ×
(4.20 × 8 + 2.60 × 15) = 120 + 7 × (33.60 + 39.00) = 120 + 508.20 = CHF 628.20.
A deposit of 30 % of the estimated fee is due within 20 days of the allocation letter; the balance is
invoiced when the last wheel leaves the cellar and is payable within 30 days.
5. EXPECTED WEIGHT AT RELEASE
Wheels lose water during ripening. As a basis for the shortfall compensation in section 6, the expected
weight of each wheel at release is set by equation (3).
mt = m0 × ( 1 − λ ) t (3)
where mt is the expected weight at release (kg), m0 the fresh weight recorded at delivery (kg), t the
ripening time in the cellar in whole months, and λ the monthly weight-loss rate of the cellar: 0.0085 in
Cave Basse and 0.0120 in Cave Haute. Results are rounded to two decimals.
Worked example: a 32 kg wheel ripened for 8 months has an expected weight of 32 × (1 − 0.0085)8
= 29.89 kg in Cave Basse, but only 32 × (1 − 0.0120)8 = 29.05 kg in Cave Haute.
Page 2 of 3 Caves d'Affinage d'Épagny SC · Alpage Shelf Permit Guide 2027 · CAE-ASP-2027

6. SHORTFALL COMPENSATION
If wheels lose much more weight than expected, the cooperative pays compensation. A loss of up to 3
% below the expected weight is normal variation and is not compensated. Compensation for a batch of
wheels released on the same day is calculated with equation (4).
K = r × n × max ( 0, 0.97 × mt −  ̄m ) (4)
where K is the compensation (CHF), r the compensation rate of CHF 16.80 per kg, n the number of
wheels in the batch, mt the expected weight at release from equation (3) (kg), and m̄  the mean
measured weight of the wheels in the batch on the release scale (kg).
Worked example: 10 wheels of 32 kg ripened for 8 months in Cave Basse have mt = 29.89 kg, so the
threshold is 0.97 × 29.89 = 28.99 kg. If their mean release weight is 28.40 kg, K = 16.80 × 10 ×
(28.99 − 28.40) = 16.80 × 10 × 0.59 = CHF 99.12, credited against the balance invoice.
Exclusions. No compensation is paid for wheels with rind damage recorded at delivery, for wheels
collected late (section 8), or for wheels released at the producer's request before the minimum
ripening of 5 months. Claims must be made on form ASP-R on the release day; claims made later
are not considered.
7. HYGIENE, INSPECTIONS AND CHEESE MITES
Permit holders may visit their wheels on Wednesdays from 14:00 to 16:30, accompanied by a member
of the cellar staff.
The cooperative takes a rind and core sample from one wheel in every twenty (at least one per permit)
during the third month of ripening.
Cheese mites and mould. Any producer who notices cheese mites, a powdery brown dust on the
rind, or unusual mould on any wheel during a visit must report it on the same day to the Hygiene and
Quality Officer, Nadine Murith (direct line 026 912 47 36), and not to the cellar staff on duty. She
decides whether boards are cleaned, wheels are brushed or the affected rack is closed. Wheels on a
closed rack are not charged care fees for the months the rack is closed.
8. RELEASE AND COLLECTION
1. Book a release date at least 10 days in advance with the cellar office; releases take place on
Mondays and Thursdays from 07:00 to 11:00.
2. The cellar master checks that each wheel has ripened at least 5 months from its date of
manufacture and records its release weight on form ASP-R.
3. Pay any open invoices; wheels are not released while a previous invoice is more than 30 days
overdue.
Wheels still in the cellar after 31 May 2028 are charged a late storage fee of CHF 1.50 per wheel per
day.
9. BREACHES AND WITHDRAWAL
A written warning is given for a delivery outside delivery hours, an unannounced visit, or missing
paperwork for a batch. A second warning in the same season ends the permit, and all wheels must be
collected within 14 days, whatever their age. A producer who withdraws in writing before 15 June 2027
receives a refund of the deposit less the application fee; later withdrawals are not refunded.

Notice to Patients: Repeat Prescriptions Move to
PillPost Medicine Lockers
Chok Khao Community Health Clinic, Mueang Lamphun · Notice No. CKC-PN-2026/07 · Issued 5 October
2026
Dear patients and carers, from Monday 2 November 2026 most repeat prescriptions at Chok Khao
Community Health Clinic will be collected from the new PillPost medicine lockers instead of the
pharmacy counter. Please keep this notice with your blue medicine book.
1. What is changing
Until Saturday 31 October 2026, repeat prescriptions are collected at Pharmacy Window 3 from Monday
to Saturday, 08:00 to 16:00. From 2 November 2026, enrolled patients will instead collect from the
PillPost lockers at the east entrance of the clinic, next to the blood-pressure self-check kiosk. The
lockers can be opened every day from 06:00 to 22:00, including Sundays and public holidays.
The bank has 48 standard compartments and 8 refrigerated compartments kept between 2 and 8 °C for
insulin and other cold-chain medicines. Using the lockers is free of charge. Window 3 stays open for new
prescriptions and patients who are not eligible.
2. Who can use the lockers
You may enrol if you are a registered patient of the clinic, aged 18 or over, and you have a repeat
prescription for a long-term condition such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol,
asthma or an under-active thyroid. Your dose must have been unchanged for at least 6 months on the
date you enrol.
The following cannot be placed in a locker and must still be collected at Window 3:
controlled medicines, including strong pain medicines and sleeping tablets;
warfarin and other medicines that need a blood test result before each supply;
the first supply after any change of medicine or dose;
bulky items such as nebuliser machines, dressing packs or boxes heavier than 5 kg.
Insulin pens and other refrigerated medicines may be placed in a refrigerated compartment, but they
must be collected within 24 hours of the text message, not the 72 hours that apply to standard
compartments.
3. How to enrol
Enrolment opens on Monday 12 October 2026. Enrol at the Patient Liaison Desk in Room 104, Monday
to Friday 08:30 to 15:30, or by telephone on the clinic line 053 510 274, extension 2. To enrol you need
your Thai national ID card (or pink card for non-Thai residents), a mobile number that can receive text
messages, and a signed consent form PP-1.
Patients who enrol by Friday 23 October 2026 will receive their first locker supply in November. Later
enrolments move to the lockers from the next refill after confirmation.

4. Ordering and collecting your medicines
1. Order your refill at least 5 working days before your current supply runs out, by refill slip, phone or the
drop box at the east entrance.
2. A pharmacist checks and packs your medicines in a sealed, labelled bag.
3. You receive a text message with the locker number and a 6-digit collection code. The code is valid
for 72 hours from the time the message is sent.
4. At the locker screen, enter the 6-digit code followed by the last 4 digits of your ID card. The
compartment door opens for 30 seconds.
5. Check the label and the seal before you leave. If the seal is broken, leave the bag in the compartment
and contact the pharmacy (Section 7).
A lost code can be resent by calling extension 2, at most 2 times per order.
5. Uncollected medicines
When a code expires, the pharmacy removes the bag on the next working morning. You can still collect it
at Window 3 within 14 days; after 14 days the medicines are returned to stock and you must order again.
A patient who misses 2 locker collections within any 3-month period is moved back to counter collection
at Window 3 for 6 months, after which they may enrol again. Collections missed because of a locker fault
reported to the clinic do not count.
6. Collecting for someone else
Each patient may register one carer to collect on their behalf. The carer must be 18 or over, must come
to Room 104 with both ID cards, and must sign form PP-2 together with the patient. The carer receives a
separate code on their own mobile phone. One carer may be registered for at most 3 patients.
7. Medicine reviews and contacts
Using the lockers does not replace your medicine review. Every patient using PillPost must attend a
review with a pharmacist in Room 108 at least once every 6 months. If a review is more than 30 days
overdue, locker supplies are paused and your next refill is prepared for Window 3, where staff will book
your review.

responsible for everything placed in the lockers. Call extension 3 during clinic hours.
Enrolment, consent forms and carer registration: Ms Supaporn Inkaew, Patient Liaison Nurse,
Room 104, extension 2.
Locker screen or door faults: press the red help button on the locker bank; outside clinic hours the
call goes to the security office at the main gate.

writing at the reception desk.
