FitAgain Denture Repair and Reline Service: A
Guide for Denture Wearers
Prasan Yim Dental Clinic, Phitsanulok · Patient leaflet PYD-LF-2026-07, version 2 · Valid from 1 October 2026
1. About the service
The FitAgain Denture Repair and Reline Service lets most patients of Prasan Yim Dental Clinic have an
acrylic denture mended, adjusted or relined on the same day, without sending it away for a week. The
service has its own small dental laboratory on the 2nd floor of the clinic building at 77/3 Boromtrailokanat
Road, Mueang Phitsanulok, staffed by two dental technicians and supervised by our prosthodontist, Dr.
Wilaiwan Chanthawong.
FitAgain is open to all denture wearers, including people whose denture was made at another clinic.
Every denture is first checked by one of our dentists, because a denture that keeps breaking often no
longer fits the gums underneath.
The service covers full (complete) and partial dentures with a pink acrylic base. Partial dentures with a
metal framework can be repaired too, but the metal work is done by our partner laboratory in Bangkok
and takes 7 working days, so these repairs are never same-day.
2. Opening hours and same-day cut-off times
The FitAgain laboratory is open Monday to Saturday. It is closed on Sundays and on public holidays. To
have your denture back on the same day, you must hand it in at reception before the cut-off time:
Monday to Friday: laboratory open 08:30–18:00. Hand in by 11:00; the denture is ready for
collection from 16:30.
Saturday: laboratory open 08:30–15:00. Hand in by 09:30; the denture is ready for collection from
14:00.
Until 30 September 2026 the weekday cut-off was 10:00. It has moved to 11:00 because the laboratory
now has a second curing unit. Dentures handed in after the cut-off are normally ready by 12:00 on the
next opening day.
Note. Hard relines and the addition of a tooth after an extraction need an impression taken by the
dentist first. On weekdays these are still same-day if the denture is handed in by 11:00, but they are
not offered on Saturdays.
3. Services and prices
All prices below are per denture and include the laboratory work and a short fit check by the dentist
when you collect it. Every visit starts with an assessment by the dentist, which costs 300 baht; this
assessment fee is waived if you go ahead with the repair or reline on the same day.
Crack or fracture repair: 900 baht for a single crack or a denture broken into two pieces. A denture
broken into three or more pieces costs 1,400 baht to repair, if the dentist agrees that it can be
repaired.

Re-attaching or replacing a tooth: 600 baht for the first tooth and 250 baht for each additional
tooth on the same denture.
Clasp repair or replacement (the metal wire hook on an acrylic partial denture): 750 baht per clasp.
Adding a tooth after an extraction (acrylic partial dentures only): 1,200 baht per tooth, including the
impression.
Soft reline: 1,800 baht. A soft cushioning layer is added at the chair in about 45 minutes. It is a
temporary measure that normally lasts around 3 months.
Hard reline: 2,900 baht. The fitting surface is rebuilt in the laboratory with new acrylic after an
impression. The denture is out of your mouth for about 4 hours.
Ease and polish adjustment (sore spots, rough edges): 400 baht, usually done in 20 minutes.
If a denture has been glued at home, the laboratory must grind away the old glue before it can repair the
break. A cleaning fee of 500 baht is then added to the repair price, and in some cases the pieces no
longer fit together and a new denture is the only option.
4. If your denture breaks: what to do before you come
Please follow these steps so that we can repair the denture quickly and accurately:
1. Take the denture out and stop wearing it.
2. Do not glue, tape or file the denture yourself. Household glue and super glue spoil the edges of the
break and may make a repair impossible.
3. Collect every piece, including any tooth that has come off, even if it is very small.
4. Wrap the pieces in a clean, damp tissue and put them in a closed box or denture case. Never put
them in hot water.
5. Call the FitAgain desk on 055 241 380 (or send a message on LINE to @prasanyim.fitagain) to say
you are coming. Calling ahead is not required, but it lets us keep a laboratory slot for you on busy
days.
6. Bring the denture, your ID card and, if you have one, your Golden Smile membership card to
reception on the ground floor.
5. What happens on the day
At reception you receive a queue number and a FitAgain ticket. The dentist examines your mouth and the
denture in Room 106 and explains what can be done and what it will cost. You must agree to the price
before the laboratory starts work. If a hard reline or an added tooth is needed, the dentist takes an
impression during the same appointment.
While the denture is in the laboratory you may wait in the patient lounge on the 2nd floor, or leave and
come back later. When the work is finished, the laboratory sends you a text message. Collect the denture
at the laboratory window in Room 204 by showing your FitAgain ticket; the dentist then checks the fit
and bite with you for about 10 minutes before you leave. Dentures that are not collected on the same day
are kept at the laboratory window for up to 30 days.
Patients who cannot travel can use the home collection service in Mueang Phitsanulok district on
Tuesdays and Thursdays. A clinic driver collects the denture in the morning and returns it the next

working day; the fee is 250 baht each way, on top of the repair price. Home collection is not available for
relines or added teeth, because these need the patient in the dentist's chair.
6. Relines: soft or hard?
A reline fills the gap that forms between the denture and the gums as they shrink over the years. The
dentist will advise which type suits you:
A soft reline is suitable when the gums are sore or still healing, for example in the first weeks after a
tooth has been removed. It is replaced or followed by a hard reline later.
A hard reline is a longer-term solution for a denture that is still in good condition but has become
loose. After a tooth has been extracted, you must wait at least 8 weeks before a hard reline, so that
the gum has time to settle.
Before a reline appointment, please do not use denture adhesive for 24 hours, and try to wear the
denture for at least 2 hours before you come, so that the dentist can see where it presses.
7. Our repair guarantee
Crack and fracture repairs, tooth replacements and clasp repairs are guaranteed for 90 days from the
date of collection. If the denture breaks again along the same line within this period, we repair it once
more free of charge. The guarantee does not apply if the denture was dropped or stepped on, if it was
glued or altered at home or by another provider after our repair, or if the new break is in a different place.
Hard relines include free ease and polish adjustments for 6 months after the reline. Soft relines are not
guaranteed, because they are temporary by nature. The guarantee never covers a lost denture.
Note. Metal-framework repairs made by our partner laboratory carry that laboratory's own guarantee
of 60 days, not the 90-day FitAgain guarantee.
8. When a new denture is the better choice
Dr. Chanthawong and her team will usually suggest a new denture if your denture is more than 7 years
old and has become loose, or if it has needed three or more repairs in the past 12 months. A new
complete denture at Prasan Yim costs from 14,500 baht per arch and takes 4 visits over about 5 weeks.
If you order a new denture within 60 days of a FitAgain repair, the price of that repair is deducted from
the price of the new denture. Reline charges and home collection fees are not deducted.
9. Payment, discounts and contact
We accept cash, debit and credit cards and QR payment. Holders of the Golden Smile card, the clinic's
free membership for patients aged 60 and over, receive a 10% discount on repairs, tooth replacements,
clasps and adjustments. The discount does not apply to relines, new dentures or the home collection fee.
For questions about the laboratory, contact Narong Phuangkaew, Dental Laboratory Coordinator, on 055
241 380 (extension 204) or at fitagain@prasanyim-dental.co.th.

Help Centre: Recovering Deposits Sent on the
Wrong Network or Without a Memo Tag
Phalang Digital Asset Exchange Co., Ltd. (PhalangX), Bangkok · Article HC-DEP-112 · Version 3 · Updated 14
September 2026
This article explains what PhalangX can and cannot do when a customer sends digital assets to their
PhalangX deposit address in a way that our systems do not credit automatically. Recovery is a manual
service, so it takes time, carries a fee and is not always possible.
1. My deposit has not arrived. Is it a mis-sent deposit?
Not always. First check the transaction on the sending platform. Most deposits are credited after the
number of network confirmations shown on the deposit page, which can take up to 2 hours at busy
times. If the transaction is still pending on the network, PhalangX cannot speed it up. You only need this
article if the transaction is complete on the network but your PhalangX balance has not changed after 2
hours.
2. Which kinds of mis-sent deposit can be recovered?
We sort every request into one of three categories. The category decides the fee, the minimum value and
the target time.
Category A – missing or wrong memo tag. A supported asset was sent on the correct network, but
the memo tag (also called destination tag) was left out or mistyped. Fee: 300 baht. No minimum
value. Target: 5 business days.
Category B – supported asset on the wrong network. A supported asset was sent on a network
that PhalangX does not list for that asset, but where we still control the private key of the receiving
address. Fee: 1,500 baht. Minimum value: 3,000 baht. Target: 15 business days.
Category C – unsupported asset. A token that PhalangX does not list at all was sent to a PhalangX
address. Fee: 2,500 baht or 5 % of the recovered value, whichever is higher. Minimum value: 10,000
baht. Target: 30 business days.
Values are measured in Thai baht at the PhalangX reference price at 00:00 on the day we receive your
complete request. For Category C tokens with no PhalangX price, the Deposit Recovery Desk uses the
average price on two independent public markets.
Note. Deposits sent to a smart-contract address, to an address on a network where PhalangX holds
no keys, or to a mistyped address that does not belong to PhalangX cannot be recovered in any
category. We will tell you this within 3 business days and no fee is charged.
3. I used an old deposit address. What happens?
All customer deposit addresses were rotated on 1 July 2026. Deposits sent to a retired address within 90
days of the rotation (up to and including 28 September 2026) were credited automatically without a

request. Deposits sent to a retired address after that date are handled as Category B requests, but the
minimum value does not apply to them.
4. How do I submit a recovery request?
1. Log in to the PhalangX app or website and open Help Centre, then Deposits, then "Recover a
deposit".
2. Enter the asset, the network you used, the amount and the transaction hash (TXID).
3. Upload a screenshot of the withdrawal record from the sending platform that shows the destination
address and, for memo-based networks, the memo field.
4. Confirm the request with your 6-digit two-factor code. You will receive a case number beginning with
"DR-".
Requests must be submitted within 60 days of the network transaction date. Until 31 May 2026 the limit
was 30 days; the longer limit applies to every request received from 1 June 2026. Target times start only
when the Deposit Recovery Desk confirms that your request is complete, so a missing screenshot or
wrong TXID delays the case.
5. Who works on my case?
The Deposit Recovery Desk, led by Kanlaya Meesuk, Head of Deposit Recovery, checks your evidence,
assigns the category and keeps you updated by in-app message. The actual transfer out of the affected
address is prepared and signed by the Wallet Security Team, because it needs access to our offline key
storage. Category C recoveries with a value above 50,000 baht must also be approved by the Wallet
Security Committee, which meets every Tuesday. The Desk does not have the authority to approve these
cases on its own.
6. How is the fee charged?
The fee is charged only if the recovery succeeds. It is deducted from the recovered asset before the
balance is credited, so you do not need to hold baht in your account. If the recovered value turns out to
be lower than the fee, we decline the case and charge nothing. Network fees for the recovery transfer are
paid by PhalangX and are already included in the fee.
7. Can I use my account while the case is open?
Yes. Trading, deposits and withdrawals of all other assets continue as normal. After a successful
recovery, the recovered asset is credited to your Spot wallet and can be traded at once, but it cannot be
withdrawn for 24 hours.
8. My request was declined. Can I appeal?
You may appeal within 14 days of the decline message. Appeals are reviewed by Worawit Thanapong,
Customer Complaints Officer, who is independent of the Deposit Recovery Desk. Open the case in the
Help Centre and choose "Appeal this decision", explaining which fact you believe was assessed wrongly.
You will receive a written reply within 10 business days. A declined case can be appealed only once.

Internal Memo: Parent Collection of Full Glass
Term-Break Milk Packs, October 2026
Ping Lowland School Meals Partnership, Saraphi and Hang Dong, Chiang Mai · Ref. PLSMP-MEMO-2026-11 ·
21 September 2026
To: Principals and school nutrition coordinators of the 14 partner schools
From: Kanokwan Chaiyanet, Programme Manager, Full Glass Milk Programme (Partnership office, Room
203, Saraphi Learning Centre, tel. 053 447 210)
Copy: Thanakorn Srisupan, Supply Coordinator; Pimchanok Daoruang, Partnership Dietitian; Arunee
Kongchai, Finance Officer
Subject: Change from take-home bags to parent collection for the second-semester break pack
1. The decision
At its meeting of 16 September 2026, the Partnership Steering Group decided that the Full Glass Term-
Break Milk Packs for the coming second-semester break will no longer be carried home by the children
on the last day of school. Instead, each pack will be collected at the school by a parent, guardian or
authorised adult on one of two collection days.
The reason for the change is the experience of the long break in March 2026. Packs were then sent home
in cloth bags with each child on the last day of term. Schools reported that the bags were too heavy for
the younger children, that 312 cartons arrived at homes crushed or leaking, and that a number of packs
were left in classrooms, on school buses and at the Hang Dong songthaew stop. Parent collection was
tested at Ban Nong Phueng School in March and almost no cartons were lost or damaged there.
2. Break dates and pack contents
The partner schools close after lessons on Friday 9 October 2026 and reopen on Monday 2 November
2026. The break therefore covers 15 weekdays, from Monday 12 October to Friday 30 October. The Full
Glass Programme provides one carton of milk for each weekday on which a child would normally have
received milk at school.
Standard pack: 15 cartons of 200 ml UHT plain milk, packed in one sealed cardboard box with the
pupil's name label. A full box weighs about 3.4 kg.
Soy pack: 15 cartons of 180 ml unsweetened UHT soy milk, for pupils who hold a valid soy-milk card
(see section 6).
Previous practice: for the long break in March 2026, each pupil received 40 cartons, delivered in two
bags of 20. That arrangement applied to the long break only and is not repeated in October.
Every pupil from Anuban 1 to Prathom 6 who is on a partner school's register on Wednesday 30
September 2026 is entitled to one pack. Pupils in Mathayom classes at the two extended-opportunity
schools are not part of the Full Glass Programme and do not receive a pack. School nutrition
coordinators must send their final pupil count to the Partnership office by 16:00 on Thursday 1 October
2026, using the green count form in the shared programme folder.

Note. Packs are for the pupil's own use during the break. Schools must not open boxes to share
cartons between pupils, to give milk to staff, or to use milk for cooking classes.
3. Collection days and opening hours
Each school opens a collection point on two days only:
Wednesday 7 October 2026, from 14:30 to 17:30;
Thursday 8 October 2026, from 14:30 to 17:30.
The collection point is the school hall, or the canteen at schools without a hall. Each collection point
needs at least two staff members during opening hours: one to check the collector against the list, and
one to hand over the boxes.
4. Who may collect a pack
A pack may be handed over only to one of the following people:
a parent or guardian whose name appears on the pupil's school record, on showing a Thai ID card,
passport or pink card;
any other adult aged 18 or over who brings the pupil's green collection slip, signed by a parent or
guardian, together with his or her own ID;
a pupil in Prathom 5 or Prathom 6 who brings his or her own signed green collection slip. These
pupils may collect their own pack only, never a pack for a brother, sister or classmate.
Pupils in Anuban 1 to Prathom 4 may not collect any pack, even with a signed slip. Class teachers will
send the green slips home with the pupils on Friday 2 October. A lost slip can be replaced by the class
teacher on the collection days.
5. What the school does

Huai Hong Dairy Cooperative will deliver all packs to the partner schools on Monday 5 October 2026,
between 07:00 and 11:00. The school nutrition coordinator, or a teacher named by the principal, must be
present to receive the delivery.
1. Count the boxes against the delivery note before the driver leaves, and write any shortfall on the

Card Holds and Pre-Authorisation Rules for Sornsin
Wayfarer Credit Cards
Sornsin Bank · Card Services Policy CSP-2026-07, version 3.1 · Issued 12 October 2026 · Effective 1
November 2026
1. Purpose and scope
This policy explains when Sornsin Bank places a temporary hold on a Sornsin Wayfarer credit card, how
large it may be, how long it stays and how to have it released early. It applies to all personal Sornsin
Wayfarer Classic, Gold and Signature cards, including supplementary cards linked to them. It does not
apply to Sornsin corporate cards.
Version 3.1 replaces version 3.0 of 1 March 2025.
2. What a hold is
Pre-authorisation hold: an amount a merchant reserves on the card before the final price is known.
It is not charged, but it reduces the available credit.
Final settlement: the actual amount the merchant charges. When the settlement arrives, the
matching hold is removed and only the settled amount appears on the statement.
3. Maximum hold amounts by merchant type
Sornsin Bank declines pre-authorisation requests above these limits:
Fuel pumps (pay-at-pump): up to 2,000 baht per transaction. Until 31 October 2026 the limit was
1,500 baht. Fuel paid at the station counter is not a pre-authorisation and has no hold.
Electric vehicle charging stations: up to 600 baht per charging session.
Hotels and serviced apartments: the room rate for the booked nights plus up to 20 % of that total
for incidentals. The full hold is capped at 15,000 baht for Classic and Gold cards and at 30,000 baht
for Signature cards.
Car and motorcycle rental: up to 25,000 baht for a car and up to 5,000 baht for a motorcycle or
scooter, on all card tiers.
Restaurants and bars: the bill amount plus up to 15 % to allow for a tip added after the card is
presented.
Note. The hotel margin is calculated on the room total only: 3 nights at 2,000 baht allow a hold of at
most 7,200 baht.
4. Automatic release periods
If no final settlement arrives, Sornsin Bank removes the hold automatically at the end of the release
period, counted in calendar days from the date the hold was placed:

Domestic holds in Thai baht at fuel pumps, EV chargers, restaurants and other merchants: 7 calendar
days.
Domestic hotel and rental holds: 21 calendar days.
Foreign-currency holds of any merchant type: 14 calendar days. Under version 3.0 this period was 30
days.
A settlement that arrives after release is posted as a normal purchase.
5. Effect on available credit, interest and fees
A hold reduces the available credit by the held amount but is never treated as a purchase. No interest is
charged on a hold and a hold never appears on the monthly statement.
The over-limit fee is 300 baht per statement cycle in which the settled balance exceeds the credit limit.
The fee is not charged if the limit is exceeded only because a hold is larger than the merchant's final
settlement. If the final settled amounts themselves take the balance over the limit, the fee applies as
normal.
6. Requesting early release of a hold
When a merchant has cancelled a booking or charged less than the held amount, the cardholder may ask
the bank to release the hold before the automatic release period ends:
1. Ask the merchant for a written cancellation or release confirmation that shows the merchant name,
date and amount.
2. Open the Sornsin app, go to Cards, then Pending Holds, select the hold and tap Request Release.
Upload the merchant confirmation. Cardholders without the app can call Card Services on 0 2118
4400, then email the confirmation to holds@sornsin-bank.example.
3. The bank checks the confirmation and releases the hold within 2 business days. Requests from
Signature cardholders received before 15:00 on a business day are released on the same day.
Without a merchant confirmation the bank cannot release a hold early.
7. Supplementary cards
Holds on supplementary cards reduce the shared credit limit of the primary account. From 1 November
2026 a supplementary cardholder may request early release of a hold placed on their own card number,
provided they have registered their own profile in the Sornsin app. They may not request release of holds
on the primary card or on other supplementary cards; those requests must come from the primary
cardholder, who may request release for any card on the account.
8. Responsibilities and complaints
Krisada Phonmanee, Head of Card Authorisations, owns this policy and reviews the hold limits every 12
months. A cardholder who disagrees with a decision under this policy may complain to the Sornsin Bank
Card Complaints Unit within 60 days of the decision. The unit replies within 15 business days.

Savings Cooperative Launches RiverPassbook
Boat Collection for Seven Mekong-Bank Villages
Tha Uthen Riverbank Savings Cooperative Ltd. · Press release PR-2026-09 · For immediate release, 1 October
2026
THA UTHEN, NAKHON PHANOM, 1 October 2026 – Tha Uthen Riverbank Savings Cooperative Ltd.
today announced RiverPassbook, a weekly boat collection service that will bring savings deposits, loan
repayments and small withdrawals to members living in seven villages along the Mekong north and south
of Tha Uthen town. The first trip departs on Monday 2 November 2026.
1. Why a boat?
Since March 2024 the cooperative has run a Saturday pickup-truck counter, but a 2025 member survey
found that 38 per cent of members in the riverside villages had missed at least one monthly savings
deposit because of travel problems. The pickup-truck counter will make its last run on Saturday 31
October 2026 and will be replaced by the boat.
The service uses the cooperative's own long-tail boat, the Nam Oom 2, fitted with a locked cash box and
a handheld passbook terminal with a receipt printer. Every trip carries two staff: Boat Collection Officer
Boonlert Phothisan and a second officer from the counter team, who takes turns according to the weekly
roster.
2. Route and timetable
The boat leaves the cooperative's river landing behind the head office at 214 Chayangkun Road at 08:00
and stops for about 50 minutes at each village landing. The weekly pattern is:
Monday (northern route): Ban Na Thon, Ban Don Toei and Ban Hat Kruat, returning by 12:30.
Wednesday (southern route): Ban Phon Sawan, Ban Nong Khiat and Ban Kham Toei, returning by
13:00.
Friday (island stop): Ban Don Sawan on Don Sawan island, the only village with no road link, from
09:00 to 11:00.
3. What members can do on board
Savings deposits: from 20 baht up to 20,000 baht per member per visit. Larger deposits must be
made at the head office counter.
Loan repayments: any instalment on an existing cooperative loan, up to 20,000 baht per visit,
counted separately from deposits.
Withdrawals: up to 3,000 baht per member per visit from an ordinary savings account.
New loans, account opening and share purchases remain at the head office.

Flood period exception. When the Tha Uthen District Office declares a local flood emergency, the
withdrawal limit on the boat rises to 5,000 baht per member per visit until the declaration is lifted.
The deposit and repayment limits do not change.
4. How to register
Members must register once before they can use RiverPassbook. Registration is free and takes about ten
minutes:
1. Collect form RP-1 from the head office counter or from your village savings committee leader.
2. Fill in the form, choose your home landing and sign it before the committee leader or a counter
officer.
3. Attach a copy of your national ID card and show your original passbook so that a QR sticker can be
added to its back cover.
4. Hand in the form by Friday 23 October 2026 to be on the list for the first trip. Forms received later are
added to the list on the following Monday.
On board, the officer scans the QR sticker, enters the amount, and prints a two-part receipt. The member
checks the amount, signs one part, and keeps the other part. Members should keep their receipt slips for
at least 60 days, until the transaction appears on their monthly statement.
5. Safety and cancelled trips
The boat does not sail when the river level at the Tha Uthen gauge is above 11.5 metres, during
thunderstorms, or if only one officer is available. Cancellations are posted in each village's LINE group by
06:30 on the day of the trip. A cancelled Monday or Wednesday trip is replaced by a make-up trip on the
next Saturday at the same times; a cancelled Friday island trip is replaced on the next Tuesday instead.
Cash on board is limited to 150,000 baht. When the cash box reaches this amount, the crew stops
accepting deposits until they return to the landing, although withdrawals continue.
6. Fees and the Boat Saver bonus
RiverPassbook transactions are free of charge until 31 October 2027. After that, any fee will not exceed 5
baht per transaction. The ordinary savings rate stays at 1.75 per cent per year.
To encourage regular saving, members who make a boat deposit of at least 100 baht in each of the first
12 weeks of the service will receive a one-off Boat Saver bonus of 150 baht, credited to their savings
account in February 2027. A missed week caused by a cancelled trip does not count against the member
if they deposit on the make-up trip.
7. Comment from the cooperative
"Our river members have always saved; the road was the problem," said Kanyarat Sriwong, Manager of
Tha Uthen Riverbank Savings Cooperative. "With RiverPassbook the counter comes to the landing."
Media contact: Siriporn Duangkaew, Member Relations Officer · Tel. 042 541 870 · press@thauthenriverbank-
coop.example

NoctiTrace HS-2 Home Sleep Test Kit: Patient
Quick-Start and Return Leaflet
Mae Ping Sleep and Breathing Centre, Chiang Mai · Patient leaflet PIL-SLP-07, version 3.1 · Issued 1 August
2026 · Replaces version 3.0 of 14 January 2026
1. About this leaflet and your kit
Your doctor has asked for a home sleep test. You will take a NoctiTrace HS-2 Home Sleep Test Kit home
and record your breathing, oxygen level, pulse and body position while you sleep in your own bed. The
kit belongs to the Mae Ping Sleep and Breathing Centre and is lent to you for a short, fixed period.
The NoctiTrace HS-2 records only. It does not treat snoring or sleep apnoea and nobody watches the
recording while you sleep.
What is in the grey kit case
Recorder unit (HS-2): a small black box with one round button and one status light. The kit number
(for example "MP-HS2-0148") is printed on its back.
Chest effort belt: an elastic belt with a clip that holds the recorder on your chest.
Nasal cannula: a thin clear tube with two soft prongs that sit just inside your nostrils. It is single-use
and sealed in its own bag; two are supplied, one for each night.
Finger oxygen sensor: a soft clip on a short grey cable, worn on the index finger of your non-
dominant hand.
USB charging cable with plug adapter, a night diary card and a padded return pouch.
2. When your test takes place
Kits are collected in person from the Sleep Test Desk, Building B, ground floor, on Monday to Thursday
between 14:00 and 16:30. We do not hand out kits on Fridays, at weekends or on public holidays. At
collection, Anuchit Thepkaew, our Kit Loan Coordinator, or one of the desk nurses will fit the kit on you
once so you can see how it goes on, and you will sign the loan form.
Your two test nights are the night of the collection day and the night immediately after it. The recorder is
programmed to accept a maximum of two recordings; it will not start a third night. If you cannot do the
test on the planned nights, do not move the nights yourself: call the Sleep Test Desk before 16:00 on the
collection day and we will arrange a new collection date.
3. Preparing for each test night
Charge the recorder during the afternoon until the status light is steady green. A charge lasts one
night only.
Do not drink alcohol after 18:00 and avoid coffee, tea, energy drinks and cola after 14:00 on both test
days.
Take your usual medicines as normal, including sleeping tablets you take every night. Tell the desk
nurse at collection about any new medicine started in the last two weeks.

Remove nail polish, gel nails or false nails from the index finger that will carry the sensor, because
they block the light the sensor uses.
4. Putting the kit on
Fit the kit in your bedroom about 15 minutes before you plan to switch off the light. Follow the steps in
this order:
1. Wash and dry your face; do not use face cream or oil around the nose.
2. Fasten the chest effort belt around your chest, just below the armpits, over a thin cotton shirt or
directly on the skin. It should be snug but you must be able to slide two fingers under it.
3. Clip the recorder onto the belt in the middle of your chest, with the button facing upwards towards
your chin.
4. Open a new nasal cannula bag. Place the prongs in your nostrils, loop the tube over both ears and
slide the small bead under your chin until the tube stays in place. Push the end of the tube firmly into
the port on the top of the recorder.
5. Put the finger sensor on the index finger of your non-dominant hand, with the cable running along the
back of your hand. Plug it into the side socket of the recorder.
6. Press and hold the round button for 3 seconds until the light flashes blue three times. The recording
has now started.
7. Write the time you switched off the light on the night diary card, then try to sleep normally.
Note. Use a fresh cannula on the second night. Never wash or reuse a cannula.
5. During the night
While the recorder is working correctly, the light gives one short green flash every 10 seconds. You can
sleep in any position. If you wake up to use the toilet, leave the kit on; note on the diary card any time
you are awake for more than about 20 minutes.
A night counts as a valid recording when there are at least 4 hours of usable signal from both the nasal
cannula and the finger sensor. The sleep physician needs only one valid night to report the result.
If the status light changes
Slow amber flash: a sensor has lost contact. Check that the cannula prongs are in your nostrils and
the finger clip is on firmly, then push both plugs in again.
Fast amber flash: the battery is low. Connect the charging cable to a wall socket and keep wearing
the kit; the recorder keeps recording while it charges.
Steady red light: the recorder has stopped and cannot be restarted that night. Take the kit off, go
back to sleep and write the time on the diary card. Use the second night as planned.
Stopping the recording in the morning
When you get up for the day, press and hold the button for 3 seconds until the light flashes blue twice,
then remove the finger sensor, cannula and belt in that order. Write your wake-up time on the diary card.

6. Who may and may not use the kit
The NoctiTrace HS-2 is approved by the Centre for adults aged 18 and over. Children and teenagers are
always tested in the sleep laboratory. The kit is also not used for patients who need oxygen at home
overnight, or for patients on a home breathing machine (CPAP or similar), unless the sleep physician has
written "home test on therapy" on the referral. People with a heart pacemaker may use the kit.
The test must cover your usual main sleep period. If you work night shifts and normally sleep during the
day, you may record your daytime sleep instead, provided you tell the Sleep Test Desk when booking and
the coordinator marks the loan form "day-sleep recording". Without this set-up a daytime recording
cannot be scored reliably and will usually need to be repeated.
7. Returning the kit
Return the complete kit, including the diary card and the charging cable, by 12:00 on the day after your
second test night. There are two ways to return it:
In person: on working days between 08:00 and 12:00, bring the case to the Sleep Test Desk counter
in Room B214, Building B, second floor (the desk moves upstairs in the mornings, when the ground
floor is used for clinics). Before 08:00 or if the desk is closed, use the grey drop box marked "Sleep
Kits" beside the main entrance of Building A; it is emptied at 08:30 and 12:00.
By courier: only for patients living outside Chiang Mai province who chose this option on the loan
form. Seal the case in the padded return pouch and hand it to the courier who collects it from your
address on the morning after the second night. Keep the tracking slip until your deposit is refunded.
Deposit and charges
A refundable deposit of 3,000 baht is paid by card or bank transfer when you collect the kit. Until 30 June
2026 the deposit was 2,000 baht; patients who collected a kit before 1 July 2026 keep the old amount.
The deposit is refunded to the same card or account within 7 working days after the kit is checked. The
following amounts are deducted when they apply:
Late return: 300 baht for each working day, or part of a day, after the 12:00 deadline.
Missing finger oxygen sensor: 1,800 baht.
Missing chest effort belt: 450 baht. Missing charging cable or adapter: 250 baht.
Damaged or lost recorder unit: the whole deposit is kept, and the Centre may ask for the remaining
repair cost.
8. Your results
The recording is downloaded at the Centre and scored by a sleep technologist, then reported by Dr.
Phakhawadee Srisombat or another sleep physician within 10 working days of the kit being returned.
Results are given at a follow-up appointment, not over the phone. If neither night reaches 4 hours of
usable signal, one repeat test is offered free of charge.
Contacts. Sleep Test Desk (kit loans, bookings, returns): 053 118 460, Monday to Friday 08:00 to 16:30.
Urgent kit problems out of hours: text your kit number to 081 774 2093 (answered 19:00 to 22:00).

Return of Loaned PureDrum Purifiers and
Generators After the 2026 Mun River Flood
Response
Saeng Thian Relief Foundation, Ubon Ratchathani · Operations Notice OPS-N-2026-31 · Issued 1 October
2026
To: village volunteer coordinators and partner sub-district relief teams in Warin Chamrap, Det Udom,
Phibun Mangsahan and Sawang Wirawong districts that borrowed equipment during the 2026 flood
response.
The emergency phase of the Foundation's 2026 Mun River flood response closes on 31 October 2026.
During the response, the Foundation lent 146 PureDrum 60 portable water purifiers and 38 portable
petrol generators to 61 villages.
1. Where and when to return equipment
All equipment is returned to the Warin Chamrap Field Depot, Warehouse B, Gate 3. The return window
runs from 13 October to 7 November 2026. The depot receives returns Monday to Saturday, 08:30–
16:00; it is closed on Sundays and on 23 October 2026 (Chulalongkorn Day).
Until 30 September 2026, returns were taken at the temporary collection point in the Det Udom school
gymnasium. That point is now closed.
2. Preparing a PureDrum 60 for return
1. Note the reading on the litre counter on the side of the drum and write it on the orange return tag that
came with the unit.
2. Drain all water from the drum and the outlet tap.
3. Flush the unit by pumping 10 litres of clean water through it, then drain again.
4. Leave the lid and tap open to air-dry for at least 24 hours in the shade.
5. Pack the hand pump handle, pre-filter sock and lid strap inside the drum.
Do not open the sealed cartridge housing yourself. The membrane cartridge in each PureDrum 60 is
rated for 20,000 litres. Depot staff will read the counter, and any unit that shows more than 18,000 litres
will have its cartridge replaced free of charge before the next season.
3. Returning generators
Generators must be returned with no more than a quarter tank of petrol, with the oil cap in place and the
extension cable reel included. Excess fuel is drained by the depot and not paid back. A generator that
has stopped working should be returned as it is, without home repairs.

4. Deposits and charges
Villages paid a refundable deposit when they borrowed equipment: 1,500 baht per PureDrum 60 and
3,000 baht per generator. The deposit is refunded by bank transfer to the village fund account within 15
working days after check-in. If parts are missing, the following amounts are deducted from that unit's
deposit:
Hand pump handle: 350 baht
Pre-filter sock: 120 baht
Lid strap: 80 baht
Cartridge housing cracked or opened: 900 baht
Generator extension cable reel: 450 baht
Normal wear and mud stains are not charged. A purifier or generator that is lost or not returned by 7
November 2026 is treated as lost: its deposit is kept and the village is invoiced an additional 4,500 baht
per purifier or 9,000 baht per generator.
5. Extension for villages still under a water advisory
Some villages are still on the Foundation Health Desk's water-safety advisory list. These villages may
keep their PureDrum 60 units until 15 December 2026. To do this, the coordinator must submit Form
KR-7 (Equipment Loan Extension) to the Health Desk by 31 October 2026. An extension covers at most
2 purifiers per village; any further purifiers the village holds must be returned in the normal window.
Generators cannot be extended under any circumstances.
Note. A village that is removed from the advisory list during the extension must return its purifiers
within 10 working days of being notified, even if this is before 15 December 2026. Form KR-7

Circular to All Drivers: Traffic Fines on Pool Trucks
and the Annual Driving Licence Check
Phu Rua Line Haulage Co., Ltd., Loei Depot · Circular DR-2026-09 · Issued 18 September 2026 · Effective 1
November 2026
To: All employed drivers, relief drivers and shift supervisors
From: Fleet Compliance Desk and Fleet Safety Office
Subject: New rules for handling traffic fines on company trucks, salary deductions, disputes, and the
yearly driving licence check
1. Why this circular is issued
Phu Rua Line Haulage runs 64 pool trucks that are registered in the company's name and shared
between drivers on a rotating roster. When a camera or roadside officer issues a fine, the notice comes to
the company, not to the driver. Under the old system, notices were often found weeks later and the early-
payment discount was lost. This circular replaces Circular DR-2025-11 in full from 1 November 2026.
Fines dated before 1 November 2026 are still handled under DR-2025-11, even if the notice arrives later.
2. How a fine notice is handled at the depot
All fine notices, whether delivered by post, by e-mail or through the registered-owner portal, are sent to
the Fleet Compliance Desk in Building B, Room 204 of the Loei depot. The desk is open Monday to
Friday, 08:00 to 16:30.
1. The desk logs every notice within 2 working days of receipt.
2. The desk matches the offence time against the DriveLog trip records and the key-cabinet sign-out
sheet to identify who was driving.
3. The identified driver receives a fine message in the DriveLog app with a photo of the notice and the
amount due.
4. The driver must open the message and either accept it or start a dispute (Section 5) within 3 working
days of the message being sent.
5. The desk then nominates the driver to the issuing authority as the person in charge of the vehicle.
Nomination must reach the authority within 7 days of the notice date, so the 3-day window cannot be
extended.
If a driver does not respond within 3 working days, the fine is treated as accepted and the nomination is
sent. A driver on approved leave has 3 working days from the first day back at work.
Note. If DriveLog and the key sheet disagree about who was driving, the key sheet signature is
treated as the deciding record. Drivers who hand a truck to a colleague mid-route must record the
handover in DriveLog with the odometer reading; otherwise the driver who signed the key out
remains responsible.

3. Who pays which fine
The general rule is that the driver pays for offences that depend on how the truck was driven, and the
company pays for offences that depend on the condition, paperwork or loading of the truck when these
were outside the driver's control.
3.1 Fines paid by the driver
Speeding, passing a red light and illegal U-turns.
Using a hand-held phone and not wearing a seat belt.
Parking or stopping offences outside a delivery address.
Driving a truck into a time-restricted zone, such as the Loei town centre heavy-vehicle ban from
07:00 to 09:00, when the route sheet showed a different approach.
3.2 Fines paid by the company
Expired vehicle tax, insurance or inspection certificate.
Defects such as broken lights or worn tyres that the driver had reported in the DriveLog pre-trip
check before the fine was issued.
Parking offences at a customer's delivery address during the delivery window shown on the route
sheet, when the customer had no loading bay available.
Overweight fines where the truck was loaded by the warehouse team and the load sheet weight was
within the legal limit.
Note on overweight fines. Every truck leaving the Loei depot with a load above 12 tonnes must
pass over the depot weighbridge, and the driver must attach the weighbridge ticket to the load
sheet. If the driver leaves without a weighbridge ticket when one was required, an overweight fine for
that trip is paid by the driver, even if the warehouse team did the loading. Loads of 12 tonnes or less
do not need a ticket.
A defect that the driver noticed but did not report in the pre-trip check is treated as a driver fine.
4. Payment and salary deductions
The company pays every accepted fine to the issuing authority within the authority's early-payment
period, so that the reduced amount applies. For driver fines, the driver is charged only the reduced
amount that the company actually paid. A driver may choose to pay a driver fine directly instead, but
must upload the receipt to DriveLog within 10 days of accepting the fine; if no receipt is uploaded by
then, the company pays and the amount is deducted.
Deduction method: deducted from the next monthly salary after payment.
Monthly cap: no more than 1,500 baht is deducted in any one month. Any balance above the cap is
carried forward to the following months until it is cleared. Under DR-2025-11 the cap was 2,500 baht;
the lower cap applies to all deductions made from the November 2026 payroll onward, including
balances carried over from earlier fines.
Leaving the company: any outstanding balance is deducted in full from the final salary payment,
without the monthly cap.

5. How to dispute a fine
A driver who believes that a fine was assigned to the wrong person, or that it should be paid by the
company under Section 3.2, may dispute it. Disputes are decided by the Fleet Compliance Officer, Ms.
Kanokwan Butsri.
1. In the DriveLog fine message, tap "Dispute" within the 3-working-day window in Section 2. A dispute
raised after the window closes is not accepted.
2. Attach evidence, such as a handover record, a pre-trip defect report or dashcam footage. The
dashcam file must be requested from the Fleet Safety Office within 48 hours of the offence, because
footage is overwritten after 72 hours.
3. The Fleet Compliance Officer gives a written decision within 5 working days. While the dispute is
open, no nomination is sent and no deduction is made.
4. If the dispute is rejected, the driver may ask the Fleet Safety Manager, Mr. Anucha Wongprasert, for a
second review within 3 working days of the decision. His decision is final for the purposes of this
circular.
6. The annual driving licence check
Every driver must hold a valid heavy-vehicle driving licence of the class required for the truck on the
roster. Once a year, in the month of the driver's birthday, the driver must bring the original licence card to
the Fleet Safety Office, Building B, Room 210, between 08:30 and 15:30 on a working day.
A driver who misses the check by the last working day of the birthday month is removed from the roster
from the first day of the next month until the check is done. The removal is unpaid unless the driver was
on approved leave for the whole birthday month.
6.1 Licence renewal
Drivers must renew their licence at least 30 days before it expires. The company grants one paid half-day
for the renewal appointment and reimburses the renewal fee up to 650 baht when the receipt is
submitted in DriveLog. A renewal done after the licence has expired is not reimbursed, and the paid half-
day is not given.
After renewal, a driver who has only the receipt and has not yet received the new card may drive
company trucks for up to 14 calendar days from the date on the receipt. From day 15, the driver is taken
off the roster until the new card is shown to the Fleet Safety Office. No company truck may be driven on
an expired licence under any circumstances.
7. Contacts
Fleet Compliance Desk (Ms. Kanokwan Butsri, Fleet Compliance Officer): fine notices,
nominations, disputes and receipts. Building B, Room 204, phone 042 811 604.
Fleet Safety Office (Mr. Anucha Wongprasert, Fleet Safety Manager): licence checks, renewals,
dashcam requests and second reviews. Building B, Room 210, phone 042 811 617.
HR Payroll Office: deduction schedules and carried-over balances. Building A, Room 112, phone
042 811 630.

Pond Share Programme: Terms and Conditions for
Neighbouring Farmers
Khao Sawang Solar Power Co., Ltd. · Khao Sawang Solar Farm, Sung Noen, Nakhon Ratchasima · Ref. KSS-
POL-WTR-03, version 3.1 · Approved by the Site Management Committee on 12 September 2026 · Effective 1
November 2026
1. Purpose and scope
Khao Sawang Solar Power Co., Ltd. ("the Company") operates Khao Sawang Solar Farm, a 48 MW
ground-mounted solar plant on 312 rai of land in Sung Noen District. The site has two retention ponds.
The North Pond, with a design capacity of 64,000 cubic metres, collects stormwater from the array
drains and the rinse water from panel cleaning. The South Pond is the site's fire-fighting reserve.
Under the Pond Share Programme, which began in the 2023/24 dry season, the Company lets registered
neighbouring farmers draw surplus water from the North Pond. These terms explain who may join, how
much water may be drawn, what it costs, and the safety rules on site. They apply to every registered
farmer and nominated helper and to all Company staff who run the programme. Version 3.1 replaces
version 3.0 of 2 October 2025.
Note. The South Pond is never part of the Pond Share Programme. No water may be drawn from it
at any time, including during a drawing suspension at the North Pond.
2. Who may join
A farm may be registered if all of the following apply:
the farmland lies within 3 km of the solar farm boundary fence, in Tambon Khorat or Tambon Na
Klang;
the applicant owns the land or holds a written lease for the whole drawing season;
the applicant has no unpaid Pond Share invoice from an earlier season.
The programme accepts at most 40 registered farms per season. If more applications arrive, farms
nearest the boundary fence are accepted first. Applications are taken from 1 to 20 October each year at
the Community Relations Office, the single-storey building beside Gate 3. The applicant brings a copy of
the national ID card, a copy of the title deed or lease, and a sketch showing where the water will be used.
Each accepted farm receives a numbered Pond Share card for the season. The card names the
registered farmer and, if requested, one nominated helper. The nominated helper must be aged 18 or
over and must sign the safety briefing sheet in person before the card is issued.
3. Drawing season, days and quotas
The drawing season runs from 1 December to 30 April. Outside the season the North Pond is kept for the
Company's own use and no drawing takes place.
Drawing days: Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, 07:00 to 11:00. There is no drawing on public
holidays.

Drawing point: the metered standpipe SP-1 on the east bank of the North Pond. Farmers may not
place their own pumps or hoses in the pond.
Monthly quota: 20 cubic metres per rai of registered farmland. Only the first 15 rai of a farm count
towards the quota, so no farm may draw more than 300 cubic metres in one calendar month.
Single visit limit: 60 cubic metres per farm per drawing day.
Unused quota does not carry over to the next month. Until 30 April 2026 the monthly quota was 25 cubic
metres per rai; it was reduced for the 2026/27 season because the Company now cleans the panels four
times a year instead of three.
4. Pond level rules
The pond level is read on gauge post NP-2, next to standpipe SP-1, every day at 16:00. The reading
decides the drawing status for the next drawing day:
Level 2.4 m or higher: normal drawing with full quotas.
Level below 2.4 m but at least 1.8 m: reduced drawing. Monthly quotas and the single visit limit are
both halved.
Level below 1.8 m: drawing is suspended. The remaining water is reserved for panel cleaning.
Any change of status is announced in the "Pond Share Khao Sawang" LINE group by 18:00 on the day of
the reading and posted on the notice board at Gate 3. A suspension ends only when the level has been
at 2.0 m or higher on three consecutive daily readings.
Exception for seedbeds. During reduced drawing, a farm that registered a rice seedbed or
vegetable nursery on its application may still draw up to 45 cubic metres per drawing day for that
seedbed, within its halved monthly quota. This exception does not apply during a suspension.
5. Fees and payment
Registration fee: 300 baht per farm per season, paid when the card is issued.
Water charge: 4 baht per cubic metre, as recorded by the SP-1 meter. Until 30 April 2026 the charge
was 3 baht per cubic metre.
Small farm allowance: farms with 5 rai or less of registered farmland pay no water charge for the first
50 cubic metres drawn in each month.
Card replacement: 100 baht for a lost or damaged card.
The Company issues an invoice on the first working day of each month for the water drawn in the
previous month. Payment is due by the 10th of that month, in cash at the Community Relations Office or
by bank transfer quoting the card number. If payment is late, the card is blocked until the invoice is paid.
A farm that pays late twice in the same season loses its card for the rest of that season.
6. Water quality and permitted uses
North Pond water is untreated. The Company rinses panels with plain water only and uses no detergents,
but the water may contain dust, bird droppings and algae. The Water and Environment Supervisor sends

a sample to an independent laboratory in Nakhon Ratchasima every quarter, and the latest results are
posted at Gate 3.
The water may be used for irrigating rice seedbeds, vegetables, field crops and fruit trees, and for
watering cattle and buffalo. It may not be used for drinking or cooking, for filling household water jars, or
for stocking fish ponds. Water may not be sold or given to farms that are not registered.
7. Access and safety on site
Pond Share farmers enter and leave only through Gate 3 on the east side of the site, off the Sung
Noen–Khorat road. They sign in at the guardhouse and show their card on every visit.
Only the registered farmer or the nominated helper named on the card may draw water. Children
under 12 may not enter the site.
The speed limit inside the site is 20 km/h. Farm trucks and tractor trailers may weigh at most 6
tonnes loaded, because of the culvert on the access track.
Visitors must stay on the access track and the east bank. Entering the fenced array area, swimming
and fishing are forbidden.
Any accident, spill or damage to Company equipment must be reported to the guardhouse before
leaving the site. Life ring stations are placed every 50 metres along the east bank.
8. Roles and responsibilities
Site Manager, Pradit Wongsa: approves these terms each season, decides on suspensions and
appeals, and may remove a farm for serious safety breaches.
Water and Environment Supervisor, Sukhon Phetrat: reads gauge post NP-2 and the SP-1 meter,
keeps the drawing log, and arranges the quarterly water tests.
Community Relations Officer, Kanokwan Thepsiri: handles applications, issues and replaces Pond
Share cards, runs the LINE group, and receives complaints.
Finance Section: prepares the monthly invoices and records payments.
9. Complaints and appeals
A farmer who disagrees with a meter reading, an invoice or a decision to block or remove a card may
submit a written complaint to the Community Relations Office within 14 days. The Site Manager gives a
written decision within 10 working days. While a complaint about an invoice is open, the card stays
active if the undisputed part of the invoice has been paid.
Community Relations Office: open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 16:30, telephone 044 118 760.

Centre Guide: Sealing, Storing and Handing Over
Answer Script Parcels
Saeng Panya National Examinations Board (SPEB), Script Logistics Section · Ref. SPEB-LOG-G04, version 2 ·
Issued 14 December 2026 · Applies to the March 2027 Grade 12 Leaving Examination
This guide explains, step by step, what an examination centre must do with completed answer scripts
from the moment a session ends until the scripts leave the centre in an SPEB collection van. It applies to
all 1,186 centres running the Grade 12 Leaving Examination (G12LE) from Monday 1 March to Monday 8
March 2027. Version 2 replaces the October 2025 guide; the main changes are the new grey parcel bags,
the shorter sealing window and the higher custodian allowance.
1. Roles at the centre
Centre Manager: normally the school director. Appoints the Script Custodian by 15 January 2027 on
Form SL-1 and is accountable to SPEB for the centre as a whole.
Script Custodian: a permanent staff member who is not teaching any G12LE subject. Receives
sealed parcels from the exam rooms, stores them and hands them to the collection crew.
Chief Invigilator: one per exam room. Counts the scripts and seals the parcel for that room.
Regional Collection Officer: an SPEB employee who plans collection routes and is the first contact
for any parcel problem. For the Northeast region this is Mr. Somkiat Laohaphan at the Khon Kaen
office.
2. Sealing the parcel in the exam room
1. When the session ends, the Chief Invigilator collects the scripts in seat-number order and checks the
count against the room attendance sheet.
2. Place the scripts in a grey tamper-evident bag. Each bag carries a printed serial number starting with
"SP-27-". A bag holds at most 40 scripts; a room with more candidates uses a second bag, and both
serial numbers go on the attendance sheet.
3. Put the top copy of the attendance sheet inside the bag, on top of the scripts. Keep the yellow copy
for the centre file.
4. Peel the strip and press the seal closed. Sealing must be finished within 20 minutes of the end of the
session. Under the October 2025 guide the limit was 45 minutes; that limit no longer applies.
5. The Chief Invigilator and one other invigilator sign across the seal label with a blue ballpoint pen and
write the session code, for example "TH1-AM".
6. Unused blank scripts and question papers never go into the grey bag. Return them in the white
envelope supplied for that subject.
Absent candidates. Do not place an empty or name-only script in the bag for an absent candidate.
Mark "ABS" next to the seat number on the attendance sheet instead. Scripts of candidates who left
early are bagged with the rest of the room.

3. Storing parcels before collection
The Chief Invigilator carries the sealed bags straight to the Script Custodian, who checks each seal,
records the serial numbers in the centre log and signs the attendance sheet's yellow copy as received.
Store all bags in a locked steel cabinet in a room with no ground-level windows. Wooden cupboards
and staff rooms are not acceptable.
The Script Custodian holds the cabinet key. The only spare key is kept by the Centre Manager in an
envelope that is signed across the flap and opened only in an emergency.
Overnight storage is allowed only at centres on an extended route (see section 4). Every other centre
must have no parcels left on site after the day's collection.
4. Handover to the collection crew
An SPEB van collects parcels from each centre between 16:30 and 18:00 on every examination day, after
the afternoon session ends at 15:30. Centres more than 150 km by road from their regional office are on
an extended route: their parcels stay in the locked cabinet overnight and the van collects them by 09:00
the next morning. Parcels from the final day, Monday 8 March 2027, are collected the same day at every
centre, including those on extended routes.
1. Ask the crew for their SPEB identity cards and check the names against the crew list e-mailed to the
Centre Manager at 12:00 that day. Do not hand over parcels to anyone not on the list.
2. Read out each serial number while the crew leader ticks it on Form SL-3, the Script Handover
Manifest.
3. Both the Script Custodian and the crew leader sign and date Form SL-3. The crew takes the white
and blue copies; the centre keeps the pink copy for 12 months.
4. If the van has not arrived by 18:30, phone the Script Logistics Hotline on 02-417-5530. Keep the
parcels locked away and do not send them by post, courier or a staff member's car.
5. Damaged seals and missing parcels
If a seal is torn, a serial number is unreadable or the script count looks wrong, do not reseal or open the
bag. Place the whole bag inside a red over-bag, write the serial number on it and report it to your
Regional Collection Officer within 1 hour of finding the problem. The Script Custodian then completes
incident Form SL-9 and gives it to the crew with the parcel.
6. Custodian allowance and contacts
SPEB pays the Script Custodian an allowance of 350 baht per examination session handled, together
with a one-off briefing fee of 500 baht for attending the online custodian briefing on 10 February 2027.
Until 31 December 2026 the session rate was 280 baht. A centre that runs both a morning and an
afternoon session on the same day counts as two sessions. The allowance is paid to the custodian's
bank account by 30 April 2027 after SPEB receives the Centre Manager's claim on Form SL-7.
Questions about this guide go to Ms. Duangporn Thepkasem, Head of Script Logistics
(scripts@speb.example, 02-417-5500). The hotline is open 06:30 to 20:00 on exam days.

Silent Signal Cup 2026 Opens Team Registration as
Hat Yai Prepares for a Visual-Cue Esports Final
Lomkhlai Esports Collective · Press Release Ref. LEC-PR-2026-09 · For immediate release, 1 October 2026
HAT YAI, Songkhla, 1 October 2026 – The Lomkhlai Esports Collective today opened team registration
for the Silent Signal Cup 2026, a national tournament in the 5v5 team game Pinwheel Siege built around
deaf and hard-of-hearing players. The tournament replaces voice communication with visual signals, on-
screen captions and Thai Sign Language at every stage, from the online qualifiers to the live final on
stage in Hat Yai.
The Silent Signal Cup started in 2025 as a one-day invitational for eight teams from the southern
provinces. After strong interest from players in Khon Kaen, Chiang Mai and Bangkok, the 2026 edition is
open to teams from anywhere in Thailand and has grown to a field of up to 32 teams.
1. The tournament at a glance
Game: Pinwheel Siege, 5v5, played on the current competitive patch announced on 1 November
2026.
Online qualifiers: 7 to 22 November 2026, played on weekends only, best-of-one group matches
followed by best-of-three play-offs.
Live finals: Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 December 2026 in the Sea Breeze Hall on level 4 of the
Lomkhlai Arena building, Thanon Niphat Uthit 2, Hat Yai. The top four teams from the qualifiers play
the finals.
Field size: up to 32 teams. If more than 32 complete teams register, places are allocated in the order
in which the entry fee was received.
Prize pool: 480,000 baht in total. The winning team receives 240,000 baht, the runner-up 120,000
baht, and the teams in third and fourth place 60,000 baht each. The 2025 invitational had a prize pool
of 150,000 baht.
2. Who can enter
Each team registers a roster of five starting players and up to two substitutes. At least three of the five
players on the server in any match must be deaf or hard of hearing; the remaining two may be hearing
players. This is a change from the 2025 invitational, where all five starters had to be deaf or hard of
hearing. Teams told the organisers that the old rule made it hard to keep a roster together, and many
mixed groups of friends wanted to play together.
Players confirm their status by signing a Hearing Status Declaration in the registration portal. No
audiogram, medical report or disability card is required, and the organisers do not keep any medical
information. All players must be at least 16 years old on 7 November 2026. Players aged 16 or 17 must
upload a guardian consent form signed by a parent or legal guardian.
Note. A player may appear on only one Silent Signal Cup roster. Coaches do not count towards the
five starters or two substitutes, and each team may name one coach, who may be hearing or deaf.

3. How the visual-cue rules work
Voice chat is switched off for all players during every official match, online and on stage. Teams
communicate through in-game pings, the text panel, and sign language between players at the booth.
Coaches may sign to players only during the draft phase and between maps, never while a round is live.
Booth light signals
During the live finals, each team booth has a light bar above the monitors that replaces the referee's
spoken calls:
Steady amber: a pause has been requested and will start at the end of the current round.
Steady red: the match is paused; players must take their hands off the keyboard and mouse.
Flashing green: play resumes in 10 seconds.
Flashing blue: a technical pause has been called by one of the teams.
In the online qualifiers the same signals appear as coloured banners in the referee's match lobby. Each
team has two tactical pauses of up to 60 seconds per map. Technical pauses have no fixed limit, but the
referee on duty decides whether a technical problem is genuine and when play continues.
Interpreters and captions
Six Thai Sign Language interpreters will work on rotation during the finals, changing every 20 minutes.
Two interpreters stand at the side of the stage for the players, and one appears in a picture-in-picture
window on the broadcast. All casting on the stream carries live captions in Thai and English, prepared by
a captioning team working with a delay of about 4 seconds.
4. How to register a team
Registration is open from 6 October 2026 until 23:59 on 25 October 2026. The team captain completes
the following steps on the Lomkhlai registration portal:
1. Create a team account and choose a team name. Names are checked by the organisers and may be
refused if they are offensive or copy a sponsor's brand.
2. Enter the roster: the in-game ID, full name and province of each of the five starters and any
substitutes.
3. Ask every player to sign the Hearing Status Declaration from the link sent to their own email. The
captain cannot sign for other players.
4. Upload a guardian consent form for any player aged 16 or 17.
5. Pay the entry fee by bank transfer and upload the transfer slip. The fee is 1,500 baht per team, or
1,000 baht per team for early-bird payments received by 15 October 2026.
6. Wait for the confirmation email, which is sent within 3 working days once all declarations and the fee
have been received.
7. Attend the compulsory online rules briefing on Sunday 1 November 2026 at 19:00, delivered in Thai
Sign Language with Thai and English captions. At least three players from each team must attend.
A team that has not completed every declaration by the closing date will not receive a place, even if the
entry fee has been paid. In that case the fee is refunded in full within 14 days.

5. Travel support for finalists
The four finalist teams receive hotel accommodation in Hat Yai for three nights, from 11 to 14 December
2026, for up to seven people per team (five players, one substitute and the coach). Finalist teams based
outside Songkhla province also receive a travel grant of 12,000 baht per team, paid by bank transfer
before 4 December 2026. The travel grant is paid in addition to any prize money and does not have to be
returned. Teams from Songkhla province receive the hotel rooms but not the travel grant.
6. Finals weekend for spectators
Entry to the Sea Breeze Hall is free, but spectators must reserve a seat in advance. The hall has 400
seats, including 60 seats in the front rows kept for deaf and hard-of-hearing spectators with a clear view
of the stage interpreters. Doors open at 10:00 on both days and the first match starts at 11:00.
Spectators are encouraged to use visual applause, raising both hands and shaking them, so that players
can see the reaction of the crowd from the booths.
Spectators who need assistive equipment, such as a vibrating wristband linked to the in-hall sound
system or a seat close to the caption screen, can request it when they book their seat.
7. Who to contact
Tournament Director, Pimchanok Rerkrai: overall running of the tournament, sponsorship, and
payment of prize money and travel grants.
Head Referee, Arthit Chanthep: match rulings, pauses, penalties and disputes. A team that wants to
appeal a ruling must send a written appeal to the Head Referee within 15 minutes after the end of the
map concerned.
Accessibility Lead, Wilaiwan Muangkaew: interpreter bookings, captioning, and requests from players
for assistive equipment at the finals, such as vibrating wristbands or a personal interpreter in the
team warm-up room. Player requests must reach her by 20 November 2026.
Registration desk: questions about the portal, declarations and entry fee payments.
"Last year we proved that a deaf team can play at the highest level without saying a word," said
Pimchanok Rerkrai, Tournament Director. "This year we want every province to send a team, and we
want hearing players to learn that our visual signals make the game clearer for everyone."
About the Lomkhlai Esports Collective
The Lomkhlai Esports Collective is a non-profit community group founded in Hat Yai in 2022. It runs
grassroots tournaments, coaching nights and accessible gaming sessions for players in southern
Thailand, and has organised the Silent Signal Cup since its first edition in 2025.
Media contact: Korawit Sombatsiri, Communications Officer, Lomkhlai Esports Collective. Media
requests for interviews with players should be made by 30 November 2026; interviews with deaf players
are arranged with an interpreter present.

Bua Khiao Pharmacy Launches ClearLabel: Large-
Print, Picture and Spoken Medicine Labels for
Older and Visually Impaired Patients
Bua Khiao Pharmacy Co., Ltd. · Press release Ref. PR-2026-09 · For immediate release · Issued 1 October
2026
SURAT THANI, 1 October 2026 – Bua Khiao Pharmacy, a family-owned community pharmacy group
with seven branches in Surat Thani province, today announced ClearLabel, an accessible labelling
service for people who struggle to read the small print on medicine packs. From 1 November 2026,
patients at the Talat Lang, Kanchanadit and Phunphin branches will be able to ask for labels in large
print, labels with picture symbols for the time of day, and spoken labels that can be played back on a
small handheld reader. The remaining four branches will follow in two stages during early 2027.
The service grew out of a review of dispensing errors reported to the pharmacy group in 2025. Of 64
incidents in which a patient took a medicine at the wrong time or in the wrong amount at home, 27
involved a patient aged over 70 who later told the pharmacist that they "could not read the sticker".
1. What ClearLabel includes
ClearLabel is not a single label but a set of three options. A patient can choose one, two or all three, and
the choice is saved on the patient's record so that it is applied automatically to every future prescription.
1.1 Large-print labels
The large-print label prints the medicine name, the dose and the instructions in 16-point bold type on a
white background, compared with the 9-point type used on Bua Khiao's standard dispensing label.
Because the text is larger, the label is printed on a wider 70 mm sticker that wraps around the box or
bottle, and a second copy is supplied loose in a clear plastic sleeve for the patient's medicine diary.
Instructions are written in plain words: "Take 1 tablet in the morning after breakfast" rather than
abbreviations.
1.2 Picture labels
Picture labels add a row of four symbols to the large-print label: a rising sun for morning, a full sun for
midday, a setting sun for evening and a moon for bedtime. The symbols for the times when the medicine
should be taken are printed in solid black; the others are shown as faint outlines. A separate symbol of a
plate shows whether the medicine is taken with food. A printed key to the symbols is given to the patient.
1.3 Spoken labels
For patients who are blind or have very low vision, the pharmacist can attach a small round sticker
containing a coded audio recording. When the SpeakDot reader, a pen-sized device, is touched to the
sticker, it plays the medicine name, the dose and the instructions aloud in Thai, or in English, Burmese or
Southern Thai dialect on request. Each recording is made by the dispensing pharmacist at the counter
and lasts up to 30 seconds. The reader works with any SpeakDot sticker, so one device covers all of a
patient's medicines.

2. Who can use the service
ClearLabel is open to any patient who has a prescription or a pharmacy medicine dispensed at a Bua
Khiao branch that offers the service. Patients do not need to prove a visual impairment to receive large-
print or picture labels; it is enough to ask. Carers and family members may request the service on behalf
of the person who takes the medicine, provided that person is registered as a Bua Khiao patient.
Large-print, picture and spoken labels are free of charge for medicines dispensed by Bua Khiao. There is
no limit on the number of items per visit.
2.1 Medicines dispensed elsewhere
Patients may also bring medicines dispensed by a hospital or clinic and ask for them to be relabelled.
The pharmacist will relabel an item only if it is still in its original pack and the original dispensing label,
showing the patient's name and the prescriber's directions, is still attached and readable. The ClearLabel
sticker is added next to the original label, never on top of it. Bua Khiao charges 30 baht per item for
relabelling medicines dispensed elsewhere. This fee is waived for patients aged 75 or over and for
holders of a disability identification card.
Note. Medicines that must be kept in a refrigerator, such as insulin pens and some eye drops, and
any medicine with a loose or missing original label cannot be relabelled from another provider. The
pharmacist will instead give the patient a large-print instruction card to keep with the medicine.
2.2 Borrowing a SpeakDot reader
Patients who choose spoken labels can borrow a SpeakDot reader from the branch for as long as they
need it. A refundable deposit of 500 baht is taken when the reader is issued and is returned in full when
the reader is brought back in working order. The deposit is waived for holders of a disability identification
card. During the pilot in 2026 the deposit was 300 baht; it has been raised because of the cost of
replacing lost devices.
3. How to ask for ClearLabel
Patients or carers can sign up at the counter at any time when the branch pharmacist is on duty. The
steps are:
1. Tell the counter staff that you would like ClearLabel and show your Bua Khiao patient card or national
ID card so that your record can be found.
2. The pharmacist asks which options you want (large print, pictures, spoken labels) and, for spoken
labels, which language the recording should use.
3. The pharmacist records your choice on your patient record and asks you to sign the ClearLabel
consent slip, which allows the pharmacy to keep the setting for future prescriptions.
4. If you have chosen spoken labels, the pharmacist issues a SpeakDot reader, takes the deposit if it
applies, and shows you how to use it on your first medicine.
5. Before you leave, the pharmacist reads each new label back to you, or plays the recording, and
checks that you understand when to take each medicine.

Patients who cannot visit in person may sign up by telephone through the ClearLabel line on 077 281
460, open Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 17:00. A carer collecting medicines must then bring the
signed consent slip on the next visit. Settings can be changed or cancelled at any time at the counter or
by telephone.
4. Rollout to all branches
ClearLabel was tested from April to August 2026 at the Talat Lang branch, where 212 patients signed up.
The full rollout runs in three phases:
Phase 1, from 1 November 2026: Talat Lang, Kanchanadit and Phunphin branches.
Phase 2, from 11 January 2027: Chaiya and Don Sak branches.
Phase 3, from 1 March 2027: Ban Na San and Wiang Sa branches.
Large-print and picture labels will be available at every branch from the first day of its phase. Spoken
labels and SpeakDot readers will reach the phase 3 branches two weeks later, on 15 March 2027, once
staff there have completed training.
In a follow-up survey of 150 pilot patients, 88 percent said they found their medicines easier to manage,
and the Talat Lang branch recorded no wrong-time incidents among ClearLabel patients during the five-
month pilot.
5. Quotes
"Many of our older patients were too polite to tell us that they could not read the label. ClearLabel means
they no longer have to ask a grandchild to read it for them," said Kesinee Boonmalert, Pharmacist-in-
Charge at Bua Khiao Pharmacy, who led the pilot.
"We are a small pharmacy group, but we believe the safest medicine is one the patient understands. We
are funding ClearLabel ourselves, and no patient will pay for a label on a medicine we dispense," said
Phichai Rattanakorn, Managing Director of Bua Khiao Pharmacy.
6. Notes for editors
Bua Khiao Pharmacy Co., Ltd. was founded in Surat Thani in 1998 and employs 19 pharmacists
across seven branches. Its head office is at the Talat Lang branch.
ClearLabel does not change any medicine, dose or prescription. It changes only how the instructions
are presented to the patient.
Photographs of sample labels and a short video of the SpeakDot reader are available to the media on
request.
Journalists who would like to see the service in use may visit the Talat Lang branch on weekday
mornings by appointment.
Media contact: Thitima Sangkhaphan, Communications Officer, Bua Khiao Pharmacy · Telephone 077
281 455 · media@buakhiao-pharmacy.example
