Incident Report: Misdated Completion Certificates
RianRuu Online (RianRuu Learning Co., Ltd., Chiang Mai) · Ref. INC-2026-031 · Issued 14 September 2026
1. Summary
Between 21:40 on 2 September and 09:15 on 4 September 2026, the CertMint certificate service printed
the course start date instead of the learner's completion date on every certificate it issued. Grades,
course hours and learner names were correct. The fault came from platform release 4.7.2, which
changed the field CertMint reads for the date. Report owner: Ploenpit Charoensuk, Head of Learner
Records.
2. Impact
In total 1,286 certificates across 19 courses were affected, the largest group being 412 for the
Professional Bookkeeping Level 2 course. Before the fix, 342 of them had been downloaded as PDF, 57
had been shared through an employer verification link and 23 printed copies had been dispatched by
courier.
3. Timeline
2 September, 21:40: release 4.7.2 deployed.
4 September, 08:20: first learner complaint received by the help desk.
4 September, 09:15: certificate issuance paused by Narongrit Thammasak, Platform Engineering
Lead.
4 September, 16:30: platform rolled back to release 4.7.1.
5 September, 10:00: issuance resumed; courses finished during the pause were certified with the
correct date.
4. Corrective actions
All 1,286 certificates were revoked and reissued with the correct date and a new verification code by 12
September 2026. The old codes show the status "Superseded" on the verification page until 11
December 2026 and are then removed.
Free reprint of printed copies: a learner who received a misdated printed certificate gets one free
corrected reprint. The request must be made through the Help Centre form by 31 October 2026. Printed
copies ordered on or after 12 September already show the correct date and are not covered. Reprints
outside this offer cost the normal courier fee of 380 baht (350 baht until 30 September 2026).
Note. If a misdated certificate was already used in a job or scholarship application, the learner may
request a signed explanation letter from Learner Records. The letter is free and is sent as a PDF
within 5 working days.
Prevention: from release 4.8.0, CertMint checks the printed date against the completion record and stops
any mismatched certificate.

Minutes of Election Committee Meeting No. 7/2026:
Post-Count Review of the Ward 3 By-election
Khlong Phai Ngam Town Municipality Election Committee, Chachoengsao · Ref. EC-KPN 07/2026 · Meeting
held 22 September 2026 · Minutes approved 28 September 2026
Venue: Council Meeting Room, 2nd floor, Khlong Phai Ngam Municipal Office, 13:30–16:20. Present:
Wiroj Kanchanasiri (Election Director, chair), Duangporn Yimsamran (Ballot Logistics Officer), Kanokwan
Thiprat (Complaints and Legal Officer), Apichart Somboonsuk (Finance Officer), Chalermchai Noiphan
(Municipal Clerk, committee member), Siriporn Bunthawi (Administrative Assistant, minutes). Observers:
one agent each for Candidate No. 1 and Candidate No. 2. Apologies: Pratuang Saelim (committee
member, ill).
1. Opening and previous minutes
The chair opened the meeting at 13:30 and confirmed a quorum of five members. The minutes of
Meeting No. 6/2026 (2 September 2026) were adopted without change. The chair explained that the
purpose of this meeting was to close the by-election held on Sunday 13 September 2026 to fill the Ward
3 council seat left vacant when the previous councillor resigned on 30 June 2026.
2. Turnout and confirmation of the result
Duangporn Yimsamran presented the consolidated figures from the eight polling stations of Ward 3
(stations 3/1 to 3/8). The final register contained 6,842 eligible voters. A total of 4,117 voters received a
ballot, a turnout of 60.2 %. This was higher than the 54.8 % recorded in Ward 3 at the 2021 general
municipal election.
Of the 4,117 ballots found in the boxes, 3,963 were valid, 96 were invalid and 58 were marked "no vote".
Candidate No. 1, Mr Thawatchai Phromsri: 1,997 votes.
Candidate No. 2, Ms Ladda Chaiwong: 1,966 votes.
The provisional margin announced on the night of 13 September was 33 votes. After the recount
described in item 3 the margin is 31 votes. The committee confirmed Candidate No. 1, Mr Thawatchai
Phromsri, as the elected councillor for Ward 3 and resolved to publish the official result notice at the
municipal office notice board and on the municipality's website on 23 September 2026.
3. Recount at polling station 3/4
Kanokwan Thiprat reported that the agent for Candidate No. 2 lodged a written recount request for
station 3/4 (Wat Bang Rak multipurpose hall) at 16:40 on Monday 14 September. Under the committee's
own by-election rules, a recount request must be made in writing within 48 hours of the end of the count
at the station concerned, must name the station, and must state a specific reason. The count at station
3/4 ended at 19:55 on 13 September, so the deadline was 19:55 on 15 September; the request was
therefore on time. The reason given was that ballots had been read out too quickly for the agents to
follow.

The recount took place on Thursday 17 September from 09:00 to 11:40 in the Council Meeting Room, in
front of both candidates' agents and two committee members. The seal numbers on the box matched
the station record. The recount found two ballots for Candidate No. 1 that had been counted as valid but
carried a second mark in the box of Candidate No. 2; both were reclassified as invalid. No other change
was found. Candidate No. 1 at station 3/4 therefore moved from 263 to 261 votes and the invalid total for
the ward rose from 94 to the final 96 shown in item 2.
The committee agreed that the recount had been properly requested and properly carried out and that
the change did not affect the result. The agent for Candidate No. 2 accepted the recount figures and
signed the recount record. Kanokwan Thiprat noted that a request lodged after the 48-hour limit is
refused without a recount, and that a request covering the whole ward instead of a named station is also
refused.
Note. The 48-hour limit applies only to recount requests made to this committee. An election petition
to a court follows the court's own time limits and is not affected by a refusal of this committee.
4. Ballot paper reconciliation
Duangporn Yimsamran reported on the ballot paper count. The committee ordered 7,200 ballot papers in
pads of 50, numbered in series KPN3-00001 to KPN3-07200. Each station received ballots equal to its
register size plus a margin of at least 1 %, rounded up to whole pads of 50, so 6,950 papers went to the
stations and the remaining 250 were kept in reserve at the municipal office. No reserve papers were
issued on polling day.
At the close of poll every station returned its unused ballots in a sealed envelope. The reconciliation for
each station, adding ballots issued and unused ballots returned, matched the number received, with one
exception. At station 3/7 (Ban Nong Kok School, Building 2) a full pad of 50 unused ballots, serial
numbers KPN3-06151 to KPN3-06200, was missing from the returned envelope. It was found on 15
September in the station's equipment box, still sealed and unused, and was handed to the Ballot
Logistics Officer the same day with a written statement by the station chair.
The committee agreed that no ballot had been misused, since the pad seal was unbroken, but that the
procedure had failed. For future elections, unused pads must be counted in front of the agents and listed
by serial number on the close-of-poll form before the envelope is sealed. The station chair will sign this
list, and the station's second member will countersign it.
5. Storage and destruction of election materials
All eight ballot boxes, the sealed envelopes of unused ballots, the counting sheets and the voter registers
signed on polling day are held in Strongroom B-104 on the ground floor of the municipal office. The
strongroom has two locks; one key is held by the Election Director and the other by the Municipal Clerk,
and the room is opened only when both are present. Every entry is recorded in the strongroom log.
The committee agreed the following retention rules for the Ward 3 by-election:
1. Ballot papers, counting sheets and unused ballots are kept for 90 days after the official result notice
of 23 September 2026, that is until 22 December 2026.

2. If Kanokwan Thiprat receives notice of an election petition before that date, nothing is destroyed until
the petition is closed and the committee has given new written approval.
3. Signed voter registers are kept for 2 years, until 23 September 2028, because they may be needed to
check claims of double voting.
4. Destruction is by cross-cut shredding at the municipal office, witnessed by two committee members
and one observer invited from each candidate. A destruction record is signed by all witnesses.
Destruction of the ballot papers is provisionally scheduled for Monday 11 January 2027 at 10:00.
6. Allowances for polling station staff
Apichart Somboonsuk reported that 64 polling station staff (eight per station) and 16 security volunteers
served on polling day. The allowance rates for this by-election, approved at Meeting No. 5/2026, are
higher than at the 2021 election, when a station chair received 1,000 baht and a station member 750
baht for polling day.
Station chair: 1,200 baht for polling day.
Station member: 900 baht for polling day.
Security volunteer: 600 baht for polling day.
Attendance at the training session of 5 September 2026: 300 baht per person, paid only to staff who
signed the attendance sheet.
All allowances are paid by bank transfer by 30 September 2026. Staff who did not give a bank account
will receive cash at the Finance counter, Room A-012, on 1 and 2 October 2026 from 09:00 to 15:00 on
showing their identity card. Two station members at station 3/6 left before the count ended without the
station chair's permission. The committee agreed that they receive the polling-day allowance at half rate,
450 baht each, but keep the training allowance.
7. Complaints received
Kanokwan Thiprat reported that 11 complaints were received between the close of nominations and the
end of polling day. Six concerned campaign loudspeaker vehicles, four of which were heard after 18:00
on 12 September, the end of the campaign period; both candidates' teams received a written warning.
Three concerned queues at station 3/2 (Wat Khlong Phai hall), where voters using wheelchairs had to
climb four steps. Two were about posters on electricity poles. The committee agreed to move station 3/2
to the level ground-floor canteen of Khlong Phai Witthaya School for the 2027 general municipal election.
No complaint was found to have affected the result.
8. Action points
Publish the official result notice on 23 September 2026: Wiroj Kanchanasiri.
Revise the close-of-poll form to list unused pads by serial number by 30 November 2026: Duangporn
Yimsamran.
Complete all allowance payments and report any unpaid staff by 5 October 2026: Apichart
Somboonsuk.
Next meeting: Meeting No. 8/2026, Tuesday 17 November 2026, 13:30, Council Meeting Room.

KlaPhrom Seedling Tray and Transplanting Service:
Dry Season 2027
Nong Kula Rice Farmers Cooperative Ltd., Bang Rakam, Phitsanulok · Leaflet Ref. NK-SV-2026-09 · Issued 28
September 2026
1. What KlaPhrom offers
KlaPhrom is the cooperative's service for members who want to switch from broadcasting seed to
machine transplanting. The cooperative sows your rice in plastic seedling trays at its nursery behind the
Nong Kula rice mill and then plants them in your field with one of its four walk-behind transplanters.
Transplanted fields need less seed and are easier to weed.
You can book trays only or trays with machine transplanting. Transplanting is not offered without
cooperative trays.
2. Varieties for the 2027 dry season
Nong Kula 3: non-glutinous white rice, 115 days from sowing to harvest; our recommended dry-
season variety.
Sai Thong 9: non-glutinous, 105 days, for fields that must be harvested before the canal closes in
late April.
Kula Niao 2: glutinous rice, 120 days. Limited to 400 rai this season.
3. Tray prices
One rai needs 34 trays, which uses about 5 kg of seed instead of the 20 to 25 kg used for broadcasting.
Members: 22 baht per tray, which is 748 baht per rai.
Non-members: 27 baht per tray, which is 918 baht per rai, and trays only (no transplanting).
Until the end of the 2026 wet season the member price was 19 baht per tray. Trays remain cooperative
property and must be returned within 7 days of planting; a missing or broken tray is charged at 45 baht.
4. Booking rounds
Seedlings are sown in three rounds. Transplanting takes place when the seedlings are 15 to 18 days old.
Round 1: sowing on 5 January 2027, transplanting from 20 to 28 January.
Round 2: sowing on 25 January 2027, transplanting from 9 to 17 February.
Round 3: sowing on 15 February 2027, transplanting from 2 to 10 March.
Bookings for each round close 14 days before its sowing date. The minimum booking is 3 rai per
member. Booking opens on 1 November 2026.
How to book
1. Bring your member book and the land document for each plot to the service counter.

2. Choose your variety, round and the number of rai for each plot.
3. Pay a deposit of 30 % of the tray cost. The rest of the tray cost and the transplanting fee are paid
after planting, or can be added to your harvest account.
4. Collect your booking slip with your booking number.
Note. Members with an unpaid balance from the 2026 wet season fertiliser credit may book only
after the balance has been paid or a repayment plan has been signed with the credit desk.
5. Machine transplanting
The transplanting fee is 550 baht per rai for members, which includes the operator and fuel. Plots of less
than 2 rai are charged as 2 rai. Each machine plants about 12 rai per day.
The operator will phone you the evening before your plot is planted. If your field is not ready when the
crew arrives, the plot goes to the end of the route and a return-visit fee of 300 baht is charged.
6. Using your own seed
Members may bring their own seed for tray sowing, but only if it passes a germination test at the
cooperative's seed room (Room 3, next to the drying yard). The seed must be delivered at least 10 days
before the sowing date of your round, and it must reach a germination rate of 85 % or higher. If it fails,
the booking is changed to cooperative seed at the normal price. Own-seed trays cost 16 baht each.
7. Preparing your field for the transplanter
Please follow these steps:
1. Plough and puddle the field, then level it so that no part is more than 3 cm higher or lower than the
rest.
2. On the day before planting, drain the field until there is 1 to 3 cm of water on the surface.
3. Clear an entry point at least 3 metres wide where the machine and the tray trailer can reach the field
from the road or a bund.
4. Place a flag or a bamboo pole at each corner of the plot so the operator can find it.
8. Cancellations and weather
A booking can be cancelled with a full refund of the deposit up to 7 days before the sowing date. After
that the deposit is not refunded. Once the seed is sown, the full tray cost is charged even if you cancel. If
flooding prevents planting, your plot is rescheduled within 5 days at no extra charge.
9. Contact
KlaPhrom service coordinator: Wanida Chuenjai, service counter at the cooperative office, open Monday
to Saturday from 08:00 to 16:30. Telephone 055 318 442. Crew line during transplanting windows: 089
641 2275, daily 06:00 to 18:00.

Green-Leaf Buying Policy for Registered
Outgrowers, 2026–27 Season
Pang Mok Khiao Tea Factory Co., Ltd. · Ref. PMK-LEAF-POL-04, version 4.1 · Approved by the Board on 22
September 2026 · Effective 1 October 2026
1. Purpose and scope
Pang Mok Khiao Tea Factory Co., Ltd. ("the Factory") processes oolong and green tea at Ban Pang Mok,
Mae Chan district, Chiang Rai. Besides leaf from its own 140-rai estate, the Factory buys fresh green leaf
from smallholder farms in nine hill villages of Mae Chan and Mae Fa Luang. Farmers who sell to the
Factory must be listed on the Leaf Partner Register.
This policy sets out who may join the Leaf Partner Register, how leaf is delivered, graded, weighed and
paid for, and how disagreements are settled. It applies to every registered outgrower and to all Factory
staff who receive, grade or pay for outgrower leaf. Version 4.1 replaces version 3.2 of 15 February 2025.
2. Joining the Leaf Partner Register
A farmer may apply to join if all of the following apply:
the farmer owns or holds a written lease of a tea plot of at least 1 rai and not more than 25 rai;
the plot is within the Factory's collection area, which is shown on the map at the Outgrower Office;
the farmer has attended the half-day Leaf Partner induction session, which is held on the first
Saturday of every month at 09:00 in the Factory training room.
Applications are made in person at the Outgrower Office, beside the main gate, open Monday to
Saturday from 08:00 to 16:30. The farmer brings a national ID card or highland resident card, proof of
land use for the plot, and the first page of a savings account book in the farmer's own name. Each
accepted farmer receives a Leaf Partner number in the format LP-0000 and a laminated farmer card,
which must be shown at every delivery.
Registration is valid for one calendar year and must be renewed by 31 January. A farmer who does not
renew by that date may still deliver leaf until 28 February, but payments are held until renewal is
complete.
3. Collection points and delivery times
Leaf is received at six collection points: Ban Pang Mok (main gate), Ban Huai Kang, Ban Saen Chai, Ban
Pha Daeng, Ban Mae Ku and Ban Lo Cha.
Morning receiving: 07:00 to 11:00, Monday to Saturday.
Afternoon receiving: 14:00 to 17:30, Monday to Saturday.
Sundays and public holidays: Ban Pang Mok main gate only, 07:00 to 11:00.
Leaf must reach a collection point within 4 hours of plucking. It must be carried in clean, ventilated
woven bags or bamboo baskets supplied or approved by the Factory. Plastic fertiliser sacks are not

accepted, because they heat and bruise the leaf. A single bag may hold at most 18 kg of leaf; heavier
bags are split at the collection point before weighing.
Note. During the first flush (1 March to 15 May) afternoon receiving at the village points is extended
to 18:30, and an extra truck runs from Ban Lo Cha at 19:00.
4. Leaf standard and grading
Every delivery is graded at the collection point by a trained grader. The grader takes a random 200 g
sample of shoots from the delivery and counts how many are fine plucks, meaning a bud with up to two
tender leaves attached.
Grade A: 70 % or more of the shoots in the sample are fine plucks.
Grade B: 50 % to 69 % fine plucks.
Grade C: less than 50 % fine plucks, or shoots with coarse stalks longer than 5 cm.
The grader rejects the whole delivery, and the Factory pays nothing for it, if the leaf is red, sour-smelling
or warm to the touch in the centre of the bag; if it contains soil, stones, weeds or other foreign matter; if it
was plucked within a no-pluck period under section 7; or if it arrives without a farmer card.
5. Weighing and wet-leaf deductions
Leaf is weighed on Factory scales in the farmer's presence, and the clerk issues a printed receipt
showing the gross weight, deductions, net weight and grade. A fixed tare of 0.4 kg is taken off for each
woven bag and 0.9 kg for each bamboo basket.
Leaf with water on its surface is reduced in weight after tare as follows:
Dry leaf: no deduction.
Lightly wet leaf (damp to the touch, no free water): 5 % deduction.
Heavily wet leaf (water drips when a handful is squeezed): 12 % deduction.
Until 30 September 2026 the deduction for heavily wet leaf was 10 %. The new rate of 12 % applies to
all leaf received from 1 October 2026.
6. Prices and payment
The base prices for the 2026–27 season, per kilogram of net weight, are:
Grade A: 32 baht per kg (30 baht per kg until 30 September 2026).
Grade B: 24 baht per kg.
Grade C: 14 baht per kg.
A quality bonus of 2 baht per kg is added to all Grade A leaf delivered by a farmer in a payment period
when at least 90 % of that farmer's net weight in the period is Grade A. The bonus does not apply to
Grade B or C leaf.
Payment is made twice a month by bank transfer to the account registered under section 2. Leaf
delivered from the 1st to the 15th of a month is paid on the 20th of the same month; leaf delivered from

the 16th to the end of a month is paid on the 5th of the following month. If a payment day falls on a
weekend or bank holiday, payment is made on the next working day. Amounts below 500 baht in a
period may instead be collected in cash at the Outgrower Office on request.
7. Agrochemical use and no-pluck periods
Outgrowers may use only the crop-protection products and fertilisers listed in the Leaf Partner
Handbook, 2026 edition. Every application must be written in the spraying log in the farmer card booklet,
with the date, product and plot. Herbicides must not be used within 3 metres of tea bushes.
No plucking for 14 days after an approved insecticide or fungicide is applied.
No plucking for 7 days after a foliar fertiliser is applied.
The Factory sends random leaf samples to an independent laboratory for residue testing. If a sample
fails, the farmer's Leaf Partner number is suspended for 60 days and the leaf from that delivery is
destroyed without payment. A second failed test within 24 months leads to removal from the Register.
8. Responsibilities
Collection-point clerks weigh the leaf, apply tare and wet-leaf deductions, and issue receipts.
Graders sample and grade each delivery and decide on rejection at the collection point.
The Head of Leaf Intake, Mr Athit Jabu, trains and supervises graders, checks the calibration of all
scales every Monday, and carries out re-checks of disputed grades.
The Outgrower Liaison Manager, Ms Duangporn Saelee, approves registrations and renewals,
decides suspensions under section 7, and handles first-stage written appeals.
The Finance Section makes payments and corrects payment errors within 10 working days of being
notified.
The Factory Manager, Mr Kittipong Thammawong, decides final appeals. His decision closes the
matter within the Factory.
9. Disputes and appeals
A farmer who disagrees with a grade, a deduction or a rejection should follow these steps:
1. Before leaving the collection point, ask the grader for a re-check. The disputed leaf is set aside, not
mixed with other deliveries, and a second 200 g sample is taken. At village points the re-check is
done by the Head of Leaf Intake or his deputy by telephone video call.
2. If the farmer still disagrees, submit written appeal form PMK-F7 at the Outgrower Office within 3
working days of the delivery, attaching the receipt.
3. The Outgrower Liaison Manager replies in writing within 5 working days.
4. If the farmer is not satisfied with that reply, a final appeal may be lodged with the Factory Manager
within 7 days of receiving it.
A grade cannot be changed once the leaf has been mixed with other deliveries, so a farmer who leaves
without asking for a re-check may appeal only against weighing or payment errors.

Step-by-Step Guide to the Shared Sample Roast
Room
Pang Khon Ridge Coffee Growers' Association, Mueang Chiang Rai · Ref. PKR-GD-11, version 2 · Issued 14
September 2026
The Association's Sample Roast Room (Room B3, ground floor of the Association building in Ban Pang
Khon) lets member farmers roast small samples of their own green coffee and have them cupped before
they agree a sale price with a buyer. It replaces version 1 of August 2025.
1. Before you book
Membership. Only members whose dues for the 2026/27 season are paid may book. Annual dues
are 1,200 baht and are due by 31 October 2026. The Treasurer keeps the list of paid-up members
and the Steward checks it before confirming a booking.
Induction. Every user must complete the Roast Room Induction before the first booking. The
induction lasts 2 hours and is held on the first Saturday of each month at 9:00. It remains valid for 24
months.
Green coffee condition. Beans must be hulled and hand-sorted, with stones and husk removed.
Moisture content must be between 10.0% and 12.0%. Test your lot on the moisture meter at the
reception desk; the test is free. Lots above 12.0% are refused and must be dried further. Until 31
August 2026 the upper limit was 12.5%.
2. Booking a slot
Book through the LINE group "PKR Roast Room" or in the paper booking book at reception, at least 2
days before the slot. The room is open Tuesday to Saturday. Each slot lasts 90 minutes and starts at
8:30, 10:00, 13:00 or 14:30. A member may hold at most 2 slots per calendar week. During the harvest
peak, from 1 December to 28 February, the limit is 1 slot per member per week so that more farmers can
use the room.
The drum sample roaster (unit SR-1) takes batches of 300 g to 1 kg of green coffee. Use of the roaster
costs 60 baht per batch; until 30 June 2026 the charge was 45 baht per batch. Cupping by the Head
Cupper costs 150 baht per sample. Charges are added to your member account and deducted from your
next parchment or green coffee payment. Cancel at least 24 hours before the slot; a late cancellation or a
no-show is charged 100 baht.
3. On roast day, step by step
1. Sign in with the Roast Room Steward. The Steward opens the main gas valve and lights the pilot
flame. Members never open or close the main gas valve themselves.
2. Weigh each batch of green coffee on the bench scale and write the lot code (farm code, picking
date), the batch weight and the moisture reading in the Roast Log.
3. Preheat the SR-1 for 20 minutes until the drum reaches the charge temperature of 200 °C.

4. Charge the beans and watch the colour. First crack usually starts after 9 to 10 minutes. For a sample
roast, drop the beans 1 minute 30 seconds to 2 minutes after first crack begins.
5. Drop the beans into the cooling tray and keep the stirring arm running until they are cool to the touch,
within 4 minutes.
6. Empty the chaff collector after every batch. This is the member's job, not the Steward's.
7. Weigh the roasted beans and record the weight loss in the Roast Log. A normal sample roast loses
13% to 16% of its green weight; batches that lose more than 18% are flagged for the Head Cupper.
8. Bag each batch and label it with the lot code, roast date and your member number.
Chaff fire. If smoke comes from the chaff collector, switch off the burner, keep the drum turning, do
not open the collector, and call the Steward at once. The extinguisher hangs beside the door. A
member involved in a chaff fire must repeat the induction before the next booking.
At the end of each day the Steward checks the chaff collector and closes the gas. Every Friday after the
last slot the Steward also cleans the roaster's chimney and exhaust fan, so the 14:30 Friday slot ends at
15:30 instead of 16:00.
4. Cupping your samples
Rest roasted samples for at least 8 hours and no more than 72 hours before cupping. Cupping sessions
are held every Thursday at 13:30. Leave 100 g of each sample on the Cupping Shelf in Room B3 by
16:00 on the Wednesday before. Each member may submit up to 4 samples per session; extra samples
wait for the following week.
The Head Cupper scores each sample on the Association's 100-point cupping form. Results are placed
in your pigeonhole and posted in the LINE group by 12:00 on Friday. A lot that scores 84 points or more
may be put forward for the Association's Ridge Reserve buyer list; lots scoring 80 to 83.75 points are
listed as Ridge Select. The Head Cupper decides which lots are put forward.
5. Taking coffee home and clearing up
The room is for samples only. A member may take home up to 2 kg of roasted coffee per calendar
month for household use. Coffee roasted in the room may not be sold; commercial roasting is
booked separately through the Marketing Office.
Remove all your green and roasted coffee on the day. Anything left in the room after 16:30 is moved
to the lost-and-found shelf at reception and thrown away after 7 days.
6. Who to contact
Malai Mueangkham, Roast Room Steward (ext. 213): bookings, gas, cleaning, equipment faults
and the Roast Log.
Anucha Saiyalak, Head Cupper (ext. 215): cupping sessions, scores, flagged batches and Ridge
Reserve recommendations.
Sudarat Wongkhiao, Treasurer (ext. 202): dues, account statements and disputes about roast or
cupping charges. Disputes must be raised within 30 days of the statement date.

Driving to Laos or Malaysia: Border Pass Questions
Wheelguard Motor Insurance PCL · Help article MC-114, version 3 · Updated 14 September 2026
The Wheelguard Border Pass extends a Wheelguard private car policy so that the insured vehicle keeps
its cover while it is driven in Laos or in Malaysia. It applies to Class 1 and Class 2+ policies only. Class 3
policies cannot be extended.
1. Which countries and roads are covered?
The Border Pass covers the whole of Laos and Peninsular Malaysia. Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore are
not covered, even if you enter them by road from Peninsular Malaysia.
2. How do I buy a Border Pass?
1. Log in to the Wheelguard app and open My Policy > Travel Abroad, or call 02-118-4460.
2. Choose the country, the travel dates and the border checkpoint you will use.
3. Upload a photo of the vehicle registration book.
4. Pay by card or PromptPay. The bilingual certificate is emailed within 2 hours; print it and keep it in the
car.
You must buy the pass at least 3 working days before departure. Requests made later are accepted only
for travel to Laos through the Nong Khai checkpoint, where same-day issue is available until 15:00.
3. How much does it cost?
For Laos the price is 180 baht per day. For Malaysia it is 260 baht per day. Any period of 15 days or
longer is charged at a flat 30-day rate of 3,900 baht for Laos or 5,600 baht for Malaysia. Until 31 August
2026 the Laos daily price was 150 baht; passes bought before that date keep the old price.
4. What excess do I pay for a claim abroad?
A fixed excess of 3,000 baht applies to each own-damage claim made outside Thailand, in addition to
any excess already shown on your Thai policy schedule. Third-party bodily injury claims have no excess.
Windscreen-only claims abroad have an excess of 1,000 baht.
Note. If the driver is under 25 years old, the excess for an own-damage claim abroad rises to 5,000
baht.
5. What should I do after an accident abroad?
Call the Wheelguard 24-hour line, +66 2 118 4499, before moving the vehicle unless it is unsafe. Get a
police report from the local police station and take photos of all vehicles. Send the police report and
photos through the app within 7 days of returning to Thailand. Repairs abroad are paid only if
Wheelguard approves the repair quote in writing first; otherwise the car is repaired at a Wheelguard
garage in Thailand.

Minutes of Clinical Services Committee Meeting
No. 9/2026
Hillward Counselling Service, Nan · Ref. HCS-CSC-09/2026 · Meeting held 24 September 2026 · Minutes
approved for circulation 1 October 2026
Venue and time: Room 204, Hillward House, Nan town, 13:30–16:10.
Present: Dr. Siriporn Wongkham (Clinical Director, chair); Ratree Saengdao (Senior Counsellor and
Safeguarding Lead); Pakorn Inthajak (Field Room Coordinator); Wilai Chaiyasit (Finance and
Administration Manager); Duangporn Mahawong (Counsellor, adolescent team); Nattapong Sukjai
(trainee counsellors’ representative); Kanokwan Thammachak (Office Manager, minutes).
Apologies: Dr. Chalerm Boonprasert (visiting psychiatrist), who sent a written comment on item 6.
1. Previous minutes and matters arising
The minutes of Meeting No. 8/2026 (27 August 2026) were approved with one correction: item 4 should
read that the evening clinic closes at 20:00, not 20:30.
2. Waiting list report
Kanokwan Thammachak reported 212 people on the waiting list on 19 September 2026, up from 168 at
the end of June. The median wait from referral to first appointment is now 41 days for adults and 23 days
for clients under 18, who keep priority. The service target remains 28 days for adults.
To shorten waits, the committee agreed to open a Saturday single-session clinic at Hillward House
from 3 October 2026, 09:00–13:00, staffed by two qualified counsellors on a rota. Each Saturday offers 8
booked single sessions of 50 minutes. People on the waiting list are offered these slots first, in order of
referral date. A single session does not remove a person from the waiting list unless they say they do not
need further counselling.
Note. The Saturday clinic is not a crisis service and does not take walk-in clients. People in crisis
continue to use the Hillward duty phone, which is staffed 08:00–22:00 every day.
3. Hillward Field Room: pilot review and extension
Pakorn Inthajak presented the review of the Field Room pilot, the mobile counselling van that ran from 6
May to 28 August 2026. The van provided 94 counselling sessions to 51 clients; 19 of them were farm
workers who said they could not travel to Nan town during the planting season.
The committee agreed to continue the Field Room permanently and to add two districts. The
schedule from October 2026 is:
Tha Wang Pha: first and third Tuesday of each month, car park of the Tha Wang Pha Morning Market,
10:00–16:00.
Pua: second and fourth Wednesday of each month, beside the Pua district community hall, 10:00–
16:00.

Chiang Klang: every Thursday from 5 November 2026, Wat Nong Bua Kham grounds, 11:00–16:00.
Song Khwae: first Friday of each month from 4 December 2026, Song Khwae village meeting hall,
10:00–15:00.
Bookings are made through the Hillward office or by telephone the day before; up to two places per van
day are kept for people who arrive without a booking. If the van cannot travel because of weather or a
breakdown, the office calls all booked clients by 08:30 and offers a phone session at the same time.
4. Session fees from 1 October 2026
Wilai Chaiyasit presented the fee review. Until 30 September 2026 a standard individual session cost 600
baht. The committee approved the following fees from 1 October 2026:
First assessment session (60 minutes): 300 baht.
Standard individual session (50 minutes): 700 baht.
Couple or family session (75 minutes): 1,100 baht.
Reduced fee: 150 baht per session for students and for clients with a monthly household income
below 12,000 baht, on showing a student card or completing the income declaration form FD-1.
Saturday single sessions: 200 baht for everyone.
Field Room sessions remain free of charge until 31 December 2026, funded by the Nan Riverbend
Community Fund grant. The committee will decide in December whether to charge the reduced fee in
2027. Clients already in a course of sessions before 1 October 2026 keep the old price of 600 baht until
that course ends or until 31 January 2027, whichever is earlier.
A missed session without 24 hours’ notice is charged at half the session fee. The charge is waived for a
first missed session, for illness with any written note, and for any Field Room session.
5. Safety concerns during Field Room sessions
Ratree Saengdao reported one incident in July, when a client disclosed thoughts of ending his life at the
end of a van session and the counsellor was unsure whom to contact. No harm occurred, but the
committee agreed that the van needs a written procedure because it operates up to 80 km from Hillward
House. The committee adopted the following procedure, effective immediately:
1. When a client shows signs of serious risk to self or others, the counsellor completes the short risk
screen (form RS-2) with the client before the session ends.
2. If the screen shows high risk, the counsellor stays with the client, or makes sure another trusted adult
does, and does not let the client leave the van alone.
3. The counsellor calls the Safeguarding Lead on the duty phone. If there is no answer within 10
minutes, the counsellor calls the Clinical Director.
4. The Safeguarding Lead or Clinical Director decides on the next step with the counsellor, such as a
same-day appointment with Dr. Boonprasert, contacting family with the client’s consent, or calling
emergency services.
5. The counsellor writes up the event on incident form IF-3 within 24 hours, and the Safeguarding Lead
phones the client within 48 hours to follow up.

6. Clinical supervision and trainee counsellors
Nattapong Sukjai asked for clearer rules on trainee placements. The committee confirmed that trainee
counsellors receive one hour of individual supervision for every six hours of client work, and qualified
counsellors receive at least two hours of supervision per month. Supervision notes are kept by the
supervisor, not in client records.
Trainees may work on the Field Room van only in a pair with a qualified counsellor who has at least two
years of practice after qualification. A trainee must never see a client on the van alone, even for a short
time; if the qualified partner is called away, the trainee pauses the session and waits. Trainees do not
take Saturday single sessions, which are reserved for qualified counsellors. In his written comment, Dr.
Boonprasert supported these limits and offered one case discussion per month for trainees, starting in
November.
7. Client records from the van
The van has no reliable mobile signal in parts of Chiang Klang and Song Khwae, so session notes are
sometimes written on paper. The committee agreed that paper notes are kept in the locked document
box in the van and scanned into the client record system within two working days of the van day. The
Office Manager checks each scan and then shreds the paper copy. Notes must not be stored on
personal phones, and the van tablet must not keep offline copies of notes after the end of the van day.
8. Interpreters
Hmong and Mien interpreters from the Hillward interpreter list must be booked at least five working days
before the session. Interpreters sign the confidentiality agreement every year. Family members may
interpret only when no listed interpreter is available and the client asks for it in writing; a child under 16
may never interpret for a client, and a family member may never interpret in a session that concerns
family violence.
9. Any other business
The service will close on Saturday 14 November 2026 for the annual staff wellbeing day; no Saturday
clinic will run that day, and the duty phone will be covered by Ratree Saengdao.
10. Action points
Publish the new fee list on the website and at reception by 30 September 2026: Wilai Chaiyasit.
Print form RS-2 and the safety procedure for the van door card, and brief all van staff by 10 October
2026: Ratree Saengdao.
Agree the Chiang Klang site with Wat Nong Bua Kham and announce the new schedule by 20
October 2026: Pakorn Inthajak.
Set up the Saturday clinic rota for October to December: Dr. Siriporn Wongkham.
