Cash, Coin and Damaged Banknote Deposit Rules
Kaewsiri Savings Bank · Ref. KSB-DEP-11, version 4 · Effective 1 December 2026
1. Purpose and scope
These rules explain how Kaewsiri Savings Bank accepts cash paid into savings and deposit accounts at
its 46 branches in northern and northeastern Thailand and at its cash deposit machines. They apply to
Everyday Savings accounts, Junior Saver accounts, Fixed Deposit accounts funded in cash, and
business savings accounts. They replace version 3 of 15 January 2025. Deposits by cheque, by bank
transfer and through the mobile app are covered by separate rules (KSB-DEP-04).
The rules are owned by the Head of Branch Operations, Wanpen Sukhawadee. Damaged banknotes that
cannot be valued at a branch are assessed by the Khon Kaen Cash Centre, managed by Thanakorn
Ruangsri.
2. Terms used in these rules
Business day: Monday to Friday, except Thai public holidays and bank holidays announced by
Kaewsiri Savings Bank.
Cut-off time: the time after which a counter deposit is given the value date of the next business day.
Interest on savings accounts is calculated from the value date.
Loose coins: coins brought in jars, boxes or plastic bags that the bank must sort and count.
Bagged coins: coins of one denomination in the bank's free clear coin bags, sealed and labelled
with the account number and the number of coins.
Third-party depositor: any person paying cash into an account that is not their own and of which
they are not a joint holder or registered guardian.
3. Cash deposits at the counter
Customers fill in deposit slip KSB-D1 or give the account number to the teller, who counts the cash in
front of the customer and prints a receipt.
Cut-off time on business days: 15:30. Cash deposited after 15:30 is credited at once but carries the
value date of the next business day.
Saturday branches: the 9 branches inside shopping centres open on Saturdays from 10:00 to 17:00.
Saturday deposits carry the value date of the following Monday, or of the next business day if
Monday is a holiday.
All banknote denominations and all Thai coins are accepted at the counter, subject to the coin rules
in section 5.
4. Cash deposit machines
Cash deposit machines accept 100, 500 and 1,000 baht notes only. Notes of 20 and 50 baht, coins and
damaged notes must be paid in at a counter. Each machine transaction takes up to 100 notes, and a

single card or account number can deposit up to 200,000 baht per calendar day through all machines
together. Until 30 November 2026 this daily limit was 100,000 baht.
Machine deposits made between 06:00 and 22:00 receive the same day's value date; deposits made
between 22:00 and 06:00 receive the next calendar day's value date. Notes that the machine cannot read
are returned to the customer at the end of the transaction. A note that the machine identifies as possibly
counterfeit is kept, and the machine prints a retention slip. The branch that owns the machine contacts
the customer within 3 business days with the result of the check. Notes found to be genuine are credited
with the original value date; counterfeit notes are handed to the police and no value is paid.
5. Coin deposits
5.1 Free allowance and fees
Each customer may deposit up to 500 loose coins per day free of charge. For loose coins above 500, a
counting fee of 2 % of the value of all the coins in the deposit is charged, with a minimum of 20 baht.
Bagged coins are always counted free of charge, whatever the number, provided each bag holds a single
denomination and the label is correct. Standard bag sizes are 500 coins of 1 baht, 200 coins of 5 baht
and 200 coins of 10 baht; 2-baht coins go in 1-baht bags but must not be mixed with 1-baht coins.
Junior Saver account holders aged under 15 pay no counting fee on loose coins of up to 3,000 coins per
visit. Above 3,000 coins in one visit, the normal 2 % fee applies to the whole deposit.
5.2 Large coin deposits
Deposits of more than 2,000 coins, whether loose or bagged, must be booked at least 1 business day in
advance with the branch, and can only be made at the three branches with coin-sorting machines: Khon
Kaen Mittraphap, Udon Thani Pho Si and Nakhon Ratchasima Mukkhamontri. Other branches accept up
to 2,000 coins per customer per day. Large coin deposits may be left at the branch against a sealed-bag
receipt; they are then counted and credited by the end of the next business day.
Coins of 25 and 50 satang are accepted up to a total value of 100 baht per deposit. Bent, corroded or
foreign coins are returned to the customer.
6. Damaged banknotes
Damaged notes can be paid into a Kaewsiri account but cannot be exchanged for cash over the counter.
The teller values a note on the spot when its condition is clear:
Torn, taped, written on, faded or slightly discoloured notes with more than 75 % of the note present:
full value.
Notes with more than 50 % and up to 75 % present, where at least one serial number can be read:
half value.
Notes with 50 % or less present: no value at the branch; the customer may ask for a Cash Centre
assessment.
Notes that are burnt, glued together, stuck in a block, eaten by insects or termites, or contaminated with
chemicals, mould or oil are not valued at the branch. The teller seals them in a pouch with Form KSB-
DN3, gives the customer a copy and sends the pouch to the Khon Kaen Cash Centre. The Cash Centre
gives its decision within 15 business days of receiving the pouch and credits the value directly to the

account named on the form; the result is sent by SMS and by letter. Assessment is free, except that
contaminated notes carry a handling fee of 300 baht per pouch, deducted from the amount credited.
Each customer may hand in up to 20 damaged notes per calendar month at branches. Larger quantities,
for example after a house fire or flood, are accepted by appointment directly at the Khon Kaen Cash
Centre, open Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 15:00.
Note. Do not try to separate, wash, iron or dry burnt or wet notes yourself. Put them in a firm box or
a sealed plastic bag as they are and bring them to the branch.
7. Large and third-party cash deposits
A source-of-funds declaration on Form KSB-SF2 is needed when a single cash deposit, or several cash
deposits on the same business day into one account, reach 500,000 baht or more. The form records
where the cash came from and the depositor's relationship to the account holder. Business savings
accounts with a completed Business Cash Profile that has been reviewed in the last 12 months have a
higher threshold of 2,000,000 baht per day. Until the profile review is completed, the 500,000 baht
threshold applies to business accounts as well.
Third-party depositors are welcome, with these limits:
A third-party depositor paying in more than 50,000 baht must show a Thai ID card or passport, and
the teller records the name on the receipt.
Third-party deposits into a Junior Saver account are limited to 10,000 baht per day. The registered
guardian has no limit.
Accounts marked dormant (no customer-initiated transaction for 24 months) cannot receive third-
party cash. The account holder must reactivate the account in person with ID before any cash is
accepted.
8. Counting differences and complaints
If cash left at a branch or a machine is later found to differ from the amount on the receipt, the branch
corrects the account within 5 business days and informs the customer by SMS, with the count record
available on request. A customer who disagrees with a count, a coin fee or a damaged note valuation
may ask for a review within 30 days of the deposit. Reviews are carried out by the branch manager, who
checks the camera recording and the count record and replies in writing within 10 business days. If the
customer is still not satisfied, the case is passed to Branch Operations, whose decision is final within the
bank.
Questions about these rules can be raised at any branch, through the Contact Centre on 043 255 900
(daily 07:00 to 21:00), or by letter to Branch Operations, Kaewsiri Savings Bank, 88 Na Mueang Road,
Khon Kaen 40000.

How to Borrow Tents, Chairs and Sound Equipment
for a Household Ceremony
Don Sawan Kham Town Municipality, Maha Sarakham · Ruam Jai Ceremony Equipment Loan Service · Guide
CS-G-2026-07 · Issued 1 October 2026
The Ruam Jai Ceremony Equipment Loan Service lends municipal tents, chairs, tables and a portable
sound system to households holding a funeral, ordination, wedding, housewarming or merit-making
ceremony at home. This guide replaces guide CS-G-2024-03 and applies to bookings made from 1
October 2026.
1. Who may borrow
Any household whose address is in the house registration of one of the 13 communities of Don Sawan
Kham Town Municipality may borrow equipment. The person who signs the booking must be at least 20
years old and listed in that house registration. Temples and schools book through the Community
Development Section instead. Households outside the municipality, including those in the neighbouring
Don Sawan subdistrict, are not eligible.
Each household may make up to 2 non-funeral bookings per calendar year. Funeral bookings do not
count towards this limit.
2. What you can borrow
One booking may include up to 6 tents (4 × 8 metres, with side curtains), 200 plastic chairs, 20 folding
tables, 4 standing fans and 1 portable sound system with two microphones. Lighting, generators and
cooking equipment are not lent.
3. Charges and deposit
Funeral bookings are free of charge, including delivery and setting up, and no deposit is required. For all
other ceremonies the charges per booking are:
Tent: 300 baht each (200 baht until 30 September 2026).
Plastic chair 3 baht, folding table 20 baht, standing fan 50 baht each; sound system 500 baht.
Delivery, setting up and collection by the municipal crew: 400 baht.
Refundable deposit: 1,000 baht, returned in cash after the inspection on collection.
Households may fetch chairs, tables and fans themselves to avoid the delivery charge, but tents are only
put up by the municipal crew, so any booking with a tent pays it.
4. Step-by-step booking
1. Check availability for your dates by calling the equipment store on 043 771 245, or on the
municipality's LINE account under "Ruam Jai".
2. Complete form CS-12 at the Citizen Service Counter, Room 104, ground floor of the municipal office,
Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 16:30. Bring your ID card and a copy of your house registration.

3. Book at least 7 days before the first day of use and no more than 60 days ahead.
4. Pay the charges and deposit at the cashier in Room 106. Your receipt number starts with "RJ-";
quote it in every later call.
5. The crew delivers and sets up the equipment on the day before your ceremony, between 13:00 and
17:00. An adult from the household must be present to sign the delivery checklist.
5. Funerals: booking at short notice
For a funeral, the 7-day rule does not apply. Call the duty phone 089 552 1180, which is answered 24
hours a day including weekends and public holidays. If equipment is in store, the crew sets it up within 6
hours of the call. Form CS-12 and a copy of the death notification certificate must then be handed in at
Room 104 within 3 working days after delivery.
6. Loan periods and late return
Equipment for non-funeral ceremonies may be kept for up to 3 days, counted from the day of delivery.
Funeral equipment may be kept for up to 7 days and extended once by a further 3 days, by calling the
duty phone before the seventh day ends. Equipment kept longer than allowed is charged a late fee of
100 baht per tent per day and 1 baht per chair per day, deducted from the deposit or, for funerals,
invoiced to the household.
7. Damage and loss
The crew and the borrower check the equipment together on collection and both sign the return
checklist. Missing or damaged items are charged as follows: a lost or broken plastic chair costs 250
baht, a broken folding table 900 baht, a damaged microphone 1,200 baht, and a torn tent canopy is
charged at the actual repair cost quoted by the equipment store. Funeral bookings pay the same damage
charges.
Note. If you disagree with a damage charge, write your objection on the return checklist before
signing it and ask for a review within 7 days. Charges accepted without a written objection cannot be
reviewed later.
8. When a booking may be refused or moved
Municipal events take priority. No non-funeral bookings are accepted from 12 to 16 April (Songkran)
or during the Don Sawan Kham Rocket Festival weekend in May.
If the Disaster Prevention Unit issues a strong wind warning, the crew will not put up tents, and you
may move your booking to a new date without charge.
9. Contacts and responsibilities
Ms. Waraporn Sitthiwong, Head of the Citizen Service Counter, is responsible for bookings, receipts and
complaints about the service. Mr. Somkiat Phanwilai, Equipment Store Supervisor, is responsible for
delivery times, the condition of equipment, damage assessments and damage reviews.

Shellnight 2026–27: Your Guide to Turtle Nesting
Season
Sai Kaew Thong Beach Resort, Khao Lak, Phang Nga · Guest leaflet GX-LF-2026-09 · Issued 15 October 2026
1. Welcome to Shellnight
Every year sea turtles come ashore on the 1.8 km beach in front of Sai Kaew Thong Beach Resort to lay
their eggs. Shellnight is the resort's guest programme for the nesting season. It explains how the beach
changes after dark, what we ask of every guest, and the turtle activities you can join during your stay.
This leaflet is placed in every room and villa and is also available at the Reef Desk in the main lobby.
The 2026–27 Shellnight season runs from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027. Most nests are laid
between December and February, and most hatchlings emerge between February and April. Last season
our patrol team recorded 31 nests and 2,140 hatchlings reaching the sea, the highest numbers since the
programme began in 2019.
The programme is led by the resort naturalist, Thanakorn Wisetsri, together with a team of six night patrol
staff. Guest-facing arrangements, bookings and complaints are handled by the Guest Experience
Manager, Pimchanok Saelim.
2. Which turtles nest here
Two species use our beach. Olive ridley turtles make up most nests. They are small (about 65 cm shell
length), usually arrive between 21:00 and 02:00, and spend around 45 minutes on the sand. Green turtles
are less frequent visitors, with three nests last season. They are much larger and can spend up to two
hours digging and covering a nest.
A female digs a body pit, lays around 100 eggs in a flask-shaped chamber and covers it before returning
to the sea. Eggs incubate in the warm sand for roughly 50 to 60 days.
Nesting turtles are easily disturbed. A turtle that sees light, movement or people near the water will often
turn back without laying, and may then lay her eggs in the sea, where they are lost. Hatchlings find the
sea by heading towards the brightest horizon. Lights from rooms, phones or torches can lead them
inland, where they die of heat or are taken by crabs and dogs. The rules in this leaflet are designed
around these two facts.
3. Beach quiet hours and lighting
During the season the beach and all beach-facing areas follow quiet hours from 19:00 to 05:30 every
night. Until last season quiet hours began at 20:00; the earlier start was introduced after the patrol team
recorded several turtles arriving before 20:00 in 2025–26.
During quiet hours:
Path and garden lights on the beach side switch automatically to low amber lamps at 19:00.
Beachfront Pool Villas (villas B01 to B24) and Sea View Deluxe rooms on floors 1 and 2 of the Ocean
Wing must keep their beach-facing curtains closed while lights are on inside. Terrace lights must stay
off; each terrace has a red-light lantern for use after 19:00.

Torches, phone lights and camera flashes may not be used on the sand. The Reef Desk lends red-
filter torches free of charge against your room key.
The Driftwood Beach Bar stops serving on the sand at 19:00 and continues on its raised deck until
22:00. Outside the season the bar serves on the sand until 23:00.
Sun loungers and umbrellas are stacked behind the dune line by 18:30 so that turtles have a clear
path.
Note. The Lagoon Pool on the garden side is not part of the quiet-hours zone and keeps its normal
opening hours until 22:00. The Beach Pool closes at 18:30 during the season instead of 20:00.
4. If you see a turtle on the beach
Turtles may come ashore anywhere along the beach, including right in front of the villas. If you see a
turtle, or tracks that look like a tractor tyre leading up from the water, please follow these steps:
1. Stop where you are and stay low. Keep at least 15 metres away from the turtle and never stand
between her and the sea.
2. Switch off every light, including phone screens. Do not take photographs at this stage.
3. Note the number of the nearest white beach marker post. Posts are numbered S1 to S18 from the
southern rocks to the river mouth.
4. Call the Shellnight Turtle Line on room extension 7700, or 076 488 270 from a mobile phone. The line
is staffed from 18:00 to 06:00 throughout the season.
5. Wait quietly at your position until a patrol member arrives, normally within 10 minutes. The patrol
member will tell you whether you may stay and watch.
Once a turtle has started laying she is less sensitive, and the patrol member may invite you to watch from
behind her using a red light. Please do not touch the turtle, the eggs or the tracks. After she has returned
to the sea the patrol marks the nest with a bamboo fence and a numbered sign.
Note. If you find a turtle that is injured, tangled in netting or stranded during the day, call the Turtle
Line straight away even outside its staffed hours. Calls between 06:00 and 18:00 are forwarded to
the Reef Desk, which can reach the naturalist at any time.
5. Shellnight activities
Night Nest Walk
A guided walk along the beach with a patrol member, looking for nesting turtles and checking marked
nests. Walks run on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays at 20:30 and last about 90 minutes. Each walk
is limited to 12 guests. The price is 650 baht per adult and 350 baht per child aged 8 to 12. The minimum
age is 8 years, because the walk takes place in near-total darkness and requires guests to stay silent for
long periods. Children aged 8 to 12 must be accompanied by a participating adult. Sightings cannot be
guaranteed: last season a nesting turtle was seen on 38 % of walks.

Hatchling release
When a marked nest begins to hatch, the patrol team guides the hatchlings safely to the water and
invites guests to watch from a roped line. Releases usually happen at dusk or before dawn and are
announced with no more than three hours' notice. To be called, add your name and room number to the
Hatchling List at the Reef Desk; the desk will phone your room. Releases are free and open to guests of
all ages, including young children, provided they stay behind the rope with an adult. Guests may not
handle hatchlings.
Nest Talk
A 45-minute illustrated talk by Thanakorn Wisetsri on turtle biology and the work of the patrol, held every
Wednesday at 17:00 in the Lagoon Room. Free, no booking needed, suitable for all ages.
6. Booking and cancellation
Night Nest Walks can be booked at the Reef Desk (open 08:00 to 20:00), through the resort app, or by
calling extension 7710. Bookings close at 18:00 on the day of the walk. The fee is charged to your room
account at the time of booking.
Guests who cancel before 15:00 on the day of the walk receive a full refund. Cancellations between
15:00 and 18:00 are refunded at 50 %, and no refund is given for cancellations after 18:00 or for guests
who do not arrive at the meeting point. If the resort cancels a walk because of heavy rain, high surf or
lightning, booked guests are offered either a full refund or a free place on the next available walk during
their stay. A guest who arrives late after the group has left cannot join that walk, as the group cannot
return to the start without disturbing the beach.
Note. Guests with a medical certificate showing illness on the day are refunded in full whatever the
time of cancellation. Please show the certificate at the Reef Desk within 24 hours.
7. Other beach rules during the season
No beach fires, lanterns or fireworks at any time, including at private villa events.
Holes dug in the sand must be filled in and sandcastles flattened before 18:00, as hatchlings can
become trapped.
Drones may not be flown over the beach between 18:00 and 06:00.
Kayaks and paddleboards are available as usual from 08:00 to 17:30 but must not be landed inside a
fenced nest area.
Dogs belonging to guests are not permitted on the beach during the season.
Private beach dinners are still available but move to the Driftwood deck after 19:00.
8. Contacts
Shellnight Turtle Line: extension 7700, or 076 488 270 (18:00 to 06:00)
Reef Desk, main lobby: extension 7710 (08:00 to 20:00)
Guest Experience Manager, Pimchanok Saelim: guest.experience@saikaewthong.example

Guide to Handing Over Completed Community
Projects to Village Committees
Muan Chon Rural Development Foundation, Nan Field Office · Ref. MCF-OPS-G12, version 2 · Issued 14
September 2026
This guide explains, step by step, how a project built with Muan Chon funding is handed over to the
village that will own and run it. It applies to every community project in Mae Charim, Wiang Sa and Na
Noi districts of Nan province whose construction is completed on or after 1 October 2026. Projects
completed before 1 October 2026 follow version 1 of this guide, except for the defects period in Step 6,
which now applies to all projects.
1. Who does what
Project Field Officer: the Muan Chon staff member who supervised construction. Prepares the
readiness checklist and the list of assets.
Handover Officer: Kanok Wongpradit, Nan Field Office. Schedules the joint inspection, chairs it, and
signs the Handover Record for the foundation. No project may be handed over without the Handover
Officer's signature.
Village Asset Committee: the group elected by villagers to own, operate and maintain the asset
after handover.
Finance Unit: led by Rattiya Chaimongkol. Transfers the foundation's contribution to the
maintenance fund and checks fund statements at follow-up visits.
Technical Reviewer: a registered engineer contracted by the foundation. Must attend the joint
inspection for any footbridge, whatever its cost, and for any other project whose construction cost is
above 500,000 baht.
2. Step 1: Confirm the project is ready
At least 60 days before the planned handover date, the Project Field Officer completes the readiness
checklist (form MCF-HR-1) and sends it to the Handover Officer. The checklist confirms that construction
is finished, that the contractor's final invoice has been approved, that the asset has run for at least 14
consecutive days without a fault (water systems and pumps only), and that operating manuals in Thai are
available. If any item is missing, the Handover Officer returns the checklist within 5 working days with a
list of what must be completed.
3. Step 2: Form the Village Asset Committee and open the maintenance fund
3.1 Committee
Villagers elect the committee at an open village meeting. The committee must have at least 5 and no
more than 9 members, and at least 2 members must be women. The village headman may sit on the
committee but may not be its chair or its treasurer. The committee chooses a chair, a treasurer and at
least two caretakers from among its members.

3.2 Maintenance fund
Before handover, the committee opens a savings account in the name of the village committee at any
bank branch, with two signatories who are not related to each other. The fund starts with two deposits:
Foundation deposit: 5% of the final construction cost, up to a maximum of 40,000 baht per project.
Until 30 June 2026 the deposit was 3% of the construction cost, capped at 25,000 baht.
Village deposit: at least 100 baht per household served, or 10,000 baht, whichever is higher. The
village may collect it in cash, in kind (sold produce) or through a village fund loan.
The Finance Unit transfers the foundation deposit only after the bank has confirmed receipt of the full
village deposit. Rice banks are an exception: their village deposit may be made as paddy (at least 1
tonne) instead of cash, recorded in the rice bank ledger.
4. Step 3: Hold the joint inspection
The joint inspection is a public walk-through of the finished asset by the committee, villagers, the
Handover Officer and, where required, the Technical Reviewer. Announce it on the village loudspeaker
and the village notice board at least 7 days in advance.
The inspection is valid only if villagers from enough households attend: at least 30% of the households
served, or 40 households, whichever number is lower. Each household counts once, however many
members attend. If attendance is too low, the Handover Officer postpones the inspection and sets a new
date within 21 days. If the second inspection also fails to reach the attendance threshold, the case is
referred to the district coordinator, who decides whether to proceed with a smaller meeting.
4.1 Classifying defects
Every defect found is written on the inspection sheet (form MCF-HR-2) and given one category:
Category A (safety or function): anything that could injure a person or stops the asset from working,
such as a loose handrail or a leaking main pipe. Must be repaired and re-checked before the
Handover Record is signed.
Category B (minor function): problems that reduce performance but do not stop use, such as a
slow-filling tank or a door that does not lock. The contractor must repair them within 90 days after
handover.
Category C (cosmetic): paint, small cracks in plaster, signage. Recorded only; repair is up to the
committee.
Note. If the Technical Reviewer and the committee disagree on the category of a defect, the higher
category applies until the Handover Officer has decided in writing.
5. Step 4: Train the committee
Before handover, the Project Field Officer runs at least 2 training sessions of 3 hours each on operation,
simple repairs, record keeping and the use of the maintenance fund. At least two caretakers must attend
both sessions. For water systems and solar pumps, the caretakers must also pass a practical test, after

which they receive a caretaker certificate valid for 3 years. A water project cannot be handed over until at
least one caretaker holds a valid certificate.
6. Step 5: Sign the Handover Record
The Handover Record (form MCF-HR-3) is signed in three copies: one for the committee, one for the Nan
Field Office and one for the district office. It is signed by the committee chair, the committee treasurer
and the Handover Officer; the village headman signs as a witness. At the signing the committee receives
the keys, the operating manuals, the spare parts list, the contractor's contact details and a copy of the
inspection sheet. Ownership and day-to-day responsibility pass to the committee on the date of signing.
7. Step 6: The defects period
For 12 months after the Handover Record is signed, Muan Chon arranges and pays for the repair of any
construction defect that the committee reports. For footbridges this period is 24 months. The defects
period does not cover:
damage caused by misuse, unauthorised changes or lack of the routine maintenance described in
the manual;
flood damage when the water level rose above the design level written in the Handover Record;
theft or vandalism, and parts that wear out normally, such as taps, filters and fuses.
Report a defect to the Nan Field Office hotline (054 710 386, Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 16:30) or the
foundation's LINE account within 7 days of noticing it, with photographs. The field office replies within 3
working days. If a water system outage affects more than 20 households, the field office sends a
technician within 48 hours, including on weekends.
8. Step 7: Follow-up visits
The Project Field Officer visits the committee 3, 6 and 12 months after handover. At each visit the
committee shows its maintenance log, meeting notes and the latest bank statement of the maintenance
fund. If at the 12-month visit the fund balance is below 50% of its starting balance, the committee must
submit a written recovery plan to the Finance Unit within 30 days, for example a monthly household fee.
After the 12-month visit, Muan Chon support is limited to advice and training; the foundation does not
fund further repairs except within a footbridge's longer defects period.
9. Partial handover
A project with several separate parts, such as a water system serving two hamlets, may be handed over
one part at a time, but only if each part works independently of the others. Each part then has its own
Handover Record, joint inspection and defects period. The maintenance fund is opened once, with the
full deposits, before the first part is handed over.
10. Contacts
Handover Officer: Kanok Wongpradit, Nan Field Office, 88 Sumonthewarat Road, Nan.
Finance Unit: Rattiya Chaimongkol, finance.nan@muanchon.example.

Policy on Keeping Savings in the Fund after
Leaving Employment and Instalment Payouts
Banyen Ceramics Employees' Provident Fund · Ref. BCPF-POL-07, version 3 · Approved by the Fund
Committee on 18 November 2026 · Effective 1 January 2027
1. Purpose and scope
This policy explains what happens to the savings of a member of the Banyen Ceramics Employees'
Provident Fund (the "Fund") when the member stops working for Banyen Ceramics Co., Ltd. at its
Lampang plant or its Hang Chat glazing workshop. It replaces version 2 of 1 July 2024.
The Fund is managed by Saeng Prakai Fund Management Co., Ltd. (the "Fund Manager"). The member's
own contributions and their returns always belong to the member in full; the employer's share vests as
set out in section 3.
2. Choosing what to do with your balance
Every leaver must tell the Fund what to do with their balance by returning Form BC-PF5 ("Leaver's
Choice") within 45 days after the last working day. Until 31 December 2026 this period was 30 days. The
form offers four choices:
1. Lump-sum payout of the whole vested balance to the member's bank account.
2. Become a retained member and keep the whole vested balance invested in the Fund.
3. Transfer the balance to the provident fund of a new employer (section 6).
4. Instalment payout, for retirees only (section 5).
If no form is received by the 45th day, the Fund treats the leaver as having chosen option 2 for up to 12
months. After the 12 months the Fund pays the balance as a lump sum to the bank account on the
leaver's record.
A leaver may become a retained member only if the vested balance on the last working day is at least
20,000 baht. Smaller balances are paid as a lump sum within 30 days after the form is received or after
the 45-day period ends, whichever comes first.
3. Vesting of the employer's share
The vested part of the employer's share depends on the member's completed years of Fund
membership on the last working day:
Less than 3 years: 0 % of the employer's share.
3 years or more but less than 5 years: 50 %.
5 years or more: 100 %.
Retirement at age 55 or above, disability or death: 100 %, whatever the length of membership.
A member dismissed for serious misconduct under the company's work rules receives only the
member's share; they may still become a retained member if that share is at least 20,000 baht.

4. Retained membership
A retained member keeps the same investment plan and receives the same returns as working members,
but no new contributions can be paid in.
Maximum period: a member who leaves before age 55 may stay a retained member for up to 5
years after the last working day. A member who retires at 55 or above may stay until the end of the
year in which they turn 75.
Annual fee: 500 baht per year, deducted from the balance on 1 March. Retirees aged 55 or above
pay a reduced fee of 200 baht per year. No fee is charged in the calendar year of the last working
day.
Partial withdrawals: not allowed for members who left before age 55. They may only take the whole
balance at once or transfer it.
5. Instalment payouts for retirees
Members who retire at age 55 or above may ask for their balance to be paid in instalments using Form
BC-PF7. They may choose monthly, quarterly or yearly payments. Each payment must be at least 5,000
baht. The first payment is made on the 25th of the month after the form is approved.
A retiree may change the payment amount or frequency once per calendar year and may stop the
instalments at any time to take the remaining balance as a lump sum. When the remaining balance falls
below 5,000 baht, it is paid in full with the next payment.
6. Transfers to another provident fund
A leaver or retained member who joins a new employer with a registered provident fund may transfer the
whole vested balance there at any time during the retention period. The member sends Form BC-PF8
with a letter from the new fund confirming it will accept the transfer. The Fund Manager transfers the
money within 15 business days after receiving complete documents. The transfer is free of charge if it is
requested within 12 months after the last working day; a transfer requested later costs 300 baht.
7. Responsibilities
Fund Secretary, Thitima Boonrueang (HR Benefits Office, Room 214, Administration Building,
Lampang plant): gives Form BC-PF5 to every leaver at the exit interview, collects completed forms
and sends the last working day and years of membership to the Fund Manager within 5 business
days.
Member Services, Saeng Prakai Fund Management, led by Chanin Rattanaphol: keeps the
records of retained members, makes all payouts and transfers, and issues each retained member an
annual statement by 31 January.
Fund Committee, chaired by Orathai Wongkhiaw: decides on appeals. A member who disagrees
with a decision on vesting or payment may appeal in writing to the Fund Secretary within 60 days;
the Committee gives its decision within 30 days after receiving the appeal.

Living Next to the Cannery: Neighbour FAQ for the
2026/27 Winter Pineapple Season
Thung Pradu Canning Co., Ltd., Kui Buri, Prachuap Khiri Khan · Ref. TPC-COM-2026-07 · Issued 1 October
2026
This FAQ is for residents of Ban Thung Pradu, Ban Nong Hin, Ban Khao Lan and other households near
our factory on the Kui Buri–Thung Pradu road. It explains what changes during the winter pineapple
season, how to report a problem, and how to use the Thung Pradu Neighbour Fund and the free peel
scheme.
1. When is the winter season and what changes?
The winter season runs from Monday 2 November 2026 to Friday 15 January 2027. During these ten and
a half weeks the factory runs two shifts, from 05:00 to 13:00 and from 13:00 to 21:00, six days a week.
There is no production on Sundays. Outside the season we run one day shift only, from 07:00 to 16:00,
Monday to Friday.
2. Which roads will the fruit trucks use, and at what times?
All contracted fruit trucks must enter from Phetkasem Road (Route 4) by the new access road opened in
August 2026 and use Gate 1 only. Trucks may not drive through Ban Nong Hin village. Trucks may queue
on the access road from 04:30, and the weighbridge opens at 05:00. The last truck is accepted at the
weighbridge at 19:30.
Finished-goods trucks taking canned fruit to Laem Chabang port leave by Gate 2 between 08:00 and
18:00 only, so no container lorries pass the Ban Thung Pradu school during morning drop-off (07:00 to
08:00).
Note. Until the access road opened, trucks used the Ban Nong Hin road and were allowed to queue
from 03:30. That arrangement has ended. A truck seen in Ban Nong Hin, or queuing before 04:30, is
breaking its contract with us and should be reported (see question 4).
3. Why does the area smell during the season, and what are you doing about
it?
The smell comes mostly from peel and core that waits in the peel yard before it is taken away, and from
the first wastewater pond. For the winter season we have made three changes:
The peel yard is now emptied at least every 6 hours, instead of once per shift.
A roof and side screens have been added to the peel yard on the side facing Ban Khao Lan.
Two extra aerators have been installed in wastewater pond 1, bringing the total to six.

4. How do I report noise, smell or a truck problem?
You can contact the factory at any hour during the season. Please give the time, the place and, for a
truck, the number plate.
Neighbour hotline: 032 618 455, answered 24 hours a day from 2 November 2026 to 15 January
2027, and from 07:00 to 17:00 on weekdays at other times.
LINE: add the official account @tpcneighbour and send a message or photo.
During the season, a duty supervisor will call you back within 2 hours of a report made between 21:00
and 05:00, and within 1 hour at other times. Our Community Liaison Officer, Ms Wanphen Ratchamanee,
follows up every report in writing within 3 working days and explains what was done. A truck reported for
using the Ban Nong Hin road receives a written warning; after a second report in the same season the
transport company is suspended from deliveries for 7 days.
5. Who can apply to the Thung Pradu Neighbour Fund?
The Thung Pradu Neighbour Fund supports small household and community projects near the factory.
For 2027 the company has set aside 1,800,000 baht. Applications for the first round are open from 2
November to 30 November 2026, and decisions are announced on 15 January 2027.
Households: households whose house registration address is within 1.5 km of the factory boundary
may apply for up to 15,000 baht, once per year, for a home or livelihood project (for example window
screens or a water tank).
Community groups: village committees, temples, schools and registered community enterprises in
Thung Pradu Subdistrict may apply for up to 60,000 baht per project.
Note. Households living more than 1.5 km from the factory are also eligible if their house stands
within 200 m of the old Ban Nong Hin truck road, because they lived with truck traffic until August
2026. Until 2025 the household limit was 10,000 baht and the distance limit was 1 km.
Application forms are available at the Community Liaison Office and the subdistrict office. Each form
must be signed by the village head. Employees of Thung Pradu Canning and members of the fund
committee may not apply for a household grant.
6. Can I take pineapple peel for my animals?
Yes. Livestock farmers in Kui Buri District can collect fresh peel and core free of charge after registering
once at the Community Liaison Office with a copy of their ID card and their livestock registration. Each
registered farmer receives a yellow collection card.
Collection is at Gate 3, from 09:00 to 15:00, Monday to Saturday during the season.
Each card holder may take up to 400 kg per day, weighed at the Gate 3 scale.
Farmers must bring their own covered containers or a pick-up truck with a tarpaulin. Uncovered
loads are refused.
Peel must not be resold. A card used for resale is cancelled for the rest of the season.

VeilGrind Witnessed Destruction Service: Terms
and Conditions for Brand Owners
Thung Lung Polymer Reclaim Co., Ltd. · Hat Yai Plant, Songkhla · Ref. TLPR-TC-VG-03 · Version 3.0 ·
Effective 1 November 2026
1. Purpose and scope
VeilGrind is the witnessed destruction service of Thung Lung Polymer Reclaim Co., Ltd. It allows brand
owners, contract packers and importers to have branded plastic packaging and products destroyed so
that they can never return to the market. Typical consignments are misprinted labels and bottles, recalled
products after the contents have been removed, obsolete packaging after a brand redesign, and
preforms or caps carrying a logo. All material is shredded, washed and turned into unbranded regrind at
the Hat Yai plant on Kanchanavanich Road. These terms replace Version 2.4 of 15 January 2025 and
apply to every consignment that arrives at the plant on or after 1 November 2026.
VeilGrind does not accept hazardous waste, containers that held pesticides, solvents or engine oil, PVC
items, pharmaceutical blister packs that still contain tablets, or electronic devices. Such items found in a
consignment are set aside and returned to the client at the client's cost.
2. Definitions
Client: the company named on the signed VeilGrind service order.
Consignment: all material delivered under one service order number, which always begins with the
letters VG-.
Destruction run: a scheduled session in which a consignment is fed into the dedicated VeilGrind
shredder line in Hall 3.
Witness: a person nominated by the client to watch a destruction run on site.
Certificate of Destruction: the signed document confirming that a consignment has been
destroyed, with its weights and the date of the run.
3. Accepted materials and preparation
Consignments are grouped into three categories, which decide the fee:
Category A, rigid single-polymer items: PET, HDPE or PP bottles, jars, caps, preforms and
closures.
Category B, flexible film: printed LDPE or PP film, shrink sleeves, labels on reels and pouches made
of one polymer.
Category C, multilayer items: laminated pouches, sachets, metallised film and tubes made of
several layers.
Material must be delivered on pallets no heavier than 1.2 tonnes each, stretch-wrapped, with the service
order number written on every pallet. Mixed categories may arrive in one truck, but each pallet must hold
only one category. Containers must be empty. If more than 2 % of the delivered weight is product

residue, such as liquid, cream or powder, the plant charges an emptying fee of 2.50 baht per kg on the
whole consignment.
4. Booking a destruction run
Destruction runs take place on Tuesdays and Thursdays, starting at 09:00 or 13:30. The VeilGrind line
does not run on other days, so that it never handles ordinary recycling feedstock. To book a run, the
client should follow these steps:
1. Send the signed service order to the VeilGrind booking desk (telephone 074 291 637), stating the
estimated weight per category and the preferred run.
2. Book at least 5 working days before the run. The booking desk confirms the run and the delivery
window by e-mail within one working day.
3. Deliver the consignment between 08:00 and 15:00 on a working day, no earlier than 3 working days
before the booked run.
4. Register witnesses as described in section 5.
For product recalls, the client may request a Priority run. A Priority run can be held 2 working days after
booking, including on a Saturday morning, and carries a surcharge of 35 % on the destruction fee.
Priority runs are limited to 2 per calendar month for the whole plant and are allocated in order of booking.
5. Witnessing
A client may send up to two witnesses to each destruction run. Witness names and national ID or
passport numbers must reach the booking desk at least 2 working days before the run. On the day,
witnesses report to the security gatehouse at Gate 1 at least 30 minutes before the run starts, complete a
20-minute safety induction and wear the ear protection and high-visibility vest provided. Closed-toe
shoes are required; visitors in sandals are not admitted to Hall 3.
Witnesses watch from the viewing gallery above the shredder. They may photograph the shredder
hopper and the regrind output bin, but photographs of other plant areas, machinery settings or other
clients' material are not allowed.
Note. If no witness can attend, the client may order a video record of the run instead. The plant films
the feeding of every pallet from the gallery camera and keeps the video for 90 days. The video record
costs 1,500 baht per destruction run and must be requested at the time of booking.
6. Fees
Destruction fees are charged on the weight recorded at the plant weighbridge when the truck enters,
minus the pallets. The weighbridge weight is final. From 1 November 2026 the fees are:
Category A: 3.40 baht per kg (until 31 October 2026 the rate was 3.10 baht per kg).
Category B: 4.10 baht per kg.
Category C: 6.80 baht per kg.
A minimum charge of 4,000 baht applies to every consignment, whatever its weight. For clean Category
A material, the plant deducts a regrind credit of 0.90 baht per kg from the fee, because this regrind can

be sold to pipe and strapping makers. No regrind credit is given for Category B or C material. Invoices
are issued after the Certificate of Destruction and are payable within 30 days. VAT is added to all fees.
7. Chain of custody and security
The client must send each consignment in a closed truck or container sealed with a numbered seal, and
give the seal number to the booking desk before the truck leaves. On arrival the gatehouse guard checks
the seal against the booking. The Site Security Supervisor, Prasert Chaowalit, is responsible for the gate
check, the locked storage and the gallery camera.
If the seal is missing, broken or carries a different number, the consignment is not unloaded into the
normal storage area. It goes to the locked quarantine cage in Bay 7, the client is informed by telephone
within 2 hours, and the material is destroyed only after the client confirms in writing that it accepts the
consignment. In that case the material is destroyed at the next free run, not at the run originally booked.
Accepted consignments are kept in the locked VeilGrind store in Hall 3 until their run. No consignment is
stored for more than 10 calendar days. If the client postpones a run beyond that limit, a storage fee of
200 baht per pallet per day is charged from the eleventh day.
8. Certificate of Destruction
The Certificate of Destruction is issued within 3 working days after the destruction run. It is signed by the
Destruction Service Manager, Natthaya Sirikhet, and states the service order number, the seal number,
the weight received per category, the weight of regrind produced and the date and time of the run. The
certificate is sent as a signed PDF, and a paper original is posted on request.
Errors in a certificate are corrected free of charge if the client reports them within 30 days of issue. A
replacement copy requested for any other reason costs 300 baht.
9. Cancellation and liability
Cancellation more than 3 working days before the run: free of charge.
Cancellation 1 to 3 working days before the run: 25 % of the estimated destruction fee.
Cancellation on the day of the run, or no delivery: 50 % of the estimated destruction fee.
The plant's liability for any consignment is limited to the destruction fee paid for it. The plant is not liable
for delays caused by a broken seal, missing documents or excluded items found in the load.
10. Contact
Questions about these terms should be sent to Natthaya Sirikhet, Destruction Service Manager, Thung
Lung Polymer Reclaim Co., Ltd., telephone 074 291 630, Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 16:30.

Bringing Animal Performers onto a Rim Bueng
Stage: Step-by-Step Guide for Productions
Rim Bueng Studios Co., Ltd., Salaya, Nakhon Pathom · Studio Operations Guide SOG-14, version 2.1 · Issued
15 September 2026
1. Purpose and scope
This guide explains what a production must do, step by step, when it wants to film live animals at Rim
Bueng Studios. It applies to every production renting Stages 1 to 6, the Green Room annex and the
outdoor backlot known as Lotus Street. "Animal performer" means any live vertebrate brought onto
studio grounds for filming, whether it appears on camera or is kept as a stand-in.
Insects and aquarium fish kept in sealed tanks of less than 60 litres are not covered by the full procedure.
For these, the production only needs to notify the Animal Welfare Coordinator by email from the
StudioDesk portal at least 2 working days before the shoot.
Version 2.1 replaces version 2.0 of March 2025. The main changes are a longer notice period for requests
(Step 1), a lower temperature limit on enclosed stages (Step 3) and a new rule on night work (Step 4).
2. Step 1: Submit the Animal Performer Request (AP-1)
The production manager submits form AP-1 through the StudioDesk portal at least 10 working days
before the first shoot day that involves animals. Until 31 August 2026 the notice period was 7 working
days. The form must list:
the species, number, age and sex of every animal, including stand-ins;
the name of the licensed animal agency and of each handler;
the scenes, stages and planned hours for each animal on each day;
any special effects planned near the animals, such as rain, haze, wind machines or blank-firing
weapons.
Duangporn Thammachat, the studio's Animal Welfare Coordinator, reviews each AP-1 and replies within
3 working days with an approval, a request for changes or a refusal. On approval, the production pays an
animal-use deposit of 10,000 baht per production, whatever the number of animals.
Late requests. A request received less than 10 working days ahead can be reviewed on an
expedited basis for a fee of 4,500 baht, but only if at least 5 working days remain before the first
animal shoot day. Requests received with fewer than 5 working days to go are refused and the
scenes must be rescheduled.
3. Step 2: Arrange handlers and veterinary checks
Every animal must arrive with a handler from a licensed agency, and the handler stays with the animal for
the whole time it is on studio grounds. The minimum staffing levels are:
dogs, cats and rabbits: one handler for every 2 animals;

horses, cattle and other large animals: one handler for each animal;
birds: one handler for every 6 birds, and birds may only fly free on Stage 5, which has a closed net
ceiling;
Each animal needs a health certificate signed by a veterinarian no more than 7 days before its first day at
the studio. In addition, the studio's contract veterinarian, Dr. Pakorn Inthawong, examines the animals on
arrival every shoot day in the Animal Holding Bay (Building C, Room C-04). The on-arrival check costs
1,500 baht per shoot day for up to five animals, plus 200 baht for each animal beyond the fifth. The fee is
invoiced to the production with the stage rental.
4. Step 3: Prepare the stage and the Holding Bay
Book the Animal Holding Bay at the same time as the AP-1. The bay has six kennels and two stalls for
large animals. Animals must rest there, not in vehicles or on the stage floor.
On enclosed stages the air temperature at floor level must stay at or below 30 °C while animals are
present (the limit was 32 °C under version 2.0). The stage electrician checks the reading every hour and
records it on the stage log. On the Lotus Street backlot, all animal work stops when the shade
temperature reaches 34 °C, and from 1 April to 31 May no animal may work outdoors between 12:00 and
15:00.
Lay non-slip rubber mats on any polished or painted floor where animals walk.
Tape down or cover all cables along animal walking routes.
Switch off haze and smoke machines whenever an animal is on the stage.
Move animals to the Holding Bay before any pyrotechnics are fired within 50 metres of them.
Keep animals at least 30 metres from blank-firing weapons, and only with ear protection fitted by the
handler.
Post the red-and-white "Animal on Set" signs, collected from the stage office, on every stage door.
5. Step 4: Plan working hours and rest breaks
Time on set counts from when the animal leaves the Holding Bay until it returns. The daily limits are:
Dogs and cats: up to 4 hours on set per day, with no more than 45 minutes in a row under lights,
followed by at least 15 minutes of rest in the Holding Bay.
Horses and cattle: up to 6 hours on set per day, with no more than 1 hour in a row, followed by at
least 20 minutes of rest.
Birds and rabbits: up to 3 hours on set per day, with no more than 30 minutes in a row.
Animals younger than 6 months, such as puppies and kittens, may work no more than 2 hours per day in
total, whatever their species, and the veterinarian must be present on the stage for the whole time they
are working.
No animal may work after 22:00. As an exception, night work up to 23:30 may be approved in the AP-1
for dogs and horses only, and on no more than two nights in any production week (Monday to Sunday). A
third late night in the same week is not allowed, even if the scenes were approved in the AP-1.

6. Step 5: Run the shoot day
Mark every scene with animals on the call sheet with the letters "AP" and the name of the handler. The
handler briefs the director, the first assistant director and the camera team at least 30 minutes before the
first animal shot. Before each take the first assistant director announces "animal on set", and from that
moment no more than 12 crew members may stand within 5 metres of the animal.
The studio sends an independent Animal Safety Monitor to every shoot day with animals. The Monitor
keeps the time log for each animal and has the authority to stop any take, or the whole animal shoot, if
an animal shows signs of stress or a rule in this guide is broken. The decision of the Monitor cannot be
overruled by the director or the producer. The Monitor costs 3,200 baht per 10-hour day, and each extra
hour is charged at 400 baht.
Note. Only the handler may give food rewards. Crew members must not feed, touch or call the
animals.
7. Step 6: If an animal is hurt or distressed
1. Stop the take at once. The handler removes the animal from the set to the Holding Bay.
2. Call the Holding Bay on extension 2404. Outside office hours the security desk on extension 2000
contacts Dr. Pakorn Inthawong, who is on call during all animal shoot days.
3. The production manager files form AP-4 (Animal Incident Report) with the Animal Welfare Coordinator
within 24 hours, with the Monitor's time log attached.
4. An animal with any injury may not return to set until the veterinarian clears it in writing. The studio
informs the animal agency the same day.
8. Step 7: Wrap and close the request
Animals must leave the stage within 30 minutes of the last animal shot of the day. Studio staff clean and
disinfect the Holding Bay after each shoot day, for a cleaning fee of 900 baht per day. The production
returns the "Animal on Set" signs to the stage office before the stage is handed back.
Within 3 working days of the last animal shoot day, the production manager submits form AP-5 (Animal
Wrap Report), listing the actual hours worked by each animal. The 10,000-baht deposit is refunded within
14 days after the AP-5 is accepted, minus any cleaning, damage or late-wrap charges.
9. Arrivals and contacts
Vehicles carrying animals must enter through Gate 2 on the Phutthamonthon Sai 4 side, between 06:00
and 20:00 only, and park in the shaded bays next to Building C. Gate 1 is for crew and equipment trucks
and may not be used for animal transport.
Animal Welfare Coordinator: Duangporn Thammachat, extension 2410, Building A, Room A-112.
Contract Studio Veterinarian: Dr. Pakorn Inthawong, through the Holding Bay, extension 2404.
Stage office (signs, temperature logs, mats): extension 2300.

Incident Report: Black-and-White Pages Billed at
Colour Rate after the PageLedger Update
Lanmai Workhouse Co., Ltd. · Sawan Withi Road building, Nakhon Sawan · Ref. OPS-IR-2026-07 · Issued 28
September 2026
1. Summary
From 8 to 19 September 2026, PageLedger, the print credit system used at Lanmai Workhouse, billed
many black-and-white pages at the colour rate. The fault affected only jobs sent to the second-floor print
queue, LW-Print-2F. The third-floor queue, LW-Print-3F, runs on a separate print server that was not
updated and charged correctly throughout.
The current print prices, in force since 1 September 2026, are 1.50 baht per black-and-white A4 page
and 6 baht per colour A4 page. Until 31 August 2026 the black-and-white price was 1 baht per page. On
each wrongly billed page a member therefore paid 4.50 baht more than they should have. In total, 214
member accounts and 23 day-pass guests were overcharged, for a combined amount of 41,380 baht.
2. Timeline
7 September 2026, 23:10: the software vendor installs PageLedger version 4.2.0 on the second-floor
print server during a remote maintenance window.
8 September, 08:42: the first black-and-white job on LW-Print-2F is billed at the colour rate.
15 September, 16:05: a Fixed Desk member reports at the front desk that a 40-page report cost 240
baht instead of 60 baht. The front desk logs the complaint as ticket FD-3381.
16 September: the Member Accounts team compares billing records with printer page counters and
confirms that the fault is systematic, not a one-off.
17 September, 10:00: LW-Print-2F is switched to "hold and release at the printer" mode, and staff
warn members by notice board and the members' chat group to print on the third floor where
possible.
19 September, 14:30: the vendor rolls PageLedger on the second-floor server back to version 4.1.3.
Test prints confirm correct billing.
20 September, 09:00: LW-Print-2F reopens for normal use.
3. Cause
Version 4.2.0 changed the default setting for colour detection. Before the update, PageLedger looked at
the content of each page and charged colour only when a page actually contained colour. After the
update, the queue fell back to "bill by driver setting". Most laptops send jobs with the driver set to
"colour" by default, even when the document is black and white, so these pages were charged at 6 baht.
Jobs printed from the touch screen on the printer itself, such as copies and scans to print, were not
affected.
Note. No member data was exposed in this incident, and no print jobs were lost. The fault affected
billing only.

4. Refunds and credits
Every overcharge will be returned in full. Members do not need to do anything unless they want a cash
refund or are a day-pass guest.
Flex Desk and Fixed Desk members: the overcharged amount is added back to the member's
PageLedger balance automatically by 3 October 2026. The credit appears in the app as "Adjustment
OPS-IR-2026-07".
Private Office accounts: the amount is shown as a credit note on the October 2026 invoice, issued on
1 November 2026.
Members whose membership ended before 30 September 2026: the amount is refunded by bank
transfer to the account on file, without a claim, by 15 October 2026.
Day-pass guests: these guests paid by card at the kiosk and have no PageLedger account. They can
claim at the front desk or by email to the Member Accounts team until 31 October 2026, with the
kiosk receipt or the card statement line.
Members who would rather receive cash than print credit can ask for a cash refund at the front desk until
31 October 2026. A cash refund is only possible when the overcharge on the account is more than 200
baht; smaller amounts are returned as print credit only. Cash refunds are paid by bank transfer within 10
working days of the request.
Note. Monthly print credits included in membership plans expire at the end of each month. Credits
returned under this report are different: they do not expire and stay on the balance until used.
5. Responsibilities
Narongrit Phanwet, Operations Manager, owns this report and the follow-up actions. From now on,
every PageLedger or print server update must be approved by him in writing before it is installed.
Thitima Rakdee, Member Accounts Lead, calculates each account's overcharge, issues the credits
and credit notes, and decides on cash refund requests and day-pass claims.
The front desk team logs every billing complaint as a ticket on the same day and passes it to
Member Accounts within one working day.
The Facilities Coordinator runs a test of 10 black-and-white and 5 colour pages on each queue after
every update and records the result before the queue is opened to members.
6. Changes to prevent a repeat
Updates to PageLedger will only be installed on Sunday nights, and never during the last three working
days of a month, when monthly invoices are prepared. The vendor must send release notes at least five
working days before any update. Member Accounts will also compare PageLedger charges with printer
page counters every Monday, instead of once a month as before.
Questions about this report can be sent to the Member Accounts team at the front desk on the ground
floor, open Monday to Saturday from 08:30 to 18:00.
